items.title: Every delivery's quality record tells the reader the Endocrine regulator has an integral term; that file's own docstring says it has none
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R6.0), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §17.2 names Endocrine (signal bus / shared context + MJM) as one of the seven biomimetic layers, and §8 W512 recorded the measured finding that `geospheric/regulator.py` "is **not a controller**: its `integral_error` is declared and never accumulated, its `dt` is discarded, its corrective actions are strings", with `vbs/quality.py` named as the one surface built to tell the truth about these layers (registered FU-307, Tier 1). OBSERVED: FU-307's correction reached the regulator's docstring (W515) and a comment at `agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:514` ("NOT a PID regulator"), but NOT the string that actually ships. `LAYER_STATE["Endocrine"]["basis"]` at quality.py:59-63 still claims an integral term, and `assure_delivery` publishes `biomimetic.layer_basis` on every quality record — reached from `api/deliverables.py`, `api/genesis.py`, `api/products.py`, `api/resource_fabric.py`, `api/swarm.py` and `api/management_systems.py`. This is the "fix every writer, not one" class, with the surviving writer being the reached one. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST http://127.0.0.1:8031/api/v1/deliverables/produce (HTTP 200) returned, at `quality_assurance.biomimetic.layer_basis.Endocrine` and again at `versions[0].quality_assurance.biomimetic.layer_basis.Endocrine`: "agentic_core/biomimicry/geospheric/regulator.py holds a real HomeostaticRegulator with an integral term and NOTHING IMPORTS IT; a second copy of the same class sits in geospheric/homeostatic_regulator.py." Contradicted by C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/biomimicry/geospheric/regulator.py:12-18 ("NOT PID CONTROL, and this docstring used to say it was (FU-307, W515). Measured on this file: `integral_error` is assigned once below as a dict of zeros and never accumulated, so there is no integral term; `dt` is computed in regulate() and never read, so there is no derivative term") and by C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:514 in the same file as the false string. Writer: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:59-63; publisher: quality.py:556 (`biomimetic["layer_basis"]`). WHY TIER 1: A reader of any produced deliverable is shown the sentence "agentic_core/biomimicry/geospheric/regulator.py holds a real HomeostaticRegulator with an integral term", and the layers_note immediately above it says "`layer_basis` names the module behind each claim" — directing the reader to trust it. The file itself records the opposite: "`integral_error` is assigned once below as a dict of zeros and never accumulated, so there is no integral term". This is not an omission and not an environment effect: it is a positive assertion about a named module's mechanism that the module contradicts, on a surface a person reaches. It is above tier 2 because nothing on the surface qualifies it — the adjacent `layer_states` value `code_exists_unreached` says the layer does not RUN, which a reader reads as real code one wiring away, exactly the impression the false clause reinforces. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the surrounding fields (`layer_states: code_exists_unreached`, `layers_note`) qualify REACHABILITY, not the mechanism claim, and the note explicitly points the reader at `layer_basis` as the authority. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: NOT REFUTED, tier UNCHANGED at 1. I reproduced the exact false clause on a reached surface and confirmed it is false of both copies of the named class. Tier 1 rather than 2: this is not an omission or an environment effect but a positive assertion about a named module's mechanism, and the sentence directly above it tells the reader layer_basis is the authority for each claim; the adjacent `code_exists_unreached` qualifies REACHABILITY ("real code one wiring away"), which reinforces rather than corrects the mechanism claim. Not tier 0/3 because nothing on the surface walks it back — the same file's own comment at quality.py:514 says "NOT a PID regulator", so the module contradicts itself and only the reached half lies. VERDICT CORRECTED DOC_OVERCLAIM -> PARTIAL: the rubric's DOC_OVERCLAIM is for the vision or a canon doc claiming more than the system; here the vision's §8 W512 record is CORRECT and the overclaim lives in shipped runtime code published on every quality record. The capability (per-layer state reporting, six honest states, an accurate `layer_states` map) genuinely works and one of its seven basis strings asserts an untruth — PARTIAL with the shortfall UNDISCLOSED. If the register prefers to treat the shipped LAYER_STATE table as canon-in-code, DOC_OVERCLAIM is defensible; the tier is 1 either way. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: Reproduced by execution: POST http://127.0.0.1:8031/api/v1/deliverables/produce (HTTP 200) returns at quality_assurance.biomimetic.layer_basis.Endocrine the string "agentic_core/biomimicry/geospheric/regulator.py holds a real HomeostaticRegulator with an integral term and NOTHING IMPORTS IT; a second copy of the same class sits in geospheric/homeostatic_regulator.py", immediately after layers_note ends with "`layer_basis` names the module behind each claim." Writer: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:59-63; publisher quality.py:556-557. Contradicted on the named file: `grep -n integral agentic_core/biomimicry/geospheric/regulator.py` returns ONLY the docstring denial (lines 13-14, 38) and `self.integral_error = {k: 0.0 for k in self.setpoints}` at line 26 — there is no `+=` and no accumulation anywhere in the file. The duplicate at geospheric/homeostatic_regulator.py has no integral field at all, so the clause is false of both copies. The other two clauses ARE true: `grep -rn HomeostaticRegulator` (excluding _archive) finds only the two class definitions and quality.py's own strings — nothing imports it, and the second copy exists. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): In agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:60, replace "holds a real HomeostaticRegulator with an integral term" with what the file records — a proportional threshold comparison that names a corrective action as a string, with no integral and no derivative term — and add a guard asserting that no LAYER_STATE basis string claims a term the named module does not compute.

items.title: The CFO cash-flow statement reports net cash movement that is structurally always zero, and cannot see the only account whose balance actually moves
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R6.1), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §12 (W446): "double-entry books with period close and CFO statements"; the close handler's own docstring claims "P&L · balance sheet · cash flow computed from the REAL double-entry postings". OBSERVED: `statements()` derives cash flow only from postings that touch the `cash` account (`receipts = _sum(lambda p: p["debit"] == "cash")`, `payments = _sum(... p["credit"] == "cash")`). The cycle's compat postings route everything through `cash` in equal and opposite totals, and the inter-VSB transfer posts `Dr transfer_out / Cr reserve_fund` — never touching `cash`. Measured on the live books, the `cash` account balance is exactly 0.0 after two cycles, a close and a transfer. Before the close the card read receipts 20,000 / payments 20,000 / net 0, where 4,000 of those "payments" were an internal move into the entity's own reserve fund, not an outflow. The P&L and balance sheet are correct and balanced throughout; the cash-flow statement is the one of the three that carries no information. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/economy/transfer {from workstation-idbo, to vsb-a42ca383af, 500} → `sender_reserve_fund_after_wst: 3500.0`. Then GET /api/v1/economy/board-pack?vsb_id=workstation-idbo → `cash_flow: {"operating_receipts_wst": 0, "operating_payments_wst": 0, "net_cash_movement_wst": 0}` while `balance_sheet.assets.reserve_fund: 3500.0` (was 4000.0). Raw store C:/tmp/m1data2/data/economy/workstation-idbo_ledger.json: last posting `{debit: transfer_out, credit: reserve_fund, amount: 500.0, source: inter_vsb_transfer}`; `accounts.cash: 0.0`. Code: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/economy/ledger.py:635-650 (receipts/payments) and 315-324 (`_COMPAT_POSTING`, every pot paired against `cash`). UI: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/VSBEconomy.tsx:688-692 renders "Cash flow · this period" / `net_cash_movement_wst` with no basis line. WHY TIER 1: The VSB Economy page prints a card headed "Cash flow · this period" showing "0 WST net" in a period in which 500 WST demonstrably left the entity (reserve_fund 4,000 → 3,500, confirmed by the transfer response's own `sender_reserve_fund_after_wst: 3500.0`). That is a financial-statement figure asserting an outcome the books contradict, with no caveat anywhere on the card or in the payload — unlike `trial_balance`, which carries a `scope` string explaining exactly what it is and is not comparable with. It is tier 1 rather than tier 2 because the card is not merely incomplete: it states a number, 0, which is false for the period shown, and the number cannot be anything else — in a complete cycle, cash in (revenue) exactly equals cash out (reserves + five distributions + declared costs), so net movement is 0 by construction, and every movement that is not a cycle bypasses `cash` entirely. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — `trial_balance` carries a `scope` string and `balances` carries a `balances_note`; `cash_flow` carries neither, and the UI card adds none. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: NOT REFUTED, tier UNCHANGED at 1. The structural claim is stronger than the assessor stated and I verified it from the posting list: `cash` is a pure transit account (Dr total == Cr total == 20,000, balance 0.0), every cycle pairs each pot against it so net movement is 0 by construction, and every non-cycle movement (close, inter-VSB transfer) bypasses it entirely. Tier 1 rather than 2: the card headed "Cash flow · this period" asserts a FIGURE, 0 WST net, in a period where the entity's only liquid asset fell 4,000 -> 3,500 and the same payload's own P&L reports net -500 for that period — a financial-statement number that is false for the label it is given, not a blank field and not a missing capability. Not tier 2 because the defect is an assertion rather than an undisclosed partiality, and the sibling trial_balance proves the codebase knows how to caveat a figure of this kind and did not. VERDICT PARTIAL retained: the P&L, balance sheet, trial balance and close are genuinely correct and balanced throughout (see index 9), so the shortfall is one of the three statements, undisclosed at both the payload and the UI card. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: Reproduced: GET /api/v1/economy/board-pack?vsb_id=workstation-idbo returns statements.cash_flow = {operating_receipts_wst: 0, operating_payments_wst: 0, net_cash_movement_wst: 0} for period 1 (from_posting 20), in the SAME payload as profit_and_loss.net_profit_wst: -500.0 and balance_sheet.assets.reserve_fund: 3500.0. I dumped all 21 postings from C:/tmp/m1data2/data/economy/workstation-idbo_ledger.json: postings 0-13 are two cycles in which cash is debited 10,000 and credited 2,000+1,600+2,400+1,600+1,200+1,200 = 10,000 (total cash Dr 20,000 = total cash Cr 20,000); postings 14-19 (period_close) touch retained_earnings only; posting 20 is `transfer_out / reserve_fund 500.00 inter_vsb_transfer` and never touches cash. Stored `accounts.cash: 0.0`. Code: ledger.py:635-637 (receipts = Dr cash, payments = Cr cash), ledger.py:315-324 (_COMPAT_POSTING pairs every pot against cash). Caveat search: `grep -rn cash_flow` over agentic_core and apps (excluding _archive) returns exactly TWO hits — the writer at ledger.py:649 and the render at VSBEconomy.tsx:691 — so no basis, note or scope string exists anywhere, unlike trial_balance, which carries a `scope` sentence in the same payload. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Give `cash_flow` a `scope`/`basis` string the way `trial_balance` has one, stating that it sums movements through the `cash` account only and that inter-VSB transfers and reserve movements post against `reserve_fund` and are not visible here — or, better, derive the statement from the movement of every asset account so the figure means what its name says. Render that basis on the VSBEconomy card.

items.close_note: c - THE CASH-FLOW STATEMENT SAYS WHAT IT SUMS. `net_cash_movement_wst` is derived only from postings that touch the `cash` account, and the cycle's compat postings route everything through `cash` in equal and opposite totals - so the figure is ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION and a reader took that for "cash in matched cash out". items.title: A period close and the board pack are credited to a "CFO agent (AI C-Suite)" that does not exist on the path, and that attribution is sealed into the
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R6.2), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §12 (W446): "double-entry books with period close and CFO statements"; §17.5 invariant 3, append-only DCS audit, which makes whatever is written permanent. OBSERVED: `agentic_core/economy/ledger.py:652` stamps `prepared_by: "CFO agent (AI C-Suite)" — computed from the double-entry postings` onto the statements (the trailing clause partly qualifies it), and `agentic_core/api/economy.py:1638` writes the BARE string `"prepared_by": "CFO agent (AI C-Suite)"` into the tamper-evident UEG close event with no qualifier. A grep for `gateway` or `query_meta` across the whole 2,002-line economy module returns zero hits, so no C-Suite resource is consulted on any economy path. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/economy/close-period {vsb_id: workstation-idbo} → HTTP 200, `statements.prepared_by: "CFO agent (AI C-Suite) — computed from the double-entry postings"`. The sealed record in C:/tmp/m1data2/data/ueg.json, event_201: `{"type": "economy.period_close", "vsb_id": "workstation-idbo", "net_profit_wst": 4000.0, "retained_earnings_wst": 4000.0, "prepared_by": "CFO agent (AI C-Suite)", "disclaimer": "Virtual/simulated WST — no real funds moved."}` with `previous_hash`/`hash` chained. Code: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/api/economy.py:1638; C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/economy/ledger.py:652. Measured absence: `grep -n "gateway\|query_meta" agentic_core/api/economy.py` → no output. WHY TIER 1: The reader of the close response and of the board pack is shown `prepared_by: "CFO agent (AI C-Suite)"`, and the hash-chained UEG record stores the bare form with no qualifier at all. No agent prepared these statements: there is not a single model call anywhere in `agentic_core/api/economy.py`, and `close_period()` is arithmetic over stored postings. This is not the AI_DISABLE_LOCAL environment speaking — it is a field asserting an actor, and no actor acted; the platform would make the same claim with models fully enabled, because nothing on this path ever calls one. It is above tier 2 because it is an assertion about who produced a financial statement, not a missing capability, and above tier 3 because nothing on the surface says the attribution is nominal. The audit chain is append-only, so the fabricated attribution cannot be corrected, only superseded. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly — the statements payload appends "computed from the double-entry postings", which a careful reader can take as the real method. The UEG record and the economy.py writer carry no qualifier at all. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: NOT REFUTED, tier UNCHANGED at 1. Tier 1 rather than 2: the field names an ACTOR for a financial statement and no actor acted — `close_period()` is arithmetic over stored postings and the module contains no model call on any line, so the platform would make the identical claim with models fully enabled. That removes the AI_DISABLE_LOCAL defence entirely: this is not "no model ran" as environment, it is an assertion of authorship the code can never satisfy. Not tier 3 because nothing on the UEG record qualifies it, and the append-only chain makes the fabricated attribution permanent and only supersedable. The statements-payload trailing clause "computed from the double-entry postings" is a partial mitigation on ONE of the two writers and does not reach the sealed one. VERDICT PARTIAL retained: the close itself is real and correct (verified at index 9); the attribution is the shortfall. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: Reproduced from the sealed record rather than by re-closing: C:/tmp/m1data2/data/ueg.json node event_201 = {"type": "economy.period_close", "vsb_id": "workstation-idbo", "net_profit_wst": 4000.0, "retained_earnings_wst": 4000.0, "prepared_by": "CFO agent (AI C-Suite)", "disclaimer": "Virtual/simulated WST - no real funds moved."} with previous_hash and hash chained, and GET /api/v1/gaas/ueg/verify returns valid: true over 441 events with anchor_state present — so the bare attribution is inside a verified, append-only chain. Live GET /api/v1/economy/board-pack returns statements.prepared_by: "CFO agent (AI C-Suite) - computed from the double-entry postings". Writers: agentic_core/api/economy.py:1638 (bare) and agentic_core/economy/ledger.py:652 (qualified) — `grep -rn prepared_by` over agentic_core and apps returns ONLY those two, so no UI reads it and no third writer qualifies it. Measured absence of any actor: `grep -n "gateway|query_meta|served_by|invoke_native" agentic_core/api/economy.py` returns ONE hit, line 1355, which reads provenance off a stored run for an unrelated route — the close path makes no model call at all. For contrast I confirmed the CCA path DOES call `gateway.query_meta` (change_control.py:1351) and labels its fallback honestly, which is what this path does not do. items.title: The pre-flight's [regchange] leg names a HARDCODED four guards; W592's register change broke seven, none of them on that list
items.why: MEASURED IN W592, on the instrument W588 added for exactly this class. The [regchange] leg of scripts/selfcheck_diff.py exists because [planpins] screens only the lines a round ADDS and therefore cannot see an assertion invalidated by the REGISTER moving. It fired correctly on every pre-flight of W592 and named the four kinds of register change the round made. But the selector it prints is a HARDCODED list of four guard names - plan_carries_every_followup, plan_projects, an_area_with_no_owner, route_whose_matcher - and W592's register and plan changes broke SEVEN assertions, of which that list named exactly ZERO: two legs of test_w469 asserting route_row's high-severity fallback (one at the function, one through the CLI), test_w535's clause (c) asserting the same fallback as the Owner's 2026-10-02 ruling had kept it, a leg reslotting FU-003 (a row that existed only because three adds used to succeed), a leg asserting "2 follow-ups ride it", two legs of test_w512 requiring prospection to carry a branch, and test_w486's assertion that excluding a one-time intake cannot lower the closed-per-round rate. Three of those went red because the plan IMPROVED - the last owner-gated rows closed and every open P2 item became sized - which is the guard-must-not-fail-on-success class. Not one was a defect in production code, and each surfaced only after the previous was fixed, so the round paid for seven serial suite runs to discover a set the pre-flight could have named in one. A hardcoded list of at-risk guards is a SPELLING: it names the guards somebody thought of when the leg was written, and says nothing about the next assertion somebody pins to plan state. The leg should DERIVE the set - the guards that read docs/FOLLOWUPS.json, docs/FABLE_DELIVERY_PROMPT.md, plan_items, raw_items, route_row, forecast or the prospection faculty are discoverable by reading the test file, and the ones that touch the kinds of change the round actually made are a subset of those. The property to aim at: after a register or plan change, the pre-flight names every guard that reads the changed artefact, so the round runs them once rather than discovering them one suite at a time. Until then the leg's own limit should be printed where it is read - that its list is illustrative and not a census - because a leg that prints four names invites a reader to believe four is the number.

items.title: OWNER: whether the scholar-review gate should also cover the five Religion RESEARCH tools, not only the learner curriculum
items.why: A.12.3 requires a named scholar to approve AI-composed religious content BEFORE A LEARNER SEES IT, and names what it blocks: QEP features 5/6/7, all of A.7, P3.10 and the guidance surfaces. W594 built the gate and wired it to the LEARNER/CURRICULUM path - POST /api/v1/qep/tajweed/lesson, a lesson plan a learner studies from. IT DID NOT wire it to the five Religion RESEARCH tools (/fatwa-research, /hadith-study, /quran-tafsir, /halal-review, /interfaith). THE REASONING, which is the author's and not the Owner's: those five already withhold on the deterministic floor, already carry 'AI-assisted scholarly research only - NOT a fatwa and NOT a substitute for authenticated sources', and already refer the reader to a qualified Islamic scholar or mufti. A tool that says 'this is not a ruling, take it to a scholar' is a different act from teaching a learner a curriculum. THE COST OF THE STRICTER READING, measured: with an empty roster the gate withholds everything, so wiring those five would stop all five returning any content until a scholar is engaged. That is a real product consequence and deserves to be asked rather than assumed. IT IS CHEAP EITHER WAY: the gate exists and those routes already have a withholding path, so the stricter reading is a few lines per route. RECOMMENDATION: leave the research tools as they are, and revisit if a user is observed treating a research answer as a ruling.

items.title: The archive's four knowledge-index candidates, assessed: only text_indexer is real and it indexes FILES not passages
items.why: The Owner asked whether earlier work on these features was already done and sitting in the archive. It was read, and the answer is mostly no. _archive/agentic_core/analysis/text_indexer.py is the one REAL artefact: a working lexical indexer, and its shape is reusable. But it indexes WHOLE FILES, recording no line, offset or passage location, so a citation built on it could name a document and never a place inside it - which is precisely the property P3.22 needs and the property the verifier built in W596 checks. Recover the shape, add locations. _archive/agentic_core/ai/rag_pipeline.py is NOT reusable: it returns a composed sentence claiming it found three relevant papers, with a literal SIM marker in the output. _archive/agentic_core/reactor/religion/qep_logic.py must NOT be recovered at all: it produces recitation scores from random.random with error positions from random.randint, which is both a fabrication and one of the six boundaries section 11 forbids, and it is the ancestor of the defect W403 deleted. It is unreachable today and should stay that way. STANDING HAZARD restated: the archived law corpus is SIMULATED - recover the SHAPE, never the corpus.

The row's finding was that the archive's one REAL candidate, text_indexer.py, indexes FILES with no line or passage location, so a citation built on it could name a document and never a place inside it. P3.22 added exactly that: _passages() splits a document into located passages numbered from 1 with BLANK LINES COUNTED, so line 42 in the index is line 42 in the file - getting that wrong would produce precise-looking citations to text the document does not contain, which is worse than no citation. search() was EXTENDED rather than replaced (the prepared patch would have defined a second function in a module that already had one, and Python keeps the last) and now returns located passages beside the file hits, with a passage whose line does not resolve reported under not_citable rather than returned without one. Its silent [:limit] now reports the cap. The row's other three candidates stand as recorded and were NOT recovered: rag_pipeline.py returns a sentence claiming it found three papers with a literal SIM marker, qep_logic.py scores recitations from random.random which is both a fabrication and a section-11 forbidden boundary, and the apoptosis stub is about components not entities. The standing hazard is unchanged and now has a mechanism behind it: recover the SHAPE, never the corpus, and a claim that cannot cite a resolvable location cannot be asserted.

items.title: agentic_core/simulation fabricates a civilisational forecast and imports a class that is not there
items.why: Measured while preparing P3.24, which was going to add a module to agentic_core/simulation/ on the belief that the package was empty. It is not, and it holds three things. ONE: RealitySimulationEngine.simulate_future computes health_projection as empathy times one-minus-scarcity times 1.5 over caller defaults of 0.5, then returns prosperity_projection of plus 24 percent or minus 12 percent chosen by a threshold on empathy, and a stability_index that is either 0.94 or 0.42. Every one of those figures is invented, and a projected percentage selected by an if-statement is the precise shape P3.24's own clause forbids - no surface may carry a predicted outcome. items.title: A dict-shaped HTTPException detail reaches React as a child at four sites, where it throws
items.why: Found by refuting this round's NEXT item before building it. A route may raise HTTPException with a dict detail - seven already do - and axios hands that object to the page unchanged. Four sites do setError(e.response.data.detail or a fallback) and then render the state value directly as a React child, and an object as a React child THROWS: the surface crashes rather than showing a poor message. The four are DomainTool.tsx lines 159 and 196, LawHub.tsx line 30, and VSBSpawnStudio.tsx line 494. I FIRST RECORDED THIS AS 22 SITES AND THAT WAS WRONG BY MORE THAN FIVE TIMES, which is worth writing down because it is the second count I inflated the same way in one night: the 22 occurrences of that expression split by SHAPE, and only the four above put the object into React state. About fifteen interpolate it into a template string, which stringifies to the object-Object text - ugly and useless to a reader, but not a crash - and three destructure it and guard with a typeof check, so they are already correct and VSBCockpit even unpacks the 422 validation array. A grep gives sites, not instances; the defect is what the site DOES with the value. NOTHING CRASHES TODAY: I checked each of the seven dict-detail routes against each of the ten files and none pair up. But the gated-curriculum refusal planned for P3.10 lands on a DomainTool endpoint and would be the first, so the class has to be closed with it rather than after it. items.title: The combining check refuses all-or-nothing, and the one file every guard shares cannot cause the collision it names
items.why: The Owner asked for MORE ROWS CLOSED PER ROUND. followups.py bundles is the mechanism that answers that, and its COMBINING line currently refuses every time, for two reasons that are both mechanical rather than substantive. ONE, IT IS ALL-OR-NOTHING ACROSS THE TOP N. combinable() walks every pair among the top six bundles and returns REFUSED if ANY pair shares a file, so one overlapping pair refuses all fifteen pairs. It never reports WHICH subset is disjoint, which is the actual decision a round needs - two bundles that genuinely do not overlap are never offered, and the output reads as though no combination were possible at all. TWO, THE SHARED FILE IS SHARED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY CONNECTION. Every guard in this project lives in integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py, so any row about a guard cites it, and the observed refusal was precisely that P2.17 and P3.2 both touch that file. But the risk the rule NAMES is that each bundle's blinds mutate the other's surface - and the test file is not a blind surface: every blind driver in scratchpad mutates SOURCE files and the plan, runs the guard, and restores bytes. So the one file guaranteed to appear in many rows cannot cause the collision the refusal cites. THE RULE ITSELF IS RIGHT and must not be weakened: two guard subjects sharing a SOURCE file would make a RED unattributable, which is exactly why blinds are driven one at a time. What is wrong is the file set it computes over and the all-or-nothing verdict. REMEDY: exclude the shared guard file from the disjointness computation (or compute disjointness over BLIND SURFACES rather than over all cited files), and report the largest disjoint SUBSET with its basis instead of a single refusal. The function's own docstring says a rule nobody can execute is indistinguishable from a rule nobody holds; a rule that always refuses is equally uninformative. A guard must assert a DISJOINT pair is reported as combinable, or the fix is unobservable.

items.close_note: combinable() now computes disjointness over BLIND SURFACES: the shared suite file is excluded, because every blind mutates source files and restores them and nothing blinds the suite, and the exclusion is reported in excluded_from_disjointness so a reader can see why two rows citing the same file were called disjoint. It reports the largest pairwise-disjoint subset (a maximum independent set, brute-forced over the six proposed bundles) with the excluded bundles named, on every path in one key set. Bundles are labelled by slot AND rows, because one item is cut into several components. The rule is not weakened: a shared SOURCE file still refuses the pair, and a blind removing that refusal goes red. Four blinds red.

items.title: OWNER: charter an INSTRUMENT item to own P2.17's eleven rows, so P2.17 can close on its own bar
items.why: P2.17 IS ONE TEST FROM CLOSING, measured W598. Its ACCEPT has three parts: (a) the bundle as a file-connected component was DELIVERED W568 with three of its four limits already met; (c) the round-cost figures computed rather than typed was DELIVERED W565; and (b) has three requirements of which two are done - the parallel suite proven to give the same pass/fail set as the serial one on one tree (W540, with figures) and the blind harness's runtime measured before and after (W569, which refuted its own row's premise: sharding gave 1.60x at two shards and got WORSE at four, because contention and not the single tree was the limit). THE ONLY MISSING REQUIREMENT is the per-worker store proven isolated by a test that would FAIL if two workers shared it, and nothing asserts that today. That test is small and is designed. BUT ELEVEN ROWS RIDE P2.17 AND NONE CLOSES WITH IT: FU-301 the parallel stall, FU-399 page guards as text scans, FU-413, FU-414, FU-415, FU-416 CI running serially, FU-418 M1's workflow not re-runnable, FU-439, FU-446, FU-455, FU-457. The register refuses to mark an item DONE while rows ride it - it refused exactly that for P3.21 this round - so they must be rehoused first. THE RECOMMENDATION: charter an INSTRUMENT item rather than scattering them into P2.20. Six of the eleven are one mechanism (the instruments that tell a round what it must check: a hardcoded guard list, a missing route warning, an all-or-nothing combining refusal, a data root moved under a test, no assertion that the register on disk matches its writer, and a forecast returning two key sets) and that six-row round is already prepared with its fix shapes located. A coherent area with prepared work is what an item is for. THE ALTERNATIVE, reslotting eleven instrument rows onto P2.20 whose subject is user context and request models, would make P2.20's own bar unreadable - which is the condition that kept P2.4 from ever closing. This is put to the Owner rather than decided because creating a plan item is their act; they approved the identical shape for P3.28 this round.

items.title: R13's entity split was measured wrong: all 112 of the 'auto-only' group have real economic history
items.why: THE OWNER APPROVED A BATCH DELETION OF 112 ENTITIES ON A BASIS I GAVE THEM, AND MEASURING BEFORE EXECUTING IT SHOWED THE BASIS IS FALSE. Nothing was deleted. The document said those 112 were referenced ONLY by an auto-seeded business plan, which every entity receives and which therefore says nothing about whether anything happened to the entity. Measured against live data: 112 of 112 carry NON-ZERO owner-payment history, typically 1200 to 1560 WST accrued across 10 to 13 entries memoed cycle owner share, with timestamps; 112 of 112 are keys in economy_owner_payments.json and 111 of 112 in economy_ventures_portfolio.json. Those are PLATFORM-LEVEL financial records, not an entity's own self-ledger, so deleting the entity records would leave payment entries pointing at nothing. WHY THE DOCUMENT GOT IT WRONG, which matters more than the number: its 'also on disk as' column was built by checking a FEW artefact kinds - a repo, a business plan - and never looked at the economy records at all. So that column never meant 'only a business plan'; it meant 'only a business plan among the kinds the script happened to check', and the column's name invited exactly the reading that was made of it. An absence in a coverage column must mean CHECKED AND NOT FOUND, or it is not evidence. AND THE EXISTING INSTRUMENT WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG: scripts/prune_test_entities.py run dry reports safe to remove 0 and KEPT referenced elsewhere 162, because its cross-reference set includes both economy records, which its own comment already calls genuine platform-level references. The document disagreed with the instrument and the document was wrong. This is the THIRD R13 figure of mine to need correcting and the most serious, because the other two were overstatements of risk while this one understated it - and it reached an Owner decision. REMEDY: a coverage column that NAMES the kinds it checked and covers every record kind; a separate statement for the economy records; a defensible rule for what makes a fixture removable when it HAS accrued virtual WST, the honest candidate being that its payment entries are removed WITH it and the removal recorded rather than the entity deleted and the entries orphaned; and the prune executed only through the script with its guard intact.

items.title: Per-worker test directories accumulate in the real data root and nothing removes them
items.why: Found while enumerating the data root to build R13's honest coverage measurement. The real data root holds 24 leftover per-worker directories - test_projects__gw0 through gw7, test_proposals__gw0 through gw7 and test_synthesis__gw0 through gw7 - with content in most of them. They are GITIGNORED, so nothing is committed and no CI or review surface is affected, which is why this is tier 3 and low. W507 already fixed one half of exactly this: data/_test_store__gw0..gw7 were being created on every run including runs with an explicit DATA_DIR, and the fix was to create the default store only when it is actually going to be used. The same reasoning was not applied to the other three roots, which conftest creates unconditionally inside the subdivision loop whenever a worker id is present - so every parallel run with an explicit root still makes eight directories per root and leaves them. WHY IT IS WORTH CLOSING even though nothing is wrong today: the directories make the data root harder to read, and reading the data root is exactly what an honest R13 coverage measurement has to do - the leftover directories are themselves candidates for a scan that is trying to find which records reference an entity. An instrument whose own debris pollutes the thing a later measurement must read is the cheap kind of defect to fix now and an annoying one to disentangle later. REMEDY: create a subdivided root only when it will be written, as W507 did for the store, or remove it on session teardown when it is empty; and assert in the per-worker isolation guard that a run leaves no empty subdivided directory behind. Do NOT simply delete the existing 24 as part of the fix - they are gitignored test output, but deleting a directory the Owner may have inspected is a separate act from stopping their creation.

MEASURED IN W601: conftest.py set PROJECTS_DIR, SYNTHESIS_OUTPUT_DIR and PROPOSALS_DIR by PLAIN ASSIGNMENT where every other path uses setdefault, so an explicit value was OVERWRITTEN - driven, with an explicit scratch path going in and data/test_projects coming out. The isolated-run recipe this project uses for every verification run has therefore never isolated those three, and the suite has been writing projects, synthesis output and proposals into the repository's own data/. The 24 __gw0..__gw7 directories are the SYMPTOM of that line, not a separate defect, and DATA_DIR was always honoured which is why the leak was invisible. Now setdefault, with both halves driven: an explicit value survives, and the default still applies when nothing is set so no plain pytest run changes. Two blinds red.

items.title: Twenty-two swallowed exceptions in the heartbeat: W589 fixed one beat step, twenty-one still fail silently
items.why: Counted by AST, not by eye: agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py holds TWENTY-TWO handlers whose entire body is a bare pass, and about fifteen of them sit immediately after an actions.append call - meaning they are BEAT STEPS whose failure is swallowed. The step raises, nothing is appended, and the beat reports a shorter actions list with no indication that anything went wrong. W589 FIXED EXACTLY ONE OF THEM and wrote the reason in place at line 340: a swallowed exception made a cadence that CANNOT RUN indistinguishable from a cadence with nothing due, because both appended no action. That sentence is true of the other twenty-one. The swallows sit under compliance_rescreen (line 472), operate_vsb_unclassified (432), operate_vsb_failed (410), alignment (571), twin_directive (589), evolution_cycle (650), evolve_vsb (697 and 699), reshipped_stale_repo (733, 738, 740), metabolic_throttle (612), transformation_tick (550), genome_scan (258), pulse (212) and the constitutional audit (750). THE CONSEQUENCE IS MEASURED, not hypothetical: FU-417 records a real flake where test_w585_p33 failed in the full suite and passed in isolation, and the ONLY reason it is now diagnosable is that W589 fixed the one swallow in its path. Any of the remaining twenty-one failing produces the same unattributable symptom with no record to read. THIS IS THE FIX-EVERY-WRITER CLASS at its plainest: a defect understood, a remedy written and applied at one site, and the comment explaining the remedy sitting six lines above twenty-one instances of the defect. REMEDY: the same shape W589 used - except Exception as err, record it into the beat's own record with the step named, and let the beat report that a step was ATTEMPTED AND FAILED rather than silently omitting it. Mechanical and uniform, which is why it belongs in one pass. A guard must assert the beat record names a failed step, driven by making one step raise.

But it added no surface for a SEARCH: the keys search() now returns - passages, passages_matched, not_citable, citation_basis, matched_files, shown_files, file_hits_basis - reach no page and no printed line. THE REASON THIS BELONGS TO P3.23 RATHER THAN BEING FIXED NOW: P3.23's ACCEPT requires that every factual particular in a generated artefact carries the document id and the LOCATION it came from, and that the unresolved checks are visible ON THE PAGE and not only in a log. items.title: _screen_candidate returns three different key sets, so a caller indexing its verdict gets undefined
items.why: The pre-flight's returns leg named two of the three: genesis.py line 76 omits compliance_covered, overall and safety_covered which a sibling return carries, and line 89 omits screen_error which another sibling carries. So _screen_candidate - the function that screens a journey candidate against section 11 - answers with a DIFFERENT SHAPE depending on which path it took: an exception path carrying screen_error and no coverage fields, and a normal path carrying coverage fields and no screen_error. A caller indexing either gets undefined on the other, and a caller testing truthiness cannot tell NOT SCREENED from SCREENED AND CLEAN from SCREENED AND FAILED - three facts collapsed into one falsy value, on the function that decides whether a candidate passes the section 11 screen. items.title: The regulator's meiosis fabricates a diversity score from the clock, and its mitosis clones dicts not entities
items.why: Measured while sizing P3.26's remaining clauses, because clause 6 says crossover ALREADY EXISTS and a round would reasonably look here first. What exists must not be built on. ONE: meiosis_recombine sets diversity_score to 0.35 plus 0.05 times time.time() modulo 1 - a figure derived PURELY FROM THE CLOCK, with both parents ignored entirely (the child is just the two dicts merged). Sampled across timestamps it returns 0.913, 1.263, 0.563, 0.4, 0.35: so a DIVERSITY score can exceed 1.0, which is arithmetically meaningless as well as fabricated, and it is logged to the UEG as regulator_meiosis diversity - a measurement nobody measured, entering the audit log. TWO: mitosis_scale returns dict clones carrying a clone_id and a timestamp. It inherits no constitution, transfers no funds and creates no entity, so it is not the mitosis clause 5 describes - a mature entity creating a subsidiary that inherits its parent's constitution VERBATIM, funded from the parent's own section 4 share so funds are conserved, through Change Control. THREE: NEITHER IS CALLED ANYWHERE in the live tree, which is the only reason the fabricated score reaches no reader today. WHY THIS IS REGISTERED RATHER THAN FIXED NOW: it is P3.26's own clauses 5 and 6, so the fix IS that item's work, and the row exists to stop a later round treating these functions as a foundation. THE REMEDY WHEN P3.26 IS BUILT: delete the clock-derived score outright rather than replacing it with another number - a recombined constitution's diversity is either computed from the two parents' actual content or not reported at all - and build mitosis on the lineage field W599 added, where a child's parent_vsb and generation make the inheritance checkable and the funds transfer assertable. Clause 6's own words are the boundary: meiosis produces a CANDIDATE, never a birth, and a recombined constitution reaches an entity only through ratification.

items.title: generation means two different things in two stores: applied evolutions in the VSB store, lineage depth on the living roster
items.why: FOUND W600 BY READING P3.2 CLAUSE (5) AGAINST THE TREE, and the misreading had already reached a guard I wrote. vsb['generation'] has exactly ONE writer - agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2914, inside the evolution-APPLY path after the Owner approves - and counts APPLIED EVOLUTIONS; W493 was registered specifically to stop a FILING cycle advancing it, so this field's meaning is load-bearing and already defended. The living roster's 'generation', which W599 added in register(), is LINEAGE DEPTH from a parent: 0 for a founder-established entity, parent+1 for a child. TWO STORES, ONE NAME, TWO FACTS. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE EXACT DEFECT P3.2 CLAUSE (5) EXISTS TO PREVENT: a child established from a parent has evolved ZERO times and carries lineage depth 1, so a reader taking the roster field as the evolution count re-scores the pillar for an entity that never evolved. W600's first version of that guard leg did precisely this, and its blinds went RED throughout - which is the lesson worth keeping: a blind proves a guard notices a change to WHAT IT ALREADY LOOKS AT and is silent on whether that is what the clause names. REMEDY: rename the roster field to lineage_generation and grep every reader (the roster, the Cockpit, any status payload); keep vsb['generation'] as the evolution measure because W493's work is built on it. A guard must assert the two are DIFFERENT fields - drive a newly established child and assert lineage depth 1 WITH applied evolutions 0 - because asserting either alone cannot tell them apart. W600 added that cross-store assertion and the lineage_basis check as an interim screen; the RENAME is this row.
items.source: W600 (reading P3.2 clause (5) against the tree)
items.slot_source: P3.2 clause (5) is the clause the collision breaks: its subject is whether an instance has evolved, and the field this round's first guard leg read means lineage depth instead. The roster field was added by the round that also delivered P3.2 clauses (1)-(4), so the item that introduced the collision is the item that owns fixing it

One reader existed outside the guards (resolve_parent reading the parent's depth); it falls back to the old key so a roster record written W599-W602 still resolves. The guard drives a child: lineage_generation 1 on the roster, no field called generation there, applied evolutions 0 in the VSB store, and the pillar re-score REFUSED for it. Blinds red: the rename reverted, the legacy fallback removed, and the gate reading the roster's lineage instead of the evolution count.

items.title: P3.2 clause (5) has no subject: nothing re-scores a living-plan pillar per instance, so a 'no re-score at generation 0' guard is vacuous at every generation
items.why: MEASURED W600. Clause (5) asks that the living-plan pillar be re-scored ONLY when an instance has evolved >= 1 generation, with a guard driving generation 0 and asserting NO re-score. Every 'pillar' in agentic_core/ is PLATFORM-level - api/living_plan.py (the vision's own pillars plus an adherence scorecard), api/cognition.py, api/integration_surface.py, api/transformation.py, api/v138/ceo.py. NOTHING scores a pillar per VSB instance. So the clause's subject is not built-but-unreachable and not built-but-unsurfaced: it is NOT BUILT, and the assertion the clause asks for would be vacuously true at every generation - green only because red is unreachable, which is the instrument-that-cannot-fail class. THIS IS WHY P3.2 DID NOT CLOSE IN W600: clauses (1) to (4) are delivered and driven red, and an item closes on its WHOLE bar. WHOEVER BUILDS IT: gate on vsb['generation'] >= 1, NOT on the living roster's lineage field (see the generation-collision row - a child that has evolved nothing carries lineage depth 1); drive generation 0 and assert the re-score is REFUSED rather than merely absent, because an absent re-score and a refused one are different facts; and place the refusal where a caller can RECEIVE it, not inside an except-pass.

items.title: Twenty-one positive source presence checks a COMMENT alone can satisfy; ten already pass on documentation only
items.why: MEASURED W600 REPO-WIDE after the blind run found five vacuous legs in one guard, three of them this cause. A guard asserting a literal is present in a source file is satisfied by that literal appearing in a COMMENT, so deleting the code it was written for leaves the check passing. This is the SILENT half of the class scripts/selfcheck_diff.py already screens as [banned]: the forbidden direction goes RED and costs a run, this direction goes GREEN and costs the guard. THE SWEEP: 21 sites across the suite; 11 have the literal in BOTH a comment and code (deleting the code leaves the comment); 10 are satisfied by a comment ONLY and are therefore passing on documentation right now. NOT 21 DEFECTS, and the count must not be read that way: several comment-only cases are LEGITIMATE - a guard asserting that a file RECORDS a reason in its own comment is a valid assertion, and this repo does that deliberately (a documented principle in religious_domain/api.py, a stated failure direction in horizon_guardrails.py, a recorded error code in conftest.py). The defect is the PAIRING of a comment-satisfied check with a message that CLAIMS A SURFACE. W600 added the [presence] leg which flags the comment+code case always and the comment-only case only when the assertion's own message speaks about a reader, a page or a render - and it was driven against the pre-fix guard first, because its FIRST version used a character class excluding the newline and flagged NOTHING on the very text it was written for: it would have shipped as an instrument that cannot fail. ALSO FOUND, and it is why [banned] reported ok for this round: SRC_READ_RE requires the path root to be literally root, app or S, so every guard reading a file via Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] - the idiom most of this suite now uses - is invisible to check_banned too. THE WORK: walk the 11 comment+code sites and the comment-only sites whose message claims a surface, and either assert over a comment-stripped copy or assert the rendered expression; and decide whether to widen SRC_READ_RE (its narrowness is deliberate for check_banned's literal scoping, so that is its own measurement).

items.title: The Qur'an study panel's provenance setter is never called, so every report reads 'provenance not recorded' - and the guard asserting otherwise passes on a comment
items.why: FOUND W600 BY THE NEW [presence] PRE-FLIGHT LEG ON ITS FIRST RUN, which is the clearest argument for the leg existing. FU-412's hold on the avatar path is released only by P3.28 clause (3), and clause (3) is released only by this ruling, so the hold's release condition now names a decision rather than a build.

So the 'Subject:' line in an upstream node's output, which reaches the next prompt under 'Inputs from upstream nodes', is read as the user's subject and counted for terms. orchestrator.py:612-614 labels the user's goal 'Overall goal:' and the task 'Your task:'. items.title: The Qur'an-translation refusal sends the learner to an edition route that refuses every translation edition — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11 rule 4 / A.9.3: translation of sacred text refuses rather than serving a template; A.12.1: only sources with an explicit licence and a named canonical edition, 'sequenced by licensing difficulty: translations first'. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/qep/translation/translate {text: Arabic basmala} → 422 with the pointer sentence above (and the same sentence sits in GET /api/v1/qep/translation/status `sacred_text`). GET /api/v1/qep/ayah/1/1?edition=en.sahih → 422; ?edition=en.asad → 422. No translation edition exists in the allowlist, and the studio copy beside the box reads 'Qur'an translations come only from licensed, sourced editions', which implies some are served. Non-Arabic text → 503 'no model resource is available to translate' (correct floor refusal). EVIDENCE: agentic_core/religious_domain/api.py:102-104 (`_ALLOWED_EDITIONS = {quran-uthmani, quran-simple, quran-simple-enhanced, quran-tajweed}` with the comment 'never a translation edition here'), :452-453 and :510-511 (the 422); the translate handler's refusal text (grep 'a translation edition' in the same file); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/QEPStudio.tsx:150-151 (`setTrRefusal(errorMessage(e))` renders the 422 detail verbatim), :418 (the 'licensed, sourced editions' copy); apps/workstation-superapp/src/lib/api.ts:91-94 (`errorMessage` → 'Failed (HTTP 422): <detail>'). Live probes 2026-10-09 against 127.0.0.1:8031. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: NO — the refusal names a path that does not exist and no surface says so.. WHY THIS TIER: The sentence a learner is shown on the QEP studio after clicking Translate on Arabic text is: 'Failed (HTTP 422): translation of Arabic / Qur'anic text is NOT OFFERED, by ruling (A.9.3)… Translations of the Qur'an come only from licensed, sourced editions (A.12.1) - read one with GET /api/v1/qep/ayah/{surah}/{ayah}?edition=<a translation edition>'. That route rejects every non-Arabic edition (422 'edition must be one of [quran-simple, quran-simple-enhanced, quran-tajweed, quran-uthmani]'), and the handler's own comment says 'never a translation edition here'. The refusal itself is correct and constitutional; the ALTERNATIVE it asserts does not exist anywhere on the platform. That is a reached surface telling a user something untrue about what the platform can do (tier 1), not an omission (tier 2) and not a disclosed gap (tier 3): nothing on the studio, in /translation/status or in the 422 body says no translation edition is served. Ranked first because it is on the one surface the constitution binds hardest and a learner following it hits a dead end they were told was the sanctioned path. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /api/v1/qep/translation/translate with the UTF-8 basmala returns 422 whose detail tells the learner to 'read one with GET /api/v1/qep/ayah/{surah}/{ayah}?edition=<a translation edition>'; GET /api/v1/qep/ayah/1/1?edition=en.sahih and ?edition=en.asad both return 422 'edition must be one of [quran-simple, quran-simple-enhanced, quran-tajweed, quran-uthmani]'. The allowlist at agentic_core/religious_domain/api.py:104 holds four Arabic text editions and its own comment (:102-103) says 'never a translation edition here'. The same sentence is served in GET /translation/status `sacred_text`, and QEPStudio.tsx:151/:424 renders the 422 detail verbatim as the amber refusal line; the studio copy at :418 ('Qur'an translations come only from licensed, sourced editions') reinforces that some are served. No surface — not the studio, not /translation/status, not the 422 body, not the vision's A.12.1 (which lists recitation audio, Hadith and Tafsir as 'unserved' but not translations) — says that zero translation editions exist on the platform. Tier 1 rather than 2: this is an assertion, not an omission — the refusal affirmatively names a sanctioned path that does not exist, so a learner who follows it is told the platform can do something it cannot. Not tier 3: nothing states the gap. The constitutional refusal itself is correct, which is why the verdict is PARTIAL rather than STUB. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Either drop the '?edition=<a translation edition>' clause from the refusal and the status `sacred_text` (and soften the studio copy to 'no licensed translation edition is served on this deployment yet'), or honour A.12.1's own sequencing by allowlisting one licensed translation edition with licence + edition recorded in `_corpus_provenance` so the pointer becomes true.

items.title: On the floor the tafsir tool fills Exegesis, Related Verses and Key Lessons with bigrams lifted from the server's own prompt wrapper and labels them the reader's request terms — MILESTONE M2 ledger v13 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v13 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11 rule 4: floor-served output is never presented as scholarship; A.11: 'The same rule that makes translation refuse is not applied here' (the tafsir surface is the constitution's weakest point). OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/religion/quran-tafsir {surah:1, ayah_start:1, ayah_end:3} and {surah:2, 285–290}: the Arabic is fetched and labelled (correct), `sections_withheld` = [Transliteration, Translation] only, and the five remaining headings (Context of Revelation, Linguistic Analysis, Exegesis, Related Verses, Key Lessons and Guidance) each carry the same five wrapper-derived bigrams. By contrast /religion/fatwa-research withholds 7 sections, /hadith-study 7, /interfaith 7 ('a citation or a school's position that nothing looked up is worse than silence'). The ReligionHub tafsir description also says 'Workstation's own AI then writes structured study notes' with no floor caveat, unlike the fatwa and hadith descriptions. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/religion.py:284-291 (the 'Subject: tafsir of … is not repeated in them' line the floor extracts from), :327-342 (only Transliteration/Translation withheld), :96-99 and :176-181 (siblings withhold research sections); apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/domains/ReligionHub.tsx:165-168 (tafsir description), :172-187 (renderExtra shows reference, Arabic, floor_note, sections_withheld); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/DomainTool.tsx:351-366 (floor_note, text, disclaimer order). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: PARTLY — 'not scholarship' is disclosed; that the bullets are the server's instruction text, and that the exegesis headings are served rather than withheld as the siblings do, is not.. WHY THIS TIER: Under every heading the reader is shown 'The list below is the request's most frequent terms, not findings about them' followed by '- sourced arabic · - repeated them · - tafsir surah · - arabic shown · - not repeated'. The reader typed surah 1, ayah 1–3 and 'classical'; none of those words is in their request — they are bigrams of the server-side line 'the sourced Arabic is shown to the reader above these notes and is not repeated in them'. The sentence is therefore untrue about the reader's own input, and nothing on the surface says where the words came from (tier 2, an invisible defect). It is not tier 1 because the surrounding floor_note ('the study notes below are a structured frame, not scholarship') and the disclaimer reach the screen, so no scholarly claim is made about the ayaat. It is not tier 3 because the mislabel itself is undisclosed, and because the three sibling research tools WITHHOLD every research section on the floor while tafsir still serves five headings over sacred text — a difference the surface does not state. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /api/v1/religion/quran-tafsir {surah:1, 1-3, classical} returns five served headings (Context of Revelation, Linguistic Analysis, Exegesis, Related Verses, Key Lessons) each carrying 'The list below is the request's most frequent terms, not findings about them' followed by '- sourced arabic · - repeated them · - tafsir surah · - arabic shown · - not repeated' — bigrams of the server-side Subject line at agentic_core/api/religion.py:293-294, not of anything the reader typed. sections_withheld is ['Transliteration','Translation'] only (:327-342), while fatwa-research and hadith-study withhold every research heading on the floor (:90-99, :170-185). ReligionHub.tsx:165-168 describes the tool as 'Workstation's own AI then writes structured study notes' with no floor caveat in the description. I hold the assessor's tier 2 rather than escalating to 1: the mislabelled sentence names no figure, outcome or scholarly content, the floor_note ('a structured frame, not scholarship') and the disclaimer reach the screen through renderExtra and DomainTool.tsx:351-366, and the wrapper sentence the bigrams come from is printed in the same paragraph ('over: tafsir of Surah 1:1-3 — the sourced Arabic is shown to the reader above these notes…'), so a reader is confused about the bullets' origin rather than told a false outcome about the ayaat. Not tier 3: nothing on the surface says the bullets are wrapper noise, or that tafsir serves five exegesis headings on the floor where its three siblings withhold theirs. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Apply W498's rule to tafsir: on the floor withhold the five study sections (name them in `sections_withheld`) and serve only the sourced Arabic, reference, provenance and referral; or at minimum pass the floor a subject that is the user's reference alone so the 'request terms' label is true.

items.title: The Board Pack's strategic layer quotes a platform-template sentence as the entity's "vision on record", and the W635 note built to flag that is suppressed on every Genesis-born entity — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R2), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §13 / §15.9: the Chief-owned business plan opens with Executive Summary · Concept · Vision — the founder's idea; §15.6 honesty over polish, label what is generated. OBSERVED: bp.json for vsb-9024a06a5f: layers.strategic.content = "[as of 2026-10-09 10:37 UTC] Strategic position derived from the plan itself: 0 aim(s) and 4 objective(s) on the roadmap; vision on record: A self-running waqf_ltd_hybrid VSB IDBO that commercialises this solution beneficently.; mission on record: Deliver: I keep bees in Yorkshire ..." and `vision_note` is ABSENT. layers.constitutional.vision = the founder's problem statement, vision_source = "the founder's problem statement, verbatim - not authored". The guard at agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1598 emits the note only when `_cv584[:60] not in _sc584`; but the strategic content always also quotes "mission on record: Deliver: {problem[:160]}" (cadence.py:188, genesis.py:1181) and the constitutional vision IS the problem statement, so problem[:60] is always inside the strategic text and the condition is always False on this path. Verified: cv[:60] in sc == True. The business plan's own `strategy` field (GET /api/v1/business-plan?scope=vsb-9024a06a5f) now holds the same cadence text, so the plan page also prints "vision on record: A self-running ..." under Strategy. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1593-1602 (the FU-584 guard); agentic_core/organism/cadence.py:181-190 (_compose STRATEGIC); agentic_core/api/genesis.py:1176-1182 (templated vision/mission); scratchpad bp.json and the business-plan GET; python check printed `cv[:60] in sc: True`. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partially: the pack narrative says "the business plan holds no Owner-written vision" and the plan page marks vision as templated; the strategic layer itself says nothing, and its purpose-built vision_note never appears.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader of GET /api/v1/vsb/{id}/board-pack is shown, in layers.strategic.content: "vision on record: A self-running waqf_ltd_hybrid VSB IDBO that commercialises this solution beneficently." Nobody wrote that sentence — genesis.py:1180 `plan["vision"] = f"A self-running {req.entity_type} VSB IDBO ..."` is a code template — and the same pack's constitutional layer says the vision is the founder's problem statement "verbatim - not authored". The strategic layer carries no qualifier, so the shortfall is invisible AT THAT LAYER (tier 2). It is not tier 1 because the sentence does exist in the plan's vision field (it is 'on record' as a template) and the pack's narrative and the plan page (PlanOpening.tsx marks `vision` as templated) say no Owner-written vision exists; it is not tier 3 because the layer that quotes it does not say so, and the fix meant to make it say so cannot fire. REFUTER: The finding is correct as far as it goes and too kind. Reproduced: bp for vsb-9024a06a5f and for my fresh entity vsb-9ac0249129 both quote 'vision on record: A self-running waqf_ltd_hybrid VSB IDBO ...' (genesis.py:1180 template) in layers.strategic.content with no vision_note; the constitutional vision is the problem statement verbatim and the strategic text also quotes 'mission on record: Deliver: {problem[:160]}', so `_cv584[:60] not in _sc584` (vsb.py:1598) is always False on the Genesis path and the note cannot fire. But the same W635 insertion did more than fail to fire: the diff (git show 3613fbe3 -- agentic_core/api/vsb.py) placed the FU-584 block between the `for _k in (constitutional, operational)` loop and its `setdefault('present', True)` / `setdefault('basis', ...)` lines, which now sit inside the new `if` (vsb.py:1603-1605) — pre-W635 (3613fbe3^ lines 1584-1588) they were loop body. Result, executed: GET /vsb/vsb-9024a06a5f/board-pack returns layers_present = ['action_plan','strategic'] and layers_state.constitutional.basis = null, operational.basis = null, although constitutional holds the vision/mission and operational the live snapshot; for vsb-9ac0249129 layers_present = []. GenesisJourney.tsx:1271-1273 prints that list as the 'Board Pack' chip ('none hold content' when empty) and :1291-1295 renders '2 empty' / '4 empty' with a tooltip 'constitutional: empty | operational: empty'. That is a reached surface telling a founder that the layer carrying their own vision holds nothing — an untrue statement, not an omission — so tier 1, not the assessor's tier 2. The guard test for FU-584 (integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py:47306, `'"vision_note"' in _src('agentic_core/api/vsb.py')`) asserts a source literal and never drives a pack, so it is vacuous for both defects. Verdict stays PARTIAL: the vision data is present and the narrative and PlanOpening.tsx disclose the template; the pack count and the quoted template vision are the shortfalls. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: In vsb.py:1598 compare against the MISSION-stripped strategic text (or compare the quoted vision substring after 'vision on record:' to constitutional.vision directly), and have cadence._compose label the quoted vision with its plan provenance (`field_sources.vision`) so the layer says 'template' itself.

items.title: A Spawn-Studio or Synthesis-Studio VSB's plan opening is headed "Chief's Opening" over code templates that carry no template mark — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R3), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5 / §15.9: the Chief owns the living Business Plan, which opens with Executive Summary · Concept · Vision — the founder's idea and intent framed by the digital-twin Chief; §15.6 honesty over polish, never fabricate. OBSERVED: GET /api/v1/business-plan?scope=vsb-dcbb1231b9 returns executive_summary/vision/mission filled from templates and `provenance: null` (also vsb-30550d832e). Genesis-born entities vsb-c0c50028a1 and vsb-9024a06a5f return provenance.templated_fields = [executive_summary, vision, mission, strategy, concept] and opening_written_by = "code templates filled from the establish request — not the Chief, and not a model…". PlanOpening.tsx computes `allTemplated` from `provenance.templated_fields`; with provenance null the set is empty and the heading falls to 'Chief’s Opening'. No provenance badge and no 'written by' sentence render either. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2264-2278 (enrich_vsb_entity seeds executive_summary/vision/mission/strategy + three KPI-less objectives, writes no `provenance`); callers: api/vsb.py:2555 (/api/v1/vsb/spawn, driven by apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/VSBSpawnStudio.tsx:62), api/synthesis_studio.py:347 and :441, economy/turnover.py:293 (child spawn). Contrast agentic_core/api/genesis.py:1183-1206 (_seed_plan_from_journey writes field_sources/templated_fields/opening_written_by). apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/PlanOpening.tsx:76-82 (heading logic), rendered by pages/enterprise/BusinessPlan.tsx:186 and pages/enterprise/VSBCockpit.tsx:827. VSBSpawnStudio.tsx:519 links to /business-plan?scope=<vsb_id>. Live: curl of the four roster plans above. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. On this path the page shows the 'Chief’s Opening' heading, the 'owned by your Chief' header, no provenance badge, no pending list and no 'generated from your establish answers' sentence.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader of /business-plan?scope=vsb-dcbb1231b9 (reached from VSBSpawnStudio's "Open plan →" link, and from the VSB Cockpit's plan tab) is shown the heading "Chief’s Opening" above an Executive Summary ("Halal Eats Birmingham is a living VSB IDBO established to solve: …"), a Vision ("A self-running waqf_ltd_hybrid VSB IDBO that commercialises this solution beneficently.") and a Mission ("Deliver: …") that are f-strings written by `enrich_vsb_entity`, composed by neither the Chief nor any model. The page header on the same screen says the plan is "owned by your Chief". That is an assertion of authorship the system did not produce, on a reached surface — tier 1, not tier 2, because the shortfall is not merely unsaid, it is contradicted by the heading. The Genesis-established path (W505/FU-158) records `templated_fields` + `opening_written_by` and the component then says "Plan opening — generated from your establish answers"; the spawn path never got that fix, so the FU-158 class is re-opened at its second writer (W475's 'fix every writer' rule). REFUTER: Reproduced. The spawn/Studio/child paths seed five f-string fields and write no provenance, so PlanOpening's templated set is empty and the heading falls to 'Chief’s Opening' over text no Chief or model wrote; the Genesis path got the FU-158 fix (field_sources/templated_fields/opening_written_by) and this second writer did not. Tier 1 rather than 2 because the shortfall is not merely unsaid — the heading asserts an authorship the system did not produce, the same claim the repo's own FU-158 fix classed as false on the other path. Not tier 0/3: nothing on the reached page (BusinessPlan via the Studio's 'Open plan →' link, VSBCockpit plan tab) says the fields are templates. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Move the FU-158 provenance block (field_sources, templated_fields, opening_written_by, body_pending) into enrich_vsb_entity so every writer of the seeded opening stamps it, and add a guard that reads a spawned plan over HTTP and asserts `templated_fields` is non-empty.

items.title: Change Control terminally rejects a HIGH change on an 'organism health' figure that counts §11 lexicon flags over the platform's own floor text as compliance regressions — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R3), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5 (Recorded W464): a HIGH change approved by a review waits for Board ratification; Change Control governs change at arm's length; §15.6 never fabricate, label simulation; §11 'a screen may flag and escalate but never clear' (W483). OBSERVED: At 10:36 board/status reported organism_health 1.0. One org cascade (22 floor calls, §11 screen escalations ['ethical:human']) plus one VSB spawn (website/webapp/mobile/repo screens) drove /api/v1/organism/systems to {health 0.1, by_type: {compliance_escalation: 5}} and health-summary to mode EMERGENCY. cca-63f6f1590b (code_change, HIGH) submitted at 10:39:52 recorded health_gate.verdict 'fail' and immune_threat 'CRITICAL'; its review at 10:40:44 returned decision 'rejected', decision_source 'health_threshold_rule'. After the 5-minute window expired (health back to 1.0) an identical-tier change cca-1334f3af84 was rule-APPROVED and reached the Board queue — the verdict depended on nothing about either change. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:486-492 (`if _comp.get('overall') == 'fail' or _escalated: immune.record(f'compliance:{label}', … 'compliance_escalation')`); agentic_core/organism/immune.py:67 (`health = max(0.0, 1.0 - total/10.0)`), :69-76 threat tiers; agentic_core/compliance/ethical_engine.py:47-48 (_HARM_SEVERE regex), :92-97 (escalate=True on a match); UEG compliance.screen node for label 'cascade' with escalations ['ethical:human']; agentic_core/api/change_control.py:1445-1470 (review: no marker → health rule; 'rejection is terminal'); agentic_core/api/board.py:111-112 (_ORGANISM_HEALTH_SCOPE string); live records: GET /api/v1/cca/cca-63f6f1590b, GET /api/v1/organism/health-summary ("Organism critical — measured health 10%"), GET /api/v1/organism/systems; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/ChangeControlAgency.tsx:102,305-310,366-370. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the record says the rule decided it and names the 0.10 figure; nothing on the change record, the Board status basis or the organism summary says the figure is a count of lexicon flags on floor-composed text rather than failures or regressions.. WHY THIS TIER: The record a submitter is shown (ChangeControlAgency.tsx renders review_result verbatim and 'decided by: organism-health threshold rule (not the model)') says: "MEASURED composite_health 0.10 < 0.5 → rejected", and the Board/organism surfaces describe that figure as "the immune system's health: AI-call failures and compliance regressions only" and "Organism critical — measured health 10%. Emergency mode." What the figure actually counted in this session was five `compliance_escalation` immune events — the ethical lexicon matching a severe-harm verb (e.g. 'abuse') inside text the deterministic floor composed for the cascade and the entity's generated public faces. W483 defines an escalation as a flag for a human that 'never convicts'; recording it as an immune error at 10% of health each means ten flags in five minutes put the organism in EMERGENCY and every HIGH review is rule-REJECTED, which change_control.py says is terminal. The submitter is therefore told their change was rejected because the organism's health regressed, when no regression was found and nothing read the change. A reader could argue tier 2 (the mechanism is named on the record), but the record asserts a measured health that misdescribes what it measured and the rejection is a terminal governance outcome asserted on it — that lands on tier 1. The twin pre-validation on the same record reads 'fail' from the same figure. REFUTER: Reproduced the mechanism in an isolated process and confirmed the live records. One evidence correction: BoardOfDirectors.tsx only TYPES live.organism_health (line 30) and never renders it or the 'compliance regressions' basis, so that sentence is response-body only; the reached surfaces are the Change Control record ('MEASURED composite_health 0.10 < 0.5 → rejected', 'decided by: organism-health threshold rule'), OrganismDashboard ('10%', 'CRITICAL', 'N errors') and OrganismAnatomy ('Organism critical — measured health 10%'). Tier 1 rather than 2 because those are assertions, not silences: 'N errors' and 'measured health 10%' report failures that did not occur — every event in the window was a word-list flag the ethical engine itself labels 'not an assessment … escalated for a human', recorded by quality.py as an immune error at 10% of health each — and a HIGH change was terminally rejected on that figure while an identical-tier change was approved 12 minutes later on nothing about either change. Not the environment: the floor did not cause this; W483's routing of an escalation into immune.record did. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Stop recording an escalation (a flag) as an immune error — record it to the UEG and route to a human as W483 intended, and record only `overall == 'fail'`; or at minimum exclude floor-served screens. Make review_result name what the measured health counted (immune.by_type) so a rule rejection carries its own basis.
