I considered tier 3 ('a surface nobody reaches'): the stats route IS fetched by a page (which ignores the field), and the response body is what a caller is given, so the fabrication is reached in the sense the tiering defines. Severity is low because no page prints any of the three. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Remove swarm_health and the trust and convergence literals, or return null with a basis; stamp generated_at from the clock or drop it.

But a user who picks it under the canon's meaning gets prompts instructed to "Assume limited capital, intermittent infrastructure and thin specialist staffing", and the surface says nothing about that, so the shortfall is invisible rather than disclosed. VISION CLAIM: §3A offering 1: immediate, usable, in-house-AI-mediated tools in each of the six domains, of comparable scope. OBSERVED: All six domains execute and return 200. On this deployment every narrative is the floor's heading frame (lesson plan sections each read "Native structured frame ... - fractions - maths"). items.title: The organism's 'measured health' counts the immune term as measured even when it has observed nothing, and every health gate passes on it — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8: profitability, satisfaction, founder-alignment and live compliance are 'continuously monitored'; §8 W482 rule: 'An engine computes or says it cannot … assessable: false with a reason, never an invented number'; §17.5 twin pre-validation before major change. OBSERVED: agentic_core/organism/biobus.py:363 sets immune_health 'measured': True unconditionally; _measured_only = immune alone when no circuit is tracked, so it is never None and mode_decidable is always true. Immune and self-healing are fed by the SAME call sites (ai/native/orchestrator.py _organism_report, ai/gateway.py), and with the floor serving, zero model calls are recorded — so 1.0 is the absence of observations. The same code treats that identical condition as 'defaulted to 1.0, not a measurement' for self-healing. Consumers: /organism/health-summary, /organism/status, CCA submit health_gate (verdict 'pass', decided_on composite_health_measured_only) and twin-prevalidate (verdict 'pass', source health_gate_default). The immune figure does become a real reading once compliance screens record fails (it later fell to 0.3 from 7 compliance_fail events), so the defect is specifically the no-observation state being certified as measured. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/organism/status at boot: composite_health_measured_only 1.0, immune events_in_window 0, self_healing overall_health null, mode_decidable true, health_summary 'measured health 100%'. POST /api/v1/cca/submit -> health_gate {measured_health 0.9, verdict 'pass'}. POST /api/v1/cca/{id}/twin-prevalidate -> verdict 'pass', method '…where too little is measured the gate returns not_assessable rather than a pass'. agentic_core/api/change_control.py:1388-1393 (not_assessable only when _m is None). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the 40% weight and the defaulted/simulated terms are disclosed; that the 'measured' 40% itself rests on zero observations is not.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader is shown 'Organism nominal on what is measured — MAINTENANCE_FOCUS cycle, measured health 100%' and, on the Anatomy card, a large '100% measured only' with a chip 'immune_health 100% · w0.4 · measured'. On a fresh process no AI call had been carried (self-healing in the same payload says 'no circuit has carried a call yet — nothing measured, health unknown' and is labelled DEFAULTED), yet immune is hard-coded measured:true. That is an assertion of a measurement that was not taken, not an omission, so it is tier 1 rather than tier 2; and the twin gate's own sentence 'where too little is measured the gate returns not_assessable rather than a pass' is unreachable on the healthy path because of it. REFUTER: Mechanism reproduced in source and partly live; tier moved DOWN from 1 to 2. agentic_core/organism/biobus.py hard-codes immune_health measured:True, and _measured_only is immune-alone when no circuit is tracked, so it is never None on the normal path and the not_assessable branch at change_control.py:1389 is reachable only on the context-error fallback. agentic_core/organism/immune.py is a pure FAILURE counter over a 300s window (health = 1 - failures/10) with no count of observations, so a quiet process and a healthy one read identically. I could not reproduce the boot state itself (the window already held 7 failures: measured-only 0.3, DEGRADED), but I watched the same figure return to 0.8 / NOMINAL about two minutes later purely because failures aged out of the window. Why tier 2 and not 1: the reading is a real count, not an invented one - zero failures recorded IS what the instrument measured, and the surface shows its derivation ('health and threat are computed from N failure(s) in the window', the Anatomy immune card prints 'N errors in window', health_basis prints '40% measured'). Self-healing is a RATE over calls and is undefined at zero calls; immune is a count and is defined at zero, so the two are not the identical condition the assessor says. What the reader is NOT told is that the counter has no denominator and that failures silently expire after five minutes, so '100% measured' can mean 'nothing happened' - and every gate passes on it. That is an invisible shortfall (tier 2), not a disclosed one (tier 3). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Have ImmuneSystem report an observation count (calls/screens seen in the window) and set immune 'measured' false, measured_only None, when it is zero — so the existing not_assessable branch becomes reachable and the summary says 'nothing measured yet'.

items.title: The Economy page's default entity 'Workstation IDBO (apex)' is, by the API's own statement, an unregistered simulation — the page never says so, and its conjured WST funds registered entities — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §12: each VSB is an autonomous economic entity that self-manages its finances with double-entry books, Owner profit share and reinvestment; virtual money until the Owner directs real rails. OBSERVED: POST /economy/cycle on the default vsb_id returned registration 'UNREGISTERED' with the simulation basis, yet the same cycle (a) accrued 140 WST to the Owner and allowed a 40 WST payout, (b) 'funded' a venture position — '105.0 WST credited to the investee's intake this cycle' for registered entity vsb-1a0e91006d, whose later autonomous cycle distributed 226.8 WST — and (c) let 50 WST be transferred from its reserve fund to registered vsb-54c32fdef9, where it entered that entity's waterfall. So the statement that the entries 'belong to no entity that exists' is also not the whole truth: the simulated funds reach entities that do exist. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/economy/cycle {revenue:1000,costs:100} -> registration UNREGISTERED + venture_investment.positions[0].funding_state 'funded'; POST /api/v1/economy/transfer from workstation-idbo -> 200, receiver_pending_wst 50; next cycle on receiver: inter_vsb_received_wst 50. agentic_core/api/economy.py:310-317; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/VSBEconomy.tsx:56,225-226,305 (no reference to registration/registration_basis anywhere in src). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — disclosed in the API body only; the UI drops the field.. WHY THIS TIER: The API response says "'workstation-idbo' is not a registered living entity: this cycle is a SIMULATION run on request values, and the ledger entries and any Owner accrual it wrote belong to no entity that exists". The page (VSBEconomy.tsx) reads only d.cycle and d.governance, so that sentence is never rendered; the user sees an option labelled 'Workstation IDBO (apex)', an Owner balance of 140 WST and a board pack. Nothing shown is a false figure (the general 'virtual/simulated WST' banner is present), so it is not tier 1; the shortfall is real and invisible at the surface, so it is not tier 3. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /economy/cycle on workstation-idbo returned registration 'UNREGISTERED' with the SIMULATION basis, and the same response carried owner_accrual 140 WST and a venture position for registered vsb-1a0e91006d with funding_state 'funded' ('21.08 WST credited to the investee's intake this cycle'). The transfer route accepts workstation-idbo as sender (overdraft refused only on balance: 'reserve fund holds 350.0 WST'). VSBEconomy.tsx defaults vsbId to 'workstation-idbo', labels it 'Workstation IDBO (apex)', and never reads registration or registration_basis (its only 'registration' strings concern the entity form). Tier 2 stands: every figure the page shows is labelled virtual/simulated WST, so no rendered figure is false (not tier 1); the specific fact that the default entity is unregistered and its funds reach real entities is stated only in the API body and dropped by the page (not tier 3). The API sentence 'belong to no entity that exists' is loose about the venture credit but is about the ledger entries and the accrual, so I do not raise it to tier 1. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Render registration_basis on the cycle card and beside the entity selector; and either register the apex as a living entity or refuse venture funding and outbound transfers from an unregistered id.

items.title: The Heartbeat page says the organism beats 'every ~60s' while the loop actually beats every 120s (up to 200s in rest phases) — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8: circadian operation — the organism runs itself on a continuous heartbeat. OBSERVED: heartbeat.run() sleeps interval_seconds * (1 / phase_intensity); with intensity 0.5 that is 120s, with 0.3 it is 200s. /heartbeat/status publishes interval_seconds 60 with no effective-interval field, and the page presents it as the cadence. The 'Intensity 50%' tile is shown but nothing links it to the beat period. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/heartbeat/status recent[].at across six beats; agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:226,876-879; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/organism/HeartbeatMonitor.tsx:119. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The page prints '{beats} beats · every ~{interval_seconds}s' = 'every ~60s'. Observed automatic beats were at 20:31:00, 20:33:01, 20:35:01, 20:37:01, 20:39:02, 20:41:02 — 120s apart. That is a stated figure that is untrue by a factor of two on a reached page, which is tier 1 by definition rather than an omission; the consequence is small, hence low severity. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. /heartbeat/status reports interval_seconds 60 and phase_intensity 0.5; automatic beats 10, 11, 12 were stamped 20:41:02, 20:43:02, 20:45:02 - 120s apart. heartbeat.py run() sleeps interval_seconds * (1/intensity). HeartbeatMonitor.tsx:119 prints '{beats} beats · every ~{interval_seconds}s' under 'Beating', i.e. 'every ~60s'. Tier 1 stands: it is a stated figure about the running system that is wrong by a factor of two on a reached page, not an omission (tier 2) and not disclosed anywhere (the Intensity tile is not linked to the period). Low severity - nobody is blocked by it. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Publish effective_interval_seconds (interval / intensity) from status and render that, or say 'base 60s, currently every ~120s (phase intensity 50%)'.

items.title: The living-cadence panel overstates time since the last refresh by exactly one hour during British Summer Time — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.3/§17.5: the living business plan refreshes on cadence and is never more than five minutes stale; figures shown are measured. OBSERVED: cadence.py parses the stored UTC stamp with time.mktime(time.strptime(...)) - time.timezone. mktime applies local DST but time.timezone is the non-DST offset, so on a UK machine in BST every parsed stamp lands 3600s early and elapsed is overstated by an hour. Weekly and quarterly refreshes therefore fire one hour early for half the year. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/organism/cadence at 20:31:57Z -> layers.strategic.due {elapsed_seconds 3657.928, last_refresh_at '2026-10-09T20:31:00Z', reason 'not due: 0.04 day(s) since the last refresh…'}; agentic_core/organism/cadence.py:85; apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/CadencePanel.tsx renders due.reason. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: 57 seconds after a refresh stamped 2026-10-09T20:31:00Z the surface said 'not due: 0.04 day(s) since the last refresh' with elapsed_seconds 3657.9 — the whole displayed figure is the error (true value 0.00 days). A wrong computed figure rendered by CadencePanel is tier 1 rather than tier 2; the practical effect is only that elapsed-time triggers fire an hour early, hence low severity. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. At 20:43:35Z, GET /organism/cadence returned last_refresh_at 2026-10-09T20:31:00Z with elapsed_seconds 4355.391 and reason 'not due: 0.05 day(s) since the last refresh'. True elapsed is 755s (0.01 day); the excess is exactly 3600s. cadence.py:85 uses time.mktime(...) - time.timezone, which ignores DST, on a machine in BST. CadencePanel.tsx:26 renders l.due?.reason verbatim. Tier 1 stands: a computed figure shown to the reader is wrong (not an omission), and nothing discloses it. Low severity: the practical effect is period triggers firing an hour early for half the year. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Parse with calendar.timegm(time.strptime(...)) (or datetime with tzinfo=UTC) and add a test that sets TZ to a DST zone.

items.title: The KPI gate stops a marketplace listing but not a ship or a repo download, while its own refusal says 'before listing or exporting' — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.5 invariant 10: KPI gate before customer delivery (absolute). OBSERVED: kpi_release_gate is called from two sites, both in agentic_core/api/marketplace.py (listing create and from-entity). It is an honest presence test and it names what is missing — that half is delivered. Shipping the entity's repo, website, webapp and mobile surfaces and downloading the zip are ungated. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/marketplace/listings/from-entity/{vsb_id} -> 409 kpi_gate, 3 of 3 seeded objectives carry no KPI; POST /api/v1/vsb/{vsb_id}/repo/ship -> 200 shipped:true on the same entity; GET /api/v1/vsb/{vsb_id}/repo/zip -> 200. grep kpi_release_gate: marketplace.py:381,464 only. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the gate's wording implies exporting is covered.. WHY THIS TIER: The gate tells the founder 'Set a KPI on each before listing or exporting'. With no KPI set, POST /vsb/{id}/repo/ship returned shipped:true and GET /vsb/{id}/repo/zip returned 200. No surface says the gate covers the marketplace only, so the shortfall is invisible (not tier 3); the ship response's own figures are qualified ('written, not verified'), so nothing shown is false (not tier 1). REFUTER: Reproduced by execution on vsb-54c32fdef9. POST /marketplace/listings/from-entity -> 409 kpi_gate, '3 of 3 objective(s) carry no KPI ... Set a KPI on each before listing or exporting'. On the same entity POST /vsb/{id}/repo/ship -> 200 shipped:true across five surfaces, and GET /vsb/{id}/repo/zip -> 200 (29 KB). kpi_release_gate has exactly two call sites, both in marketplace.py (381, 464). Tier 2 stands: the listing half is delivered and honest; the export half is ungated and no surface says the gate is marketplace-only. Not tier 1 because 'before listing or exporting' is an instruction rather than a factual claim about the system, and the ship response qualifies itself ('written, not verified'); not tier 3 because the limit is stated nowhere. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Either call kpi_release_gate on ship/zip, or state in the gate text and on the ship result that the KPI gate applies to marketplace release only.

items.title: The scholar-review gate and the never-generate rule are enforced per route, so the general lesson-plan and deliverable routes compose the religious teaching content QEP withholds — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R1), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11 rule 1: Qur'an Arabic is NEVER AI-generated. A.12.3: a named human scholar approves AI-composed religious content before a learner sees it, enforced as a pipeline gate; unreviewed content is WITHHELD, never shown with a disclaimer. OBSERVED: screen_subject() is imported by agentic_core/api/education.py only and called once (line 74, the curriculum handler). lesson-plan, assessment, deliverables/produce and the gateway carry no sacred-text or religious-subject guard (grep of agentic_core/ai for quran/sacred finds only a comment). With a model serving, these routes would hand a model a prompt asking for Quranic Arabic and tajwid teaching with no fetch, no do-not-reproduce instruction and no review. That model-served outcome was read from source, not executed. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/education/curriculum {subject:'Quran and Tajwid: ...'} -> 409 'Not composed here ... Matched: quran, tajwid'. POST /api/v1/education/lesson-plan {subject:'Quran and Tajwid', topic:'Rules of Idgham in Surah Al-Fatiha'} -> 200, keys [plan_id, subject, topic, level, duration_minutes, lesson_plan, ai_provenance, generated_at], no screen field. POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce (brief asks for full Quran Arabic + translation + fatwa) -> 200 with a six-section frame. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The lesson-plan and deliverable responses carry the generic floor badge only; nothing says a religious subject bypassed the scholar gate.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader of the QEP studio is told 'This is not shown because no scholar has reviewed it ... A disclaimer is not a review, so nothing is shown in its place', and POST /education/curriculum refuses the same subject with 'Not composed here'. POST /education/lesson-plan for subject 'Quran and Tajwid', topic 'Rules of Idgham in Surah Al-Fatiha' returns 200 with a composed plan and no word about the gate; POST /deliverables/produce accepts a brief asking for 'the full Arabic text of the Quran verses, a translation, and a fatwa'. Not tier 1: on this floor-only deployment what comes back is a labelled frame, no Arabic and no ruling is fabricated. Not tier 3: neither response says the gate was skipped, so the shortfall is invisible. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution and grep. screen_subject is imported and called only in agentic_core/api/education.py (line 74). POST /education/curriculum with a Quran/Tajwid subject -> 409 'Not composed here'; POST /education/lesson-plan with subject 'Quran and Tajwid' -> 200 with a composed floor frame and no gate field; POST /deliverables/produce with a brief asking for full Quran Arabic, a translation and a fatwa -> 200. The QEP route withholds even the floor frame for the same subject, so the gate is per-route. Tier 2 not 1: what came back is a labelled term-frame, no Arabic, no ruling. Not 3: neither response says the scholar gate was not applied. The model-served consequence is source-read only. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Call screen_subject at the shared composition floor (or in every education and deliverable handler) and refuse/refer as curriculum does; add an untouched-caller guard.

items.title: The Synthesis Studio registers an 'active' enterprise for a casino, alcohol and 40% payday-loan challenge and its completion event never mentions that the §11 screen failed it — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R1), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11: compliance engines are integrated into every synthesis/generative/operational workflow, not bolted on. OBSERVED: POST /studio/synthesise ran 9 stages with no screen event in the stream (0 occurrences of 'screen', 'sharia' or 'quality_assurance' in 30 KB of SSE; the only 'compliance' strings are floor section headings). The entity was written to the store and the living roster as active with a Waqf-Ltd waterfall. /compliance/check on a near-identical subject returns overall 'fail'. No frontend file references /api/v1/studio/synthesise, so this was assessed as an API surface (response and stored record). EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/studio/synthesise {challenge:'An online casino with alcohol delivery and payday loans at 40% interest'} -> 200 text/event-stream, final frame done/entity_id vsb-77cfdceb. GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-77cfdceb -> status 'active', status_basis 'active as a record; every stage is a floor scaffold', first_screen {'overall':'fail','regression':False}. apps/.../ComplianceChecker.tsx itself states 'the Synthesis studio does not call this screen at all'. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly and elsewhere: the Compliance page says the Synthesis studio does not call the screen; the studio's own response does not, and the record's status stays 'active' beside a failed first screen.. WHY THIS TIER: The stream ends with {"stage":"done", "entity_id":"vsb-77cfdceb", "stages_completed":9} and the stored record reads status 'active'. The failure exists only as first_screen {overall:'fail'} deep in the record. Not tier 1: nothing states the subject is compliant. Not tier 3: the response a caller receives does not say the screen failed or that nothing was blocked, while Genesis vetoes the same class of subject. REFUTER: Reproduced from the stored record and the handler source (I did not re-run the stream, to avoid writing another entity). GET /vsb/vsb-77cfdceb shows status 'active', status_basis about floor scaffolds only, and first_screen overall 'fail'. synthesis_studio.py line 378 emits the done frame with synthesis_id, entity_id, solution_name, duration_ms, stages_completed and no screen field; the handler never yields a screen event and sets status 'active' unconditionally (line ~326). No frontend file references /api/v1/studio/synthesise. Tier 2: nothing asserts compliance (not 1), and the caller's response omits the failed screen (not 3). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Emit the first_screen verdict in the done frame and set status to a held/blocked value on fail, as Genesis does with its veto.

items.title: Genesis headings say each stage was 'tested & validated' and that 'candidates [were] modelled' over a payload that records neither — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R1), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §10 as amended: tested · validated are named with NO instrument and are not reported as met; modelled is WITHHELD on identical candidates with the reason rather than attested. OBSERVED: GenesisJourney.tsx line 796 renders the static title; line 853 renders stage_5_model_simulate_rank.method verbatim. agentic_core/api/genesis.py line 572 builds the method string beginning 'candidates modelled;' unconditionally on the floor branch. With a model serving, the chips under the same title would read '✓ concept · 86%' from coverage/specificity/structure proxies, which the title would then call tested & validated (read from source, not executed). EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/genesis/journey -> method 'candidates modelled; forward-simulation NOT run ...'; candidates_distinct 1; candidates_are_alternatives false; bar_measured summary '0 measured · 1 attested · 2 screen-only · 13 not measured (of 16)'; stages_verified '0/0'; stages_floor_served 6. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The body of both cards discloses the truth (amber note that all 3 candidates were identical; 'not assessable' chips). The title and the first clause of the method line are the untrue parts.. WHY THIS TIER: The card title a reader is shown is 'Stage verification — each stage tested & validated (§5)' and the §4.5 method line opens 'candidates modelled;'. The same response records stages_verified '0/0', every stage verified:null, and bar_measured.modelled = 'not attested: candidates_distinct=1 of 3 — one text modelled 3 times is not 3 candidates modelled'; tested and validated are 'not measured by this gate' and §10 says no instrument exists for either. These are assertions of an outcome the platform did not produce, not omissions, so tier 1 rather than 2; the chips beneath contradict the title ('— n/a', '6 floor-served, not assessable'), which limits how far a reader is misled but does not make the title true. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution and source. GenesisJourney.tsx line 796 renders the static title 'Stage verification — each stage tested & validated (§5)'; genesis.py line ~572 opens the method 'candidates modelled;' on the floor branch. My own POST /genesis/journey returned that method string, candidates_distinct 1, candidates_are_alternatives false, stages_verified '0/0', stages_floor_served 6, and bar_measured with modelled 'not attested: candidates_distinct=1 of 3', tested/validated 'not measured by this gate'. (My run gave '0 measured · 0 attested · 2 screen-only · 14 not measured' because I passed no domain; the assessor's '1 attested' is the categorised criterion.) The title and first clause assert outcomes the same payload denies: an assertion, so tier 1 rather than 2, though the card body contradicts it. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Retitle the card 'Stage checks — coverage/structure proxies (§5)' and make the method string say 'one text returned for all N candidates' when candidates_distinct is 1.

items.title: The scholar-review pipeline has a withholding half and no reachable reviewing half: no route or screen lets anyone join the roster, read the queue or approve — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R1), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: A.12.3: draft → in review → approved by a NAMED reviewer → published, enforced as a pipeline gate. OBSERVED: The gate withholds correctly and queues items (by_state in_review 2 after my calls). Nothing can move an item out of in_review through the product. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/scholar_review.py defines roster/add_scholar/submit/decide/published_body/gate_status and no APIRouter. POST /api/v1/qep/curriculum -> gate {scholars_on_roster:0, items:2, by_state:{in_review:2, approved:0}}. LearnTeachModule.tsx lines 185-192. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The empty roster is disclosed prominently. The absence of any reviewer-facing route or screen is not.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is told 'A scholar registry now exists: a roster, an approval bound to the exact text it approved ... nothing can be approved until the Owner engages a reviewer'. That sentence is true of the code, and it leaves the reader believing engagement is the only missing step. In the running product add_scholar(), decide() and the queue are Python functions with no HTTP route (no path containing 'scholar' or 'review' for them in the 528-path OpenAPI) and no UI, so even an engaged scholar could approve nothing. An omission rather than a false statement, so not tier 1; not stated at the surface, so not tier 3. REFUTER: Reproduced. scholar_review.py has no APIRouter; add_scholar() has no caller anywhere outside its own definition (grep of agentic_core and scripts); the 528-path OpenAPI has no scholar/roster/queue path. decide() is called only by QEPAuthoringReactor (reactor factory), which no UI drives and which would deny on the empty roster anyway. POST /qep/curriculum showed in_review growing (6 now) with approved 0. LearnTeachModule line 186-188 tells the reader the registry exists and is empty, and does not say no route or screen can fill it or approve. An unstated shortfall, not a false sentence: tier 2, not 1; not 3 because the missing reviewing half is not disclosed. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Either add Owner-only roster and review routes, or add one sentence: 'no reviewer screen or route exists yet; approval is not possible through the product'.

items.title: The Genesis page's three 'Open the ...' buttons open the generated Web app and Phone app as blank pages and the Website unstyled with dead links — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R2), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §13: the Website is a real multi-page static site, the Web app a real client-side interactive app, the Phone app a real installable PWA; the platform generates, version-controls and serves them. OBSERVED: GenesisJourney.tsx lines 1194/1223/1254 call openExport(preview). lib/download.ts openExport fetches the HTML and window.open()s a blob: object URL. A blob: URL cannot be a base for relative URLs, so <script src="app.js">, <link href="styles.css">, fetch('data.json'), manifest.webmanifest and sw.js never load. This is the only place in the UI that previews the three surfaces (the Cockpit's fetch list has only repo, repo/file, repo/zip, repo/ship). EVIDENCE: Executed in the Browser pane on http://127.0.0.1:8031: fetched each /api/v1/vsb/vsb-90de68f898/{webapp,mobile,website}/page/index, wrapped it in a Blob exactly as openExport does, loaded it in an iframe. Result: webapp #app children = 0, body text only 'Website · Phone app', 0 stylesheets; mobile #app children = 0, 0 stylesheets; website 0 stylesheets. Node: new URL('app.js','blob:http://127.0.0.1:8031/x') throws 'Invalid URL'. Loaded directly by URL the same web app renders 3 children and its template note. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown a card reading 'Web app · client_web_app' with an 'interactive' chip and a button 'Open the web app →' (likewise 'installable' / 'offline' and 'Open the phone app →', and 'Open the live site →'). Clicking yields an empty page and nothing on the card or the opened tab says the preview is broken. It is not tier 3 because no surface states the shortfall; I did not put it at tier 1 because the chips are true of the files written - what is hidden is that this button cannot show them. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. lib/download.ts openExport fetches the page and window.open()s a blob: URL; GenesisJourney.tsx 1194/1223/1254 use it for all three previews and none of the served index pages carries a <base>. In the Browser pane I wrapped each served index in a Blob and loaded it in an iframe: webapp #app children 0, 0 stylesheets, text only 'Website · Phone app'; mobile #app children 0, 0 stylesheets; website 0 stylesheets. Loaded directly the mobile app renders 3 children. Tier 2 not 1: the card's words ('interactive', 'Open the web app') are true of the files; nothing false is asserted, the button just cannot show them. Not 3: nothing on the card or the opened tab says the preview is broken (the catch only reports a failed fetch). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Open the preview by its real URL (or serve a single self-contained document with assets inlined) so relative assets resolve; until then label the button as a raw-HTML view.

items.title: The Phone app card says 'installable' and 'offline' with no condition, while at the only address the platform serves it the app shell is never cached and the start URL is a 404 — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R2), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §13: the Phone app is a real installable PWA (offline-capable when hosted) - never a fabricated native binary; the platform does not host or deploy them. OBSERVED: sw.js pre-caches './' and 'index.html'; under the platform's page route both 404, so the shell is not cached and the offline fallback caches.match('index.html') is empty. manifest start_url './' resolves to /mobile/page/ which is 404. EVIDENCE: Browser pane at /api/v1/vsb/vsb-90de68f898/mobile/page/index: service worker registered and active; cache 'vsb-pwa-v1' holds app.js, styles.css, data.json, manifest.webmanifest only (no index). GET .../mobile/page/ = 404, .../mobile/page/index.html = 404. GenesisJourney.tsx 1240-1253 renders kind, the two chips and features; no reference to pwa.note. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: In the API body (note) yes; on the Genesis card no. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown two unconditional chips, 'installable' and 'offline' (from installable:true / offline_capable:true). The API's own note qualifies this ('Installable + offline-capable when hosted ... not deployed/hosted') but GenesisJourney.tsx never renders pwa.note, so the qualifier that would make it tier 3 does not reach the user. Not tier 1 because the files are a genuine manifest + service worker that would work from a static host; the shortfall is the dropped condition. REFUTER: Reproduced in the Browser pane: service worker active with scope .../mobile/page/, cache 'vsb-pwa-v1' holds app.js, styles.css, data.json, manifest.webmanifest and NO index; /mobile/page/ and /mobile/page/index.html are 404, so sw.js's './' and 'index.html' pre-cache entries fail and the offline fallback caches.match('index.html') is empty; manifest start_url './' is a 404. GenesisJourney.tsx 1241-1253 renders the 'installable' and 'offline' chips and features.join (which includes 'offline (service worker cache)') and never renders pwa.note, the only place the 'when hosted' condition lives. Tier 2 rather than 1: the vision's own ratified scope is 'offline-capable when hosted' and the files are a genuine manifest + service worker, so the chip describes the artefact truthfully with its condition dropped. Not 3: the condition does not reach the card. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Render the manifest's note beside the chips ('when hosted; not hosted here'), or word the chips 'installable when hosted'.

VISION CLAIM: §13: the canonical output is bespoke to the concept→commercialisation solution and integrates a Website, a Web app and a Phone app. OBSERVED: webapp/app.js and mobile/app.js are byte-identical (cmp), as are the two data.json files: the 'Web app' and the 'Phone app' are one 4-tab viewer of the entity record. 'runs directly in a browser — no build' additionally does not hold for a double-clicked copy from the zip, because app.js does fetch('data.json') which Chromium blocks on file:// (reasoned from source, not executed). EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-90de68f898/webapp and /mobile -> note fields quoted above; zip contents: webapp/app.json, mobile/app.json, webapp/data.json template_note; cmp webapp/app.js mobile/app.js -> identical; cmp data.json -> identical. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Contradicted, not disclosed: the app's Overview tab carries the true statement, the manifest the false one. WHY THIS TIER: The stored record and route body state: 'Bespoke client-side interactive web app (... data-driven from the entity, runs directly in a browser — no build)' and 'Bespoke installable PWA'. The same repository's data.json says: 'This app is the platform's standard template ... the same app for every entity. It does not deliver the solution itself.' One of the two sentences is untrue and it is the manifest's - an assertion in the record, not an omission, so tier 1 rather than 2. The in-app note keeps the severity moderate. REFUTER: The gap is reproduced; the VERDICT is wrong. STUB means a surface that pretends, and this surface does not: the app's own first screen says it is the standard template. items.title: The Board Pack carries an emerald 'DCS-registered' chip, but the registered hash does not cover the pack — two packs with different content share one DCS hash — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R3), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.3: 'Board Pack (on-demand): assembled fresh from live data, DCS-registered.' OBSERVED: Pack v1 (content_hash 6b0ece4d…) and pack v2 (content_hash 282ab00d…, after the cadence filled the strategic and action-plan layers) both report dcs_registered: true with the SAME dcs_hash 0f1818e3ba1e7a14…. The 'DCS hash' is the quality record hash of the narrative text only (agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1742-1743 takes it from qa.quality.quality_record_hash; vbs/quality.py:469 seals the QA record over the narrative's content_sha3). The layers, economy and entity verdict that make up the pack are not in the controlled document. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/vsb/{vsb_id}/board-pack three times on vsb-d121609493 and GET /api/v1/vsb/{vsb_id}/board-packs: versions 1 and 2 list different content_hash and identical dcs_hash. GenesisJourney.tsx:1304 renders 'DCS-registered' in emerald with the hash as its title; the pack's own note reads 'on-demand Board Pack, assembled fresh from live data, DCS-registered.' DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader sees 'DCS-registered' on the pack and a hash offered as its registration. The hash stays the same when the pack's content changes, so the document control system does not hold this pack. The surface certifies a registration that does not cover what it is attached to — tier 1, not tier 2, because the chip is a positive claim. REFUTER: Reproduced, and it is wider than the assessor reported. GET /api/v1/vsb/{id}/board-packs on vsb-d121609493 shows version 1 (content_hash 6b0ece4d…) and version 2 (282ab00d…) both with dcs_hash 0f1818e3ba1e7a14…. I then established a different entity (vsb-6356e12f01) and its first pack (content_hash 1057f716…) carries the SAME dcs_hash 0f1818e3…. So one hash is offered as the registration of different packs of different entities. vsb.py:1742-1743 takes it from the QA record of the narrative text, which on the floor is the same 'narrative pending' text everywhere. GenesisJourney.tsx:1304 renders an emerald 'DCS-registered' chip with that hash as its title, and the pack note says 'DCS-registered'. A positive certification that does not cover what it is attached to: tier 1, not 2. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Register the pack itself (qms.control_document over layers + economy + narrative, keyed by vsb and version) and report that hash; or relabel the chip 'narrative quality record sealed' and say the pack's layers are versioned by content_hash only.

items.title: A review gate left pending can only be decided on the Genesis page in the session that established the entity — after a reload no screen can approve it, and the entity stays held — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.4 Mode 3: 'optional human review gates at any Concept→Commercialisation stage (set in the VSB genome) … a Human review gates (Mode 3) panel on the Genesis page.' §17.3: 'an Assemble Board Pack action on the Genesis page surfaces it.' OBSERVED: The gating itself works (see the DELIVERED finding). But '/review-gates' and '/board-pack' are called only from GenesisJourney.tsx (lines 461-497), which holds the entity in component state set solely by an establish response (setVsb at 233/283/391/403; nothing loads an existing entity from the URL). VSBCockpit.tsx has no gate or pack control; on a refusal it prints '<error> — gate 'design' is <status>' (line 340-342) and drops the response's clear_by instruction. The UI also never sends review_gates at establishment, so 'gates can be set at birth' is API-only. EVIDENCE: grep of apps/workstation-superapp/src for 'review-gates' and 'vsb/.*/board-pack': GenesisJourney.tsx only. Executed: POST /api/v1/genesis/establish with review_gates ['design'] -> status 'held'; POST /api/v1/vsb/{id}/repo/ship, /evolve, /board-pack and POST /api/v1/swarm/cascade all 409 with clear_by naming an API call. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The refusal names the gate but not that the only control lives on a page that cannot reopen this entity.. WHY THIS TIER: The Cockpit tells the founder the gate is pending, which is true, but never says there is no screen on which to decide it once the Genesis session is gone. The entity is blocked and the shortfall is unstated, so tier 2; nothing false is asserted, so not tier 1. REFUTER: Reproduced from source (no browser driven). 'review-gates' and 'vsb/…/board-pack' are fetched only in GenesisJourney.tsx:461-497. Its vsb state is set only from an establish or name response (lines 233, 283, 391, 403); useSearchParams reads seed/problem/domain/realm/product only, so nothing reloads an existing entity. No frontend file sends review_gates at establishment. VSBCockpit.tsx:341-342 prints the error, gate and status and drops clear_by. By execution: an entity established with review_gates ['design'] is 'held', and evolve, ship and board-pack return 409. The Cockpit's refusal is true but nothing says no screen can decide the gate once the Genesis session is gone. Nothing false is asserted (not tier 1); the block is real and unstated (not tier 3). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Render the same gates panel and the Assemble Board Pack action on the VSB Cockpit for the selected entity (the routes already take vsb_id).

items.title: The Board Pack's strategic layer shows a superseded derived sentence and omits the Strategy the Owner wrote, while reporting the pack unchanged — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.3: the Board Pack is 'assembled fresh from live data'; Strategic layer = 'position, growth, resource posture'. OBSERVED: I wrote a Strategy and a Concept on the entity's plan (POST /api/v1/business-plan/set; owner_edits stamped, field_sources 'owner_supplied'). The next pack's strategic layer still read '[as of 2026-10-10 12:42 UTC] Strategic position derived from the plan itself: 0 aim(s) and 3 objective(s) on the roadmap…' — the plan then held 5 objectives and an Owner-written strategy, which appears nowhere in the pack. The pack stayed 'version 2' with the same content_hash, i.e. it reported itself unchanged across the Owner's edit. Cause: the layer is built from cadence.latest() (last APPLIED refresh, organism/cadence.py:172-176), and once the Owner edits the field the cadence only proposes, so the layer is frozen on the pre-edit text. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/business-plan/set (strategy, concept) -> 200; POST /api/v1/organism/cadence/refresh?layer=strategic&force=true -> refreshed false, proposed true; POST /api/v1/vsb/{vsb_id}/board-pack -> version 2, content_hash 282ab00d…, strategic.content as quoted, refresh_at 12:42:36Z. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the refresh id and time are shown; that the Owner's own strategy exists and is not in the pack is not.. WHY THIS TIER: The layer carries its own as-of stamp and names the refresh it came from, so the sentence is dated rather than false — not tier 1. But nothing tells the reader that the plan's current strategy is different and Owner-written, and 'assembled fresh' plus 'unchanged' suggest the opposite — an invisible shortfall, tier 2. REFUTER: Reproduced. The plan for vsb-d121609493 holds an Owner-written strategy ('Start with one venue and two volunteer tutors…', owner_edits stamped 12:46:49Z) and 5+ objectives. The latest pack's strategic layer still reads '[as of 2026-10-10 12:42 UTC] … 0 aim(s) and 3 objective(s)', version 2, unchanged true. The Owner's strategy text appears nowhere in the pack body (searched for it: 0 matches). A forced strategic refresh returned refreshed false and left the Owner text in place, so the pack layer stays frozen on the pre-edit refresh (cadence.latest takes applied rows only). The sentence carries its as-of stamp and refresh id, so it is dated rather than false (not tier 1); nothing says a newer Owner-written strategy exists and is left out (not tier 3). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: When owner_edits.strategy is set, assemble the strategic layer from the plan's strategy field (source: Owner-written) and include plan strategy/concept in the pack content hash.

items.title: The Chief's unprompted directive re-files the Owner's last instruction as a second identical objective, and the record calls that 'executed' — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5: the Chief delivers 'the founder's role and responsibilities autonomously in the founder's presence and absence'. OBSERVED: With auto_align on, a heartbeat beat issued dir-e6122ed9 (kind twin_directive_unprompted) restating my instruction. The workstation plan now holds TWO identical objectives 'Launch a halal-certified tutoring service…' (obj-4defec81 from dir-daf0c6b2, obj-f15a784d from dir-e6122ed9), both source chief_instruct_fallback, objective_count 2. The stored record says "executed": true, "cascaded_to_ceo": true beside "filed_as_fallback": true; executed is bool(objectives_added) (board.py:577), so filing a duplicate counts as execution. The trigger is a change in the Owner's input COUNT, so a ratification of an unrelated change also re-files the last instruction. On the Board page the row renders as a card with the kind badge and an EMPTY title (BoardOfDirectors.tsx:387 reads d.topic ?? d.instruction; the row has acted_on) and no basis; HeartbeatMonitor.tsx does not render last_twin_directive. On the plan page the two objectives are indistinguishable apart from the directive id. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/board/status (recent_directives), GET /api/v1/business-plan/roadmap?scope=workstation (two identical objectives), GET /api/v1/heartbeat/status (last_twin_directive). agentic_core/api/board.py:501-604; agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:661-683 (apex scope only). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: In the API record's basis only; not on the plan page, the Board page or the Heartbeat page.. WHY THIS TIER: The record's basis sentence does say the instruction was 'filed as ONE fallback objective … not a plan the AI CEO produced', so the body is not flatly false — I hold it at tier 2 rather than 1. But the plan page shows a second objective with nothing saying it is the twin's restatement, and the Board page shows a blank card: the shortfall is invisible where a person meets it. REFUTER: Reproduced from stored state. GET /api/v1/business-plan?scope=workstation shows two identical open objectives 'Launch a halal-certified tutoring service…' (obj-4defec81, obj-f15a784d), both source chief_instruct_fallback. GET /api/v1/board/status shows the twin_directive_unprompted row dir-e6122ed9 with executed true, cascaded_to_ceo true, filed_as_fallback true, and a basis saying it was filed as one fallback objective. That row has acted_on but no topic or instruction, and BoardOfDirectors.tsx:387 renders d.topic ?? d.instruction, so its title is blank. board.py:577 sets executed = bool(objectives_added). The record's own basis states the fallback, so the body is not flatly false (not tier 1). The duplicate on the plan and the blank card are unmarked where a person meets them (not tier 3). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Do not add an objective when an identical open one from the same instruction exists; set executed from objectives_parsed, not objectives_added; render acted_on and basis on the Board card.

items.title: A VSB's Chief is prompted with every scope's instructions, not that entity's own — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5/§17.4: each Chief is the twin of THAT founder, 'modelled … specifically for the founder's instructions and input data'; §17.5 user isolation. OBSERVED: GET /api/v1/board/chief/model?scope=<vsb> correctly counts only that scope's instructions (1). But the prompt builder founder_profile() calls founder_model() with no scope and no owner (board.py:316), and chief_instruct embeds it for every scope (board.py:752). So an instruction written for the workstation apex or another entity is handed to this entity's Chief as 'The Owner's recent instructions (remember them; stay consistent)'. With auth on, the same unscoped read would cross owners. Not observable in output here because the floor does not interpret the prompt. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/board.py:229-303, 306-331, 745-760; executed GET /api/v1/board/chief/model with and without scope (counts 1 vs 3). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The Cockpit says 'Instruct this entity's Chief' and the model surface reports a scoped record, while the prompt actually carries all scopes. Nothing displayed is false on this environment (no model read the prompt), so not tier 1; the mismatch is invisible, so tier 2. REFUTER: Reproduced from code and counts. founder_profile() (board.py:306-316) calls founder_model() with no scope or owner, and chief_instruct embeds founder_profile() in the prompt for every scope (board.py:745-752). GET /api/v1/board/chief/model?scope=vsb-d121609493 counts 2 instructions; unscoped counts 4. So a VSB Chief's prompt carries other scopes' instructions while the scoped model surface reports only its own. Not observable in output here because the floor does not interpret the prompt, so nothing displayed is untrue (not tier 1). The mismatch is stated nowhere (not tier 3). The cross-owner consequence with auth on was not executed by me or the assessor. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Pass scope (and owner) through founder_profile(scope, owner) at every call site in board.py, business_plan.py and swarm.py.

items.title: The swarm roster offers a 'Religious Affairs Advisor — Islamic jurisprudence' agent that accepts a request for a ruling with no §11 refusal — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3)

On this environment the floor returned a term-count frame, so no ruling was produced — and no refusal either. The Agent Hub tab lists the role under 'Platform roster (swarm, live)' with that expertise as its tooltip. I could not observe a served model's answer (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: I am not reporting the boundary as missing — the boundary is ratified. The gap is that this door does not refuse and does not say it will not rule. What I saw returned was a labelled floor frame, not a ruling, so nothing untrue was told (not tier 1); the unenforced boundary is invisible (tier 2). REFUTER: Reproduced. The boundary itself is ratified and is not reported as missing; the gap is that this door does not refuse. What came back was a labelled term-count frame, not a ruling, so nothing untrue was told (not tier 1). The unenforced boundary is invisible (not tier 3). What a served model would return was not observable. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Run the existing constitutional screen on the delegate and cascade task text and return its refusal; rename the role's expertise so it does not advertise jurisprudence.

items.title: A 'human review' gate decision records no reviewer, and its DCS entry names the author with the fixed label 'human-reviewer' — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R3), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.4 Mode 3: human review gates; 'each config + decision append-only DCS-audited (§17.5)'. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/vsb/{vsb_id}/review-gates/{stage}/decision with reviewer and notes fields returned decision {decision:'approve', note:'', at:…}: the reviewer was dropped silently (GateDecisionRequest is not strict) and no principal is stamped even though the handler receives `user`. The DCS document is written with actor literal 'human-reviewer' (vsb.py:2243). Any caller, including an automated one, clears a gate and is recorded as a human reviewer. EVIDENCE: Executed the decision route; agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2227-2247. Auth-on behaviour not executed. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The decision record's blank reviewer is an omission (not tier 1). The DCS actor label is a fixed word rather than an identity, and nothing says the gate does not know who decided — an unstated shortfall, tier 2. REFUTER: Reproduced. POST /api/v1/vsb/{vsb_id}/review-gates/{stage}/decision with a reviewer field returned a decision of {decision, note, at} only. GateDecisionRequest (vsb.py:2169-2171) has no reviewer field and is not strict, so the field is dropped silently. The handler receives `user` but stamps no principal, and the DCS document is written with the literal actor 'human-reviewer' (vsb.py:2243). The CCA ratification route, by contrast, records by 'single-user-mode' and by_verified false. The blank reviewer is an omission. The fixed actor label is a role name on a stored record rather than an identity claim shown to a user, so I hold tier 2 rather than 1, though it is close to 'certifies what it could not assess'. Nothing discloses that the gate does not know who decided, so not tier 3. items.title: The Resource Fabric presents the composed Digital Twin as a simulator that ran, while its own run row says no simulator or engine ran — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R4), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §7: 'every composed resource runs its REAL engine' (corrected W652: the composed twin stage does not, and 'the product's run row says so'); §15.6 label simulation. OBSERVED: Four reached statements say the twin simulates/ran; one row field and a tooltip say it did not. (a) Catalogue card (ResourceFabric.tsx:432 renders r.description): 'Forward-simulates a system under a scenario on the native swarm (state trajectory · emergent behaviour · stress points · setpoints) — the §7 Simulator facility', endpoint /api/v1/twin/simulate. (b) GET /resources/cell/availability: digital_twin state 'available', with basis "'available' means the fabric can run the resource's engine". (c) POST /resources/compose/simulate with digital_twin returns engines_not_run_by_fabric: [] whose basis reads 'a resource listed here contributes a prompt stage and its engine is not run' - the twin is not listed, so the preview shows no 'Engine not run by the fabric' warning. (d) On the run card, outcome 'narrated' matches none of the UI branches (read/assessed/specified/raised/no_calls_ran) and falls to the default green chip 'RAN'; the heading counts only produced/read/specified/failed, so my 4-resource run reads '4 composed resource(s) invoked · 2 ran an engine · 1 read existing state · 0 drafted a blueprint · 0 failed' - the twin is in no bucket. The truth is present only as the chip's hover title and in the row output's floor banner: 'wrote a scenario narrative from a persona prompt — no simulator or engine ran, nothing was computed'; 'invoked: orchestrator.complete with a simulator persona - /api/v1/twin/simulate was NOT called'. UI behaviour reasoned from source, not driven. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/resources/compose/simulate + /compose + /compositions/comp-c900d92a/run (run cr-653f4ed7); GET /api/v1/resources/digital_twin; GET /api/v1/resources/cell/availability; GET /api/v1/resources/cell/contract/digital_twin (says 'no simulator or engine runs' but no UI file reads the contract route); agentic_core/api/resource_fabric.py:169, 1040-1056, 1149, 2029-2045; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/synthesis/ResourceFabric.tsx:432, 571-581, 789-831 (no 'narrat' anywhere in the file). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly - only in the row's hover tooltip, the floor banner inside the row output, and an API contract route no page calls.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader is shown a green 'RAN' chip and the sentence 'Forward-simulates a system under a scenario' for a stage where nothing was simulated; those are assertions, not omissions, so tier 1 rather than 2. It is not tier 3 because the disclosure lives in a hover title and a field the UI does not surface as text. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution and source. GET /resources/digital_twin returns the description 'Forward-simulates a system under a scenario on the native swarm ... the §7 Simulator facility' with endpoint /api/v1/twin/simulate; ResourceFabric.tsx:432 renders it. My own run (comp-42b244f2 / cr-c47036d9) returned the twin row with outcome 'narrated', outcome_phrase 'no simulator or engine ran, nothing was computed' and invoked '/api/v1/twin/simulate was NOT called'. ResourceFabric.tsx:815-828 has no branch for 'narrated', so it falls to the emerald 'ran' chip, with the truthful phrase only as the hover title; the heading at 796-797 counts produced/read/specified/failed only, so the twin sits in no bucket. compose/simulate returned engines_not_run_by_fabric [] for a design containing the twin. Tier 1 rather than 2 because the card sentence and the 'ran' chip are assertions, not blanks. Not tier 3 because the correction is in a tooltip and in floor-banner text that only exists because the floor served. Caveat: 'ran' is literally true of a prompt call and the heading does not count it as 'ran an engine', so the chip alone is borderline; the catalogue sentence carries the tier. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Add a 'narrated' branch to the run-card chip and heading count; list _NARRATIVE_RESOURCES in engines_not_run_by_fabric (or a sibling field); reword the digital_twin registry description to what the contract already says.

items.title: The Model Ensemble headline counts the deterministic floor twice as '2 of 2 owned models produced output … consensus synthesised' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R4), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §6 own models + orchestration; §15.6 never fabricate. Capability text: 'Run a prompt across MULTIPLE owned models in parallel, then synthesise a consensus'. OBSERVED: POST /native-ai/ensemble with models ['native','ollama:llama3.2'] returned two members both served_by 'native' (the ollama member carries no 'skipped' note, unlike /complete's resources_tried) and method 'parallel ensemble across 2 owned model(s) → consensus synthesis'. NativeAI.tsx:849-861 renders 'Ensemble · 2 of 2 owned models produced output · run in parallel → consensus synthesised' because it counts members without an error key. No model ran: /native-ai/status on the same page says the floor is 'NOT an LLM'; one deterministic engine produced the same scaffold twice and a third scaffold was labelled Consensus. The per-member chips ('ollama:llama3.2 · native') and 'synthesised by native' do show the server. UI reasoned from source. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/native-ai/ensemble (executed); agentic_core/ai/native/orchestrator.py:347-352; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/developers/NativeAI.tsx:840-876. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly - member chips show 'native', the headline and method string do not.. WHY THIS TIER: The figure '2 of 2 owned models produced output' and the API's 'across 2 owned model(s)' assert a count of models that is untrue (zero models, one floor) - a fabricated figure on a reached page, so tier 1. The adjacent served-by chips mitigate but do not retract the headline; a reader of the headline alone is told an ensemble consensus happened. REFUTER: Reproduced. POST /native-ai/ensemble with ['native','ollama:llama3.2'] returned models_run ['native','ollama:llama3.2'], two members both served_by native with identical scaffolds, and method 'parallel ensemble across 2 owned model(s) → consensus synthesis'. Tier 1 because '2 of 2 owned models' and models_run are counts and names of things that did not run. Not tier 2: the per-member '· native' chip mitigates but does not retract the headline figure. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Count distinct non-floor servers in the label and method; when every member is floor-served say so and withhold 'consensus'; carry resources_tried on each member.

items.title: Two reached surfaces disagree about the Respiratory and Endocrine layers: every run's quality record says they cannot run, while the Agent Hub is labelled 'Respiratory layer' and the signal bus runs — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R4), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.2 realisation map: Respiratory → the Agent Hub + org cascade (real bus, records only); Endocrine → the biomimetic signal bus + shared context (organism/biobus.py) — REAL as the bus. OBSERVED: The biomimetic block attached to every composition run and org-cascade run (and persisted with them) says: 'CODE EXISTS BUT CANNOT BE IMPORTED — so the layer could not run even if something called it: Respiratory' (basis: molecular/triad_integration.py) and 'CODE EXISTS BUT NOTHING CALLS IT — so the layer does not run anywhere: Endocrine' (basis: geospheric/regulator.py). The same build serves a page headed 'Respiratory layer · Agent Hub' (AgentHubPanel.tsx:130), and biobus is imported by 10+ live modules and fired during the very requests that carry the record (GET /organism/nervous/signals showed the signals). The same record also calls Musculoskeletal 'composable facilities that run real engines' without the twin exception. The record and the vision map name different modules for the same layer; one of the two statements a user reads is wrong. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/resources/compositions/{cid}/run and POST /api/v1/swarm/cascade (quality_assurance.biomimetic.layers_note / layer_basis); agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:37-79; apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/organism/AgentHubPanel.tsx:130; apps/workstation-superapp/src/lib/api.ts:322-343 (tooltip 'code exists but nothing calls it: Endocrine'); grep of biobus imports. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No - neither surface mentions the other mapping.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader is told in a flat sentence 'the layer does not run anywhere: Endocrine' on a durable record while the module the canon maps to that layer ran in that request - an untrue statement under the vision's own map, hence tier 1 not 2. I rank it below the two above because it under-claims rather than certifies; if the Owner rules the quality record's mapping is the correct one, the untruth moves to the Agent Hub label and the vision map instead. REFUTER: Reproduced. My composition run's quality_assurance.biomimetic.layers_note reads 'CODE EXISTS BUT NOTHING CALLS IT — so the layer does not run anywhere: Endocrine. CODE EXISTS BUT CANNOT BE IMPORTED — so the layer could not run even if something called it: Respiratory', and its Musculoskeletal basis says 'composable facilities that run real engines' with no twin exception. AgentHubPanel.tsx:130 heads a live page 'Respiratory layer · Agent Hub'. Vision lines 843-848 map Respiratory to the Agent Hub and Endocrine to organism/biobus.py, which 20+ live modules import. The two reached statements cannot both be true. Tier 1 because the record makes a flat universal ('does not run anywhere') that is false under the canon's own mapping and is persisted with every run. It is the weakest of the three tier-1s: layer_basis on the same record names the module it means, so a careful reader can see it is a mapping disagreement. I did not drop it to tier 2 because a contradiction between two assertions is not an unstated shortfall. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: One layer→module table read by quality.py, the Agent Hub heading and the vision map; state per layer which module is meant.

items.title: The Digital Twin's own routes are persona prompts that return and store no provenance, and no page can run them — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R4), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. The response keys are simulation_id, result, parameters, time_horizon - no served_by, no is_external, no statement that the result is a narrative; the stored simulation row drops the result and keeps no server either. Under the floor the banner inside `result` discloses it; with a served model the metric table would be model-written with no label anywhere on the response or record. DigitalTwins.tsx only calls GET /twin/models and /twin/models/{id} - model/simulate/optimise have no UI caller. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/twin/model, POST /api/v1/twin/simulate, GET /api/v1/twin/models (executed); agentic_core/api/digital_twin.py:144-197; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/developers/DigitalTwins.tsx:33-59. It is an omission rather than a false field, and the floor text carries its own banner here, so not tier 1. REFUTER: Reproduced from the handler; I reached the route only as a 422 on my first body and did not complete a simulate call. digital_twin.py:143-196 builds one persona prompt ('You are a simulation engineer... Run the simulation and provide... Key Metrics Over Time (table...)... Sensitivity Analysis'), makes one gateway.query_meta call, and returns simulation_id/model_id/scenario fields/result/run_at with no served_by or is_external; the stored row drops result and keeps no server. Not tier 1: that is an omission, and under the floor the result text carries its own banner. Not tier 3: the body does not state the shortfall. items.title: A Genesis journey records a realm that is not one of the four and attests 'categorised: met'; an unrecognised product is replaced by Reactor and stamped 'chosen by the caller' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R5), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.1: the grid is 4 Realms x 6 Domains x 4 Products; 'a Genesis journey takes and RECORDS a product, with an unrecognised value falling to the default rather than being stored as given'. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/genesis/journey with realm='cosmic', product='bogus' returned 200, status 'complete', realm echoed as 'cosmic', and quality bar row categorised = {met: true, attested: true, source: 'caller', basis: "caller evidence: realm 'cosmic' x domain 'science' categorisation, both chosen by the caller"}. The same response carries product 'reactor', product_label 'Reactor — rapid AI generation', product_source 'chosen by the caller' — the caller chose 'bogus'. Meanwhile the prompt was built with normalise_realm (genesis.py:328), i.e. 'Enterprise', so the record names a realm the run did not use. EVIDENCE: Executed twice (valid: scholarship/laboratory recorded correctly; invalid: cosmic/bogus as above). C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/api/genesis.py lines 223-234 (categorised attested from any sent value, no is_realm check), 850 ('realm': req.realm), 854-858 (product normalised but product_source still 'chosen by the caller'). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — nothing in the response says the realm was unrecognised or that the product was substituted.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader of the response body and the stored journey record is shown "categorised: met: true ... attested: true" over a realm that does not exist in the taxonomy, and "product_source: chosen by the caller" over a product the caller did not choose. Both are assertions of an outcome that did not happen, not omissions, so this is tier 1 rather than 2. It is not worse-ranked because the UI (GenesisJourney.tsx:204-206) only sends canonical values, so the reached form is the API body and stored record only. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /api/v1/genesis/journey with realm='cosmic', domain='science', product='bogus', establish=false returned 200, status 'complete', realm 'cosmic', product 'reactor', product_source 'chosen by the caller', and quality row categorised = {met:true, attested:true, source:'caller', basis:"caller evidence: realm 'cosmic' x domain 'science' categorisation, both chosen by the caller"}. Code agrees: genesis.py ~223-234 attests from field presence with no membership check; the return dict stores req.realm raw while the prompt uses normalise_realm; product_source is decided from model_fields_set, not from whether the sent value survived normalisation. Tier 1 rather than 2: these are affirmative statements (met:true/attested:true over a realm outside the four; 'chosen by the caller' over a value the caller did not send), not blanks. Not lower because the API body and stored journey record ARE the reached form for an API caller. The UI only sends canonical values, so no screen user hits it. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: In the journey handler, withhold 'categorised' when is_realm(req.realm) is false (reason: not a taxonomy realm), store the normalised realm beside the value given, and set product_source to 'defaulted — the value sent was not a product' when normalise_product changed it.

items.title: A journey that established nothing still carries the basis sentence 'an entity record was created and persisted' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R5), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §3A offering 2 / §15 principle 6: the lifecycle establishes a living VSB; never fabricate. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/genesis/journey with establish=false returned enterprise_established: false, established_vsb: null, enterprise_operating: null, and enterprise_established_basis: "an entity record was created and persisted; `enterprise_operating` says whether it is operating, from its derived status". The 'deliverable' field in the same body correctly says 'NO enterprise was established'. EVIDENCE: Executed (both journey calls). C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/api/genesis.py:933 — the basis is an unconditional literal emitted whatever the value of enterprise_established. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Contradicted elsewhere in the same body, not corrected at the field.. WHY THIS TIER: The sentence shown is "an entity record was created and persisted" beside a false flag — a basis string asserting an event that did not occur, which is an assertion and not a blank, hence tier 1 not 2. It is ranked low because no frontend file reads the field (grep of apps/workstation-superapp/src finds none) and the sibling 'deliverable' contradicts it honestly. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution: same journey (establish=false) returned enterprise_established false, established_vsb null, enterprise_operating null, and enterprise_established_basis 'an entity record was created and persisted; `enterprise_operating` says whether it is operating, from its derived status'. genesis.py ~933 emits that literal unconditionally. Tier 1 rather than 2: the sentence is a past-tense assertion of an event that did not happen, not an omission. It is the weakest tier-1 in the set: the flag beside it is false and 'deliverable' says 'NO enterprise was established', so a careful reader is not misled, and no frontend file reads the field. I hold it at 1 because the tier turns on what the sentence says, and a basis that contradicts its own flag is an untrue statement in the response body; a reader who argued tier 2 on the ground that the adjacent fields correct it would not be unreasonable. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Make the basis a function of the value: when nothing was established say 'no entity record was created — establish was not requested'.

items.title: The Care risk tool offers four instruments that have no scoring and tells the user the narrative is 'an AI aid' when the floor composed it — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R5), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §3A offering 1: in-house AI-mediated care tools; §15 principle 6. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/care/risk-assess with tool dementia_care or safeguarding (also offered: mental_health, discharge) returns score = {available: false, note: 'no published arithmetic exists for this tool — the narrative below is an AI aid only, not a score', basis: 'computed in-house from the published table — a decision aid, not a diagnosis...'}. Nothing was computed, and the narrative is a floor frame whose own disclaimer says it is 'not an interpretation by AI or by a clinician'. CareHub renders score.note in amber for available=false, so the page shows 'an AI aid' and, a few lines down, 'not an interpretation by AI'. The narrative for every care risk call also reads 'the subject (not identified to this engine by the tool that called it)'. EVIDENCE: Executed risk-assess for news2, must, waterlow, dementia_care, safeguarding. Read apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/domains/CareHub.tsx:79-118 (select lists eight tools; line 82-83 renders the note). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly — floor note and disclaimer are correct; the note and score.basis are not.. WHY THIS TIER: The sentence shown is 'the narrative below is an AI aid only' while the amber floor note and the disclaimer on the same card say no AI interpreted anything. Because the floor is disclosed on the same surface the reader is not left believing a model ran, which keeps this out of tier 1; because the two statements contradict and the stored score.basis claims a computation that did not happen, the disclosure is not clean, so tier 2 rather than 3. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution, and I tier it HARSHER than the assessor (2 -> 1). POST /api/v1/care/risk-assess tool=dementia_care returned score {available:false, note:'no published arithmetic exists for this tool — the narrative below is an AI aid only, not a score', basis:'computed in-house from the published table — a decision aid, not a diagnosis…'}. The narrative is a floor frame and the disclaimer on the same response says 'NO SCORE WAS COMPUTED… not an interpretation by AI'. CareHub.tsx renders score.note in amber when available===false, so the screen prints 'an AI aid' for a narrative no model wrote; score.basis (stored and exported, not drawn) asserts a computation from a table the note says does not exist. Source of both literals: agentic_core/care/scoring.py lines 19 and 391. Why 1 and not 2: this is not the 'no model ran' environment case — the floor IS disclosed — it is an affirmative sentence saying AI produced the narrative and a basis saying a score was computed, both untrue, on a reached screen and in the stored record. I apply the same rule as index 1 (an untrue sentence stays untrue when a neighbouring field contradicts it). The counter-argument for tier 2 is that the disclaimer and amber floor note on the same card correct it. Also confirmed: with only patient_data the narrative reads 'the subject (not identified to this engine by the tool that called it)'; with clinical_context filled it does name the subject. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: For tools without arithmetic, set basis to 'no score exists for this tool' and make the note serving-aware ('a structured frame' on the floor); consider labelling those four options 'no score' in the select.

items.title: Starting a project from a domain hub opens a form whose Realm dropdown cannot show the value it holds, and touching it drops the domain — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R5)

VISION CLAIM: §17.1: realm and domain are separate axes of one grid; §3A: flow from a domain into building. OBSERVED: Reasoned from source (no browser driven). CreateForm puts that in state `realm` and renders a <select value={realm}> whose only options are the four canonical realms, so no option matches and the browser displays the first one ('Enterprise') while the form would post realm='care'. If the user picks any realm, state becomes that realm and the care/law domain is no longer sent at all. With no query string the default is 'technology', again not an option. The second dropdown labelled 'Domain' lists Product/SaaS/Research/Content/Service/Policy/Curriculum, not the six domains. GET /api/v1/projects/ returned 0 projects, so no stored example exists to count. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No (the project card later labels the stored field 'domain · area', ProjectsHub.tsx:367).. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown a field labelled 'Realm' displaying 'Enterprise' while the request would carry 'care'; nothing says the field doubles as the domain or that changing it discards the domain. No false result is certified (the backend labels realm_source), so not tier 1; the shortfall is not stated on the form, so not tier 3. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Carry the hub's domain in its own read-only field on the form and bind the Realm select to taxonomyRealm.

items.title: The Transformation picture marks 'One self-running, self-healing, self-improving organism' as 100% REALISED on three presence checks — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R6), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8: 'A quantity may carry the name of a law only when computed by that law (the naming invariant): API-surface coverage is not vision realisation.' §8 W512: the organism does not yet regulate, turn over or select. OBSERVED: GET /api/v1/transformation/realisation returns self_running {realisation: 1.0, status: 'realised'} with evidence 'Self-evolution live', 'An evolution cycle has run' (true because I ran one floor-served cycle minutes earlier), 'Continuous heartbeat (scheduler)'. biomimetic is 'realised' on one check ('Economic metabolism live'); economy on two ('Economy engine live', 'A VSB ledger exists'). TransformationDashboard.tsx line 322 renders `{Math.round(p.realisation*100)}% · {p.status}` with tone() = emerald for 'realised'. The same figure is the heartbeat's `realisation` (0.955) and POST /transformation/orchestrate's `realisation_before`. EVIDENCE: curl GET /api/v1/transformation/realisation (pillar rows quoted); agentic_core/api/transformation.py:110-112 (evidence lambdas), :191 `status = "realised" if frac >= 0.999`; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/TransformationDashboard.tsx:104-108, 316-332. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the section heading and the overall gauge say 'API surface coverage — not delivery'; the per-pillar status word and colour say 'realised'.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown, in emerald, '100% · realised' beside the pillar 'One self-running, self-healing, self-improving organism' (also 'Biomimetic + biogeo-physical mediation' and 'VSB as hybrid Waqf/Trust autonomous economy'). That is an assertion, not an omission, and it is untrue by the vision's own W512 text (cannot regulate, turn over or select). It is tier 1 rather than 2 because the status word itself states the outcome; it is BORDERLINE with tier 3 because the page heading above the rows reads 'router and store checks — coverage, not delivery' and the API carries a top-level `measure` saying the same. The per-pillar object carries no caveat and the word shown is 'realised'. REFUTER: Reproduced. GET /transformation/realisation returns self_running, biomimetic and economy each at realisation 1.0 / status 'realised' on route-presence checks (transformation.py:110-121, status rule at :191). TransformationDashboard.tsx:322 prints '100% · realised' in emerald beside 'One self-running, self-healing, self-improving organism'. It is not tier 2/3 because the caveat ('router and store checks - coverage, not delivery') is on the section heading only; the per-pillar word and colour contradict it and the pillar object carries no caveat. Genuinely borderline, as the assessor said: the heartbeat's copy of the figure does carry last_realisation_measure. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Rename the per-pillar status vocabulary at the writer (e.g. 'covered' / 'partly covered' / 'not covered') and the field `realisation` -> `coverage`, adding the new field rather than changing the old one's meaning; render the new word.
