items.title: The VSB Economy page's default entity 'Workstation IDBO (apex)' is one the backend says does not exist, and the page never shows that statement — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R6), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §12: each VSB is an autonomous economic entity with double-entry books, owner payments in virtual WST; §15.6 label simulation. OBSERVED: POST /economy/cycle with the default vsb_id posted 8 ledger entries, accrued 120 WST to the Owner, and a 20 WST payout was then accepted — all against an id the same response labels UNREGISTERED. grep for registration_basis / UNREGISTERED / `.registration` across apps/workstation-superapp/src returns nothing. EVIDENCE: curl POST /api/v1/economy/cycle {revenue:1000,costs:200} -> registration:'UNREGISTERED' + registration_basis; POST /economy/owner-payments/payout {amount:20} -> paid; VSBEconomy.tsx:56 (default 'workstation-idbo'), :305 (option label), cycle-result block :526-560 renders no registration field. WHY THIS TIER: The API body says: "'workstation-idbo' is not a registered living entity: this cycle is a SIMULATION run on request values, and the ledger entries and any Owner accrual it wrote belong to no entity that exists." The page shows none of it: the selector reads 'Workstation IDBO (apex)' and the run produces a waterfall, an 'Owner balance 100 WST' in the good tone, and a board pack. Tier 2 not 1: the figures are arithmetic on typed values and the page says all flows are virtual WST; tier 2 not 3 because the one statement that the books belong to nothing registered never reaches the page. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Render `registration_basis` at the top of the cycle result and beside the selector when the selected id is not on the living roster; relabel the option.

items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R6), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8: the organism defends itself; health and live compliance 'continuously monitored, evaluated'. OBSERVED: immune.py's docstring says it tracks 'HTTP 5xx error counts' and 'rate-limit throttle events'; no caller records either (the only writers are the AI gateway, the native orchestrator, biobus.record_error from management_systems, the heartbeat's compliance regression and vbs/quality). With zero events the term is 1.0 and flagged measured:true, whereas the sibling self-healing term in the same state reports null 'nothing measured, health unknown'. CCA review then approved a governed-lever change on 'MEASURED composite_health 0.90 >= 0.5' and the twin pre-validation passed on the same figure. EVIDENCE: curl GET /api/v1/organism/systems, /organism/status, /organism/health-summary; grep 'http_5xx' -> only the dataclass comment (immune.py:24); grep immune.record callers; biobus.py:299, :363; curl POST /cca/{id}/review -> decision_source 'health_threshold_rule'. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No on the organism pages (OrganismAnatomy.tsx:306-318, OrganismDashboard.tsx:383-392 print the percentage and the count); yes on GET /transformation/realisation.. WHY THIS TIER: The Organism and Anatomy pages show 'Immune 100% NOMINAL · 0 errors in window' and 'measured only 100%', and the summary sentence 'Organism at peak on what is measured'. Nothing on those surfaces says which errors can be counted. It is not tier 1 because the number is a true count of what the sensor received and the basis says 'computed from 0 failure(s) in the window'; it is not tier 3 because the narrow scope is stated only on a different surface (transformation's organism_health_basis: 'AI-call failures and compliance regressions only - route 5xx failures are not tracked'). REFUTER: Reproduced. immune.py's docstring lists HTTP 5xx and rate-limit events; the only writers are the AI gateway, the native orchestrator, biobus.record_error, the heartbeat compliance regression and vbs/quality - 'http_5xx' appears only in a dataclass comment. The term is flagged measured:true and is the sole measured term (40% weight) deciding mode and gates; the CCA record cca-a7668e7429 shows decision_source 'health_threshold_rule'. At my read the figure was 0.9 with 1 compliance_fail, not 100%/0, but the gap is the same. OrganismAnatomy.tsx:306-318 prints the percentage and 'N errors in window' with no scope; the scope sentence (HEALTH_SCOPE, 'route 5xx failures are not tracked') exists in immune.py:146 and on the transformation response but not on the organism cards. Tier 2: a true count of a narrow sensor, narrowness unstated where read; not tier 1 because nothing shown is false. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Carry the scope sentence transformation already has into immune.status()['health_basis'] and render it on both cards; report health as null-with-reason when events_in_window is 0 and nothing has been observed, as self-healing does; correct the docstring.

items.title: Charity allocation silently drops a cause below a top-5 cut while its rule says the remainder is split across 'every cleared cause' — MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v15 (R6), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §12: 'donates intelligently to causes by real-world urgency (WATER · Orphan · Conflict/disaster · Dawah; 100%-donation-only)'; Owner directives honoured. OBSERVED: Default run: 6 grants summing 90.00, refugee_support absent with no reason. With exclusions:[conflict_relief] the exclusion WAS honoured and refugee_support was then funded — so the cut is positional. Exclusions, priority floor (10% each) and unfunded-priority reporting all work. EVIDENCE: curl POST /api/v1/economy/cycle (grants list vs GET /economy/charity/candidates' 7 rows); agentic_core/economy/charity.py:216-224 ranked(top=5), :246 `winners = self.ranked(top)`, :321-327 allocation_rule; VSBEconomy.tsx:597-609 (row renders cause, score, amount only). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — neither the response nor the page names the cut for a non-priority cause.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader of the cycle response is told: 'the remaining 60.0% is split pro-rata by score across every cleared cause'. On the default directives 'Refugee & displacement support' (score 0.8487, ranked above Dawah's 0.8482 on the candidates list) received nothing and appears in neither grants, excluded_by_compliance nor priorities_unfunded. The top-5 cut is named only for unfunded PRIORITIES. Tier 2 because the cut is a real, unstated shortfall; not tier 1 because 'cleared' is technically the screened top-5 set, so the sentence is evasive rather than flatly false. Two smaller things ride with it: the page's grant rows do not show each grant's §11 verdict although the rule says 'each grant carries its verdict' (all were 'review' = unassessed), and on one run the grants summed to 64.45 WST against a 64.44 budget (the venture side records absorbed_rounding_wst; charity does not). REFUTER: Reproduced by code and the candidates route (I did not re-run a cycle). charity.py allocate() takes ranked(top=5), then adds only PRIORITIES from outside the cut; GET /economy/charity/candidates lists 7 causes with refugee_support (0.8487) sixth, above dawah (0.8482), so on default directives it gets nothing and lands in none of grants / excluded_by_compliance / priorities_unfunded. allocation_rule says the remainder goes to 'every cleared cause' and `method` says 'budget split pro-rata by score' - neither names the cut. VSBEconomy.tsx:597-609 rows show cause, score, amount only. Tier 2: an unstated cut; not tier 1 since 'cleared' is literally the screened set. Weight is modest: the dropped cause is not one of the four the vision names. The 64.45 vs 64.44 rounding claim I did not check. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Add `not_funded_below_cut: [{id, cause, rank, why}]` to allocate() and say 'top-N' in allocation_rule; render each grant's compliance verdict; absorb the rounding penny into one named grant.

items.title: The constitutional output gate records `compliant: true` after an eight-pattern shell/SQL/private-key regex, with no coverage statement, and the platform's own count is 37 of 64 modules gated — MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v15 (R6), measured 2026-10-10 against HEAD ab829862 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.5 invariant 2: mandatory GaaS gate on every output. OBSERVED: Every AI generation through the gateway IS pre-gated, post-screened and chained (267 `ai.generation_gated` events on a verifying chain). The post screen is `_UNSAFE_OUTPUT` (rm -rf /, DROP/TRUNCATE, unbounded DELETE, private-key headers). If the gate cannot load it fails open with compliant:True plus a `gate_unavailable` note. GET /transformation/realisation itself reports 'GaaS gate on EVERY output (§17.5 invariant 2): 37 of 64 API modules' as not met. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/gaas/v5/policy_gate.py:65-74, :121-128 vs :116-119; agentic_core/ai/gateway.py:31-37, :66-85; curl GET /api/v1/gaas/status (by_type); curl GET /transformation/realisation (governance pillar 0.5 partial). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The 37-of-64 coverage is disclosed on the Transformation page; the narrowness of a 'compliant' pass is not disclosed on the record.. WHY THIS TIER: The stored UEG event and the completion's governance_checkpoint say `compliant: true` / `post_compliant: true`. The pre-gate was given a `coverage_limit` sentence precisely so a pass is not read as a clearance (W580); the post-gate returns a bare {compliant: True, violations: []}. It is tier 2 (a narrow screen whose narrowness is unstated) rather than tier 1 because the UI chip a person sees says 'gate: checked', not 'compliant', and it borders tier 1 for a reader of the ledger record. Not tier 3 because nothing at the record says what was not screened. REFUTER: Reproduced, and I tier it HARSHER than the assessor (2 -> 1). validate_output (policy_gate.py:121-128) returns a bare {compliant: True, violations: []} after one eight-alternative regex; gateway.py:66-85 writes that into every completion's governance_checkpoint as gate 'constitutional_policy_gate_v5', post_compliant: true, and chains it as ai.generation_gated with compliant: true (382 such events at my read). The task defines an API surface's reached form as its response body and stored record, and tier 1 includes certifying what could not be assessed: 'compliant' under the name of the constitutional gate is a clearance of constitutional compliance that a shell/SQL/private-key regex cannot give. The same file gave the PRE-gate a coverage_limit sentence for exactly this reason and left the post-gate bare. Not tier 2 because this is a positive boolean assertion, not a silent narrowness. Mitigations that keep it borderline: the UI chip reads 'gate: checked' (NativeAI.tsx:24), and the fail-open path does carry gate_unavailable. The 37-of-64 coverage part is disclosed and would be tier 3 on its own. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Return `screened: 'unsafe_payload_patterns'` and a coverage_limit from validate_output and carry both into the checkpoint and the UEG event; add a field rather than renaming `compliant`.

items.title: A pasted deliverable is certified 'QMS pass · specifically designed: met · verified: met' against a structure taken from its own headings — MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R1), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §10 as built: 'specifically designed · verified' are computed from the delivery's coverage against its DECLARED structure, and are recorded NOT ASSESSABLE where the check cannot fail. OBSERVED: POST /deliverables/produce with `content` and no `sections` sets sections to the content's own `#`/`##` headings (deliverables.py:260-262), then measures coverage of those headings in that same content. Any text of 200+ characters with one heading and no stub word passes. The export banner then reads '§10 bar: 2 measured'. The gate's own code (quality.py W616 comment) names this class - 'a coverage the generator guarantees is not a measurement' - and routes it to not-assessable for repo/web-app templates via `sections_by_construction`, but not for verbatim ingest. Reach: on this floor-only deployment the UI callers (GenesisJourney 'save as deliverable', line 319-332) pass served_by 'native' so they get 'not assessable'; the certifying path is reached by API today and by that same Genesis button as soon as a model serves a journey (that second part is read from code, not executed). EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce {type:'report', brief:'A full market report', content:'## Notes\n'+filler} -> sections ['Notes'], delivery_coverage 1.0, basis '1 declared section(s) checked against the delivered content', qms_gate_passed True, deliv-f81c6e01 and deliv-c14e3453. GET /api/v1/deliverables lists both with qms_gate_passed true. agentic_core/api/deliverables.py:255-275; agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:353-360. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The basis says 'declared structure'; nothing says the structure was read off the content being measured.. WHY THIS TIER: The stored record and response say `qms_gate_passed: true`, `verified: {met: true, measured: true, source: 'gate', basis: 'QMS gate on real coverage/stub metrics'}` and `specifically designed: {met: true ... 'delivery coverage 1.0 against the declared structure'}` for a body that was one heading plus 'blah blah words that say nothing' twelve times. The 'declared structure' is the list of headings found in the pasted text, so coverage is 1.0 by construction: the gate certified what it could not assess. That is a certification, not an omission, so it is tier 1 rather than 2. It is not tier 3 because nothing in the record says the structure was self-derived. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /deliverables/produce with content '## Notes' plus twelve repeats of 'blah blah words that say nothing' and no sections gave sections ['Notes'], delivery_coverage 1.0, qms_gate_passed true, 'specifically designed: met, measured, source gate' and 'verified: met'. The structure is read off the measured text (deliverables.py:260-262), so the check cannot fail. Tier 1 rather than 2 because the record asserts a measured pass, which is a certification and not an omission; not tier 3 because nothing says the structure was self-derived. Reach is the API record and export today; the Genesis save button passes the journey's served_by (GenesisJourney.tsx:332), so the UI path certifying under a model is read from code, not run. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: In produce(), when `req.sections` is empty and the sections were derived from the content, pass `sections_by_construction='the sections were read from the supplied text itself'` to assure_delivery so the gate records not-assessable; or measure against the type's declared sections (_TYPES[type]).

items.title: An exported deliverable says 'composed in-house by <whatever the caller typed>' over text the platform did not compose — MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R1), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11 rule 4-5: every AI-served surface renders serving provenance; AI content is labelled with provenance, never authoritative. §15.6: never fabricate. OBSERVED: `source_served_by` is typed `Any` and unvalidated. `_provenance_phrase` resolves a verbatim ingest to the caller-declared origin and, for any string that is not 'native'/'template'/'verbatim-ingest', returns 'composed in-house by {token}'. The same string also switches the §10 gate from not-assessable to assessable. With no origin declared the export is honest ('supplied verbatim by the caller - the platform did not compose this text and records no origin for it'). EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce {content:..., source_served_by:'anything-i-type'} -> deliv-c14e3453; GET /api/v1/deliverables/deliv-c14e3453/export?format=md -> '_report · composed in-house by anything-i-type_'. Same with 'local-qwen' (deliv-918dd417, deliv-0ddcee2c). agentic_core/api/deliverables.py:165-173, 447-460. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The export drops the record's own 'supplied verbatim by the caller' note once an origin string is present.. WHY THIS TIER: The exported Markdown file reads '_report · composed in-house by anything-i-type_'. No model ran (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), the platform composed nothing, and the stored record itself says 'content supplied verbatim by the caller - not regenerated'. The file a third party receives asserts an in-house composition by a named producer on the strength of a free-text request field. That is an untrue provenance statement travelling with the output, so tier 1; it is not tier 2 because the sentence is asserted, not omitted. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution with my own string. source_served_by 'refuter-typed-this' produced an md and html export reading 'composed in-house by refuter-typed-this' while the stored ai_provenance.note says 'content supplied verbatim by the caller — not regenerated'. The same string also set the gate's served_by, so the gate ran and passed. Tier 1 because the exported file asserts an untrue composition by a named producer; it is an assertion, not an omission, and nothing in the file qualifies it. Reach is API-only (both UI callers pass a real served_by), and the tier definition counts the response and stored record as the reached form. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: For a verbatim ingest with a declared origin, word the line as a declaration: 'supplied verbatim by the caller, who declared it as produced by {token} - the platform did not compose it and has not verified that origin'.

items.title: A deliverable's 'regressed / unchanged' verdict is computed against the floor's coverage of 1.0, which the same record calls not assessable — MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R1), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §10: verified · tested · validated; a criterion is recorded NOT ASSESSABLE when the floor served the output. OBSERVED: Replacing a floor scaffold with a person's own text is reported as a regression because the scaffold echoes every requested heading. A floor-to-floor regenerate reports 'unchanged', coverage 1.0 -> 1.0. Coverage is also a case-insensitive substring test: 'no analysis whatsoever' counted the 'Analysis' section as present. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/deliverables/{id}/regenerate on deliv-df6b42cd with content -> improvement {coverage_before:1.0, coverage_after:0.333, verdict:'regressed', note:'This version scored LOWER...'}; on deliv-5d59a505 with a new brief -> verdict 'unchanged'. Rendered at apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/Deliverables.tsx:259-272 (read, not driven in a browser). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The tooltip gives the coverage figures but not that the prior figure cannot fail.. WHY THIS TIER: The page shows a chip 'v2 regressed -67%' and the sentence 'This version scored lower than the one it replaced', and the record says 'This version scored LOWER than the one it replaced' with coverage_before 1.0. That 1.0 belongs to a floor frame whose own QMS basis says 'coverage cannot fail by construction'. The figure is real arithmetic, so it is not a fabricated number (not tier 1), but the surface does not say the baseline is the unassessable one, so it is not tier 3. REFUTER: Reproduced. A floor report (deliv-1532562c, coverage 1.0, qms basis 'coverage cannot fail by construction') regenerated with a person's own text returned verdict 'regressed', coverage 1.0 -> 0.333, and the note 'This version scored LOWER than the one it replaced'. The 0.333 confirms the substring test: my text had one heading and the phrase 'no analysis whatsoever', and 'Analysis' was counted as covered. Tier 2: the arithmetic is real, so it is not a fabricated figure, but neither the chip nor the tooltip (Deliverables.tsx:259-272, read not driven) says the baseline is the unassessable one, so it is not disclosed. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: When either version's gate is not assessable, set improvement.verdict to 'not_compared' with the reason; the page already hides the chip for that value.

items.title: The tafsir tool tells the reader a model would translate the ayah, while the translation tool says translation of Qur'anic text is not offered whatever model is available — MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R1), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: A.9.3: translation of sacred text refuses rather than approximates; it is not an ordinary feature. Translations come only from licensed, sourced editions (A.12.1). OBSERVED: When a model is available the tafsir prompt adds '## Transliteration' and '## Translation (AI-assisted, working from the provided text...)' and a model-served reply keeps them. THE MODEL PATH IS READ FROM CODE, NOT EXECUTED (no model can serve here). A general deliverable brief asking to 'translate each ayah into English and give a tafsir' was also accepted (deliv-5d59a505); on the floor it produced only a keyword frame, and the Owner ruling of 2026-10-10 deliberately does not refuse general documents by subject, so only the tafsir route is reported as the gap. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/religion.py:313-319 and 338 ('A model-served tafsir keeps them'). Executed: POST /api/v1/religion/quran-tafsir {surah:1, ayah_start:1, ayah_end:3} -> floor_note as quoted; POST /api/v1/qep/translation/translate with Arabic -> 422 'NOT OFFERED, by ruling (A.9.3) ... whatever model is available'. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The tafsir result shows 'no translation or transliteration is offered (a translation must come from a model...)'. The QEP translation surface shows 'Arabic / Qur'anic text is NOT translated here, by ruling, whatever model is available'. On this deployment nothing untrue is served (the floor withholds), so not tier 1. But the ratified boundary is applied on one route and not the other, and neither surface says so, so it is an invisible shortfall rather than a disclosed one. REFUTER: Reproduced on both halves that can run here. The tafsir floor_note says 'a translation must come from a model'; POST /qep/translation/translate with Arabic returns 422 'NOT OFFERED, by ruling (A.9.3) ... whatever model is available'. religion.py:313-316 adds '## Translation (AI-assisted ...)' to the prompt when a model is available and the comment says a model-served tafsir keeps it. The model path is read from code, not executed. Tier 2, not 1: the floor withholds both sections here, so nothing untrue is served, and the note is true of the code. Not tier 3: neither surface says the boundary is applied on one route only. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Remove the two model-only sections from the tafsir prompt and offer the sourced Pickthall rendering (already served at /qep/translation/{surah}/{ayah}) beside the Arabic; change the floor_note to say translation is not composed here by ruling.

items.title: The scholar-review gate withholds correctly, but no route or page can add a scholar or record an approval, and the page describes the registry as if it could be used — MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R1), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: A.12.3: a named human scholar approves AI-composed religious content before a learner sees it, enforced as a pipeline gate: draft -> in review -> approved by a named reviewer -> published. The heartbeat was started by another session mid-run and none of these moved. By the same code a status of 'operating - the heartbeat is tending this entity' would survive the heartbeat being stopped (inferred from the writers, not driven - I did not stop a shared heartbeat). The constitutional layer, by contrast, labels its fields honestly ('derived from the founder's problem statement - not authored'). EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/genesis.py:1450 and :1689 (`"ceo_specification": (req.commercialisation or req.concept)[:2000]`); agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2176-2195 (_strategic_layer: any non-placeholder text => holds 'content', basis 'the AI CEO specification recorded on this entity'); live pack for vsb-90defc9445 (version 1, dcs_registered true); apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/synthesis/GenesisJourney.tsx:1289-1297 renders `{k}: {v.holds}` emerald for 'content' with title=v.basis. The text under it is the sentence I typed into the Concept box, verbatim; no AI CEO (model or floor) composed anything. That is an authorship assertion that is untrue on a reached, DCS-registered record, so it is tier 1 rather than tier 2 (it is not merely silent about a shortfall) and not tier 3 (the adjacent refresh_basis repeats the claim: "this layer is whatever the CEO specification is"). REFUTER: Reproduced live: POST /api/v1/vsb/{id}/board-pack for vsb-90defc9445 returns layers.strategic {ceo: the founder's concept sentence verbatim, holds 'content', present true, basis 'the AI CEO specification recorded on this entity'}, layers_present includes 'strategic'; genesis.py:1450/:1689 write ceo_specification = (req.commercialisation or req.concept); GenesisJourney.tsx:1289-1298 renders an emerald 'strategic: content' chip with the basis as tooltip. I move the tier DOWN from 1 to 2. That is an unstated shortfall on a reached, DCS-registered record (tier 2), not tier 3 because nothing discloses it, and short of tier 1 because the literal statement about the field is true. The organisation is presented as reconfigurable with user design control, and the one axis that changes how the mission is screened is fixed silently - an invisible shortfall (tier 2). Nothing untrue is printed (not tier 1); nothing discloses it (not tier 3). REFUTER: Reproduced: SwarmIntelligence.tsx:163 posts `domain: 'enterprise', realm: 'enterprise'` as literals; the only other mention of domain in the file is a comment at :300, so neither a control nor the result card shows it. My API cascade with domain 'religion' and csuite_roles [CFO, COO] ran (run 62ec933204) and the roster basis says 'a custom CoE specialism is honoured, a custom officer is not', confirming the backend accepts what the UI never sends. Tier 2: nothing untrue is printed, and the fixed axis is not disclosed. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Add realm/domain selects (from lib/taxonomy.ts) and a CoE-specialism input to the delegate panel, or at minimum print 'run as: enterprise / enterprise' on the result card.

items.title: A facility's compliance verdict says the user's subject 'describes itself with halal vocabulary' when the word came from the platform's own floor template — MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R4), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §15.6 honesty over polish (never fabricate); §7 digital resources (Reactor = Incubator + Experimentation + Studio) with honest quality/compliance records OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/reactor/studio with title 'Hive losses' and POST /api/v1/reactor/experiment with subject 'low-cost hive monitoring subscription' (neither contains the word) both returned quality_assurance.quality.compliance.verdicts[sharia_halal] = status 'review', coverage 'vocabulary', reason "the subject describes itself with halal vocabulary ('halal') and no prohibited (haram) term matched — that is the subject's own claim". The word is in the deterministic floor's own option frame ('Score each against value, feasibility, risk, and values-fit (halal/beneficence)'), which the route passes to assure_delivery as the content to screen. POST /api/v1/petri/culture on the same subject, whose floor sections contain no option frame, returned 'no halal vocabulary is present' (coverage 'none'). EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/products.py:767 `qa = await assure_delivery(insight or ..., ...)` (insight = gateway output) and :590 (experiment, `combined`); agentic_core/api/compliance.py:397 builds the sentence from _HALAL_VOCAB.search(text). Live responses saved from the three calls; ReactorStudio.tsx:218 renders a compliance chip from this block. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the verdict attributes the vocabulary to the subject; nothing says the screened text was the platform's own composed output.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown the sentence "the subject describes itself with halal vocabulary ('halal') … that is the subject's own claim". That is an untrue statement about what the user wrote, on a faith-sensitive framework, in the response body and behind the Reactor Studio compliance chip. It is not tier 2 because it is an assertion, not an omission; the mitigating clause ('not a certification') does not correct the false attribution. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /api/v1/reactor/studio with title 'Hive losses' (no such word in my input) returned sharia_halal status 'review', coverage 'vocabulary', reason "the subject describes itself with halal vocabulary ('halal') ... that is the subject's own claim". The only occurrence of the word is the floor's own option frame in the returned insight ('values-fit (halal/beneficence)', agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py:525), which products.py:767 hands to assure_delivery as the text to screen. Tier 1 rather than 2: it is a positive false attribution to the user's subject on a faith framework, not an omission; the 'not a certification' clause does not retract it. Not higher-impact than that: status is 'review', never a pass. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Screen the user's subject (title/subject/objective) for self-description vocabulary, not the composed output; or have the reason say the word was found in the composed text and name which text was screened.

items.title: The Operations page puts a green success tick on every run that merely returned text, beside a headline that says success was not assessed — MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R4), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §6 'optimised … verified, tested and validated' cascades; §8 continuously monitored and evaluated; §15.6 never certify what was not assessed OBSERVED: GET /api/v1/operations/outcomes rows carry success:true together with quality_gate:null, quality_verdict:null and success_basis 'NOT ASSESSED — no quality gate evaluated this run; it produced output'. GET /api/v1/operations/summary says success_rate null, '0 assessed of 140 … not a success measure'. The page's 'Recent outcomes' list renders `o.success ? <CheckCircle2 emerald/> : ✕` and ignores quality_gate/success_basis, so all floor-served unassessed rows show a green tick. top_resource in the summary is '/api/v1/cognitive/mjm', a route whose every recorded run failed. EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/OperationalExcellence.tsx:268 (tick from o.success), :100 (headline 'not assessed'); live /operations/outcomes and /operations/summary bodies; agentic_core/api/operational_excellence.py:536 top_resource = ranks[0]. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Contradicted on the same page: the headline discloses, the per-row tick asserts.. WHY THIS TIER: A user sees a green check mark next to 'agent:mgmt_audit … native' — a per-run success mark for a run nothing assessed, while the stat card two inches above says 'Success rate (gate-assessed): not assessed'. A success tick is a certification of an outcome the platform could not assess, which is tier 1 rather than tier 2; it is not tier 3 because the row itself carries no qualifier on screen. REFUTER: Reproduced. GET /operations/outcomes rows carry success:true with quality_gate:null and success_basis 'NOT ASSESSED'; GET /operations/summary says success_rate null over 190 runs, 0 assessed. OperationalExcellence.tsx:268 renders an emerald CheckCircle2 from o.success alone and never reads quality_gate or success_basis on the row. The same page's code comment (W495) already treats 'returned text shown as success' as a defect for the headline stat. Tier 1 not 2 because a success mark is rendered per run from a field named success for runs nothing assessed; not tier 3 because the row itself carries no qualifier. The top_resource detail also holds: /operations/rankings ranks /api/v1/cognitive/mjm first (kind route_failure, produced_rate 0.0); at my call the summary named /api/v1/law/matter/assemble, likewise a route_failure with produced_rate 0.0 — a failing route is presented as 'top'. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Render the row mark three-state from quality_gate (assessed-pass / assessed-fail / grey 'produced, not assessed') and title it with success_basis; pick top_resource only from resources that produced.

items.title: The cognitive engine catalogue contradicts itself about whether any engine computes, how many have modules and whether its solver is installed — MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R4), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.2 Nervous — the nine cognitive engines; §8 W482 'an engine computes or says it cannot', one registry, one contract OBSERVED: GET /api/v1/cognitive/engines returns, in one body: basis "12 of the 12 engines exist as modules and run; the 0 meta engines are PLANNED (no module yet …). No engine computes yet: each of the 12 returns a fixed marker"; registry.what_registration_does_not_mean "the three META engines genuinely compute their named quantity … and so do the three AUXILIARY engines"; registry.what_the_denominator_means "Only the 6 foundational engines have modules" (12 are registered); rows with status 'built-computes' and computes:false; and declared_but_absent_basis 'POT is not installed' while GET /api/v1/minimisation/status says 'its solver (POT) IS importable in this deployment'. Executed: POST /api/v1/cognitive/engine with niyyah and tawazun each validated its inputs and refused with a specific basis — not a fixed marker — so 'each of the 12 returns a fixed marker' is false. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/cognitive.py:87 `_e.setdefault('computes', False)` applied to every row; :123-126 the stale basis f-string; live bodies of /cognitive/engines, /cognitive/engine (niyyah, tawazun), /minimisation/status. No frontend file calls /api/v1/cognitive/* (grep of apps/workstation-superapp/src), so the reached form is the response body. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the page states both sides as fact.. WHY THIS TIER: The body shows a reader the sentences 'No engine computes yet: each of the 12 returns a fixed marker' and 'the three META engines genuinely compute', plus 'POT is not installed' against another live route's 'POT IS importable'. At least one of each pair is untrue as stated on a reached (API) surface, so it is a truth defect rather than an undisclosed gap; it under-claims rather than over-claims, which is why it is ranked below the two above. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. One GET /cognitive/engines body states: basis '12 of the 12 engines exist as modules and run; the 0 meta engines are PLANNED ... No engine computes yet: each of the 12 returns a fixed marker'; registry.what_registration_does_not_mean 'the three META engines genuinely compute'; what_the_denominator_means 'Only the 6 foundational engines have modules' with 12 registered; six rows status 'built-computes' with computes:false; and 'POT is not installed' against /minimisation/status 'its solver (POT) IS importable in this deployment'. POST /cognitive/engine for niyyah and tawazun returned input-specific refusals (served_by 'native-refused'), not a fixed marker, so the basis sentence is false. Tier 1: untrue sentences in a reached API body (no frontend caller of /api/v1/cognitive/* found). It under-claims, which bounds the harm, but it is an assertion, not an omission. I could not settle which POT statement is right (the shell's python has no 'ot' module, but that may not be the backend's interpreter); the contradiction stands either way. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Compute `computes` per row from the tier (false for the six foundational, true-or-refuses for meta/auxiliary), rebuild the basis sentence from those counts, and take the POT statement from one import probe shared by both routes.

items.title: A composed Genome stage shows a green 'ran' chip and fitness 0.5 with the 'not encoded — defaults' label stripped — MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §7 'every composed resource runs its REAL engine'; §17.2 Genome; provenance travels with the output OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/resources/compositions/{cid}/run with the genome resource returned a real_resource_runs row {resource:'genome', fitness:0.5, traits: all ten 0.5, dominant_trait:null, kind:'facility_run', outcome:'produced', outcome_phrase:'ran its engine and produced this output'} with no served_by, encoded, fitness_provenance or encoding_note. The engine's own route (POST /api/v1/organism/genome/encode) returns for the same input encoded:false, fitness_provenance 'default-unencoded', served_by 'native' and 'this vector is NOT an analysis of the entity'. Each composed run also adds another default genome to the population store. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/resource_fabric.py:695-716 (the returned dict keeps genome_id/fitness/traits and drops encoded, fitness_provenance, encoding_note, served_by); ResourceFabric.tsx:830-834 falls to the emerald 'ran' chip for outcome 'produced' and :870 shows a provenance badge only when rr.served_by exists; heading at :797 counts it in 'N ran an engine'. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No, at the composition run; yes on the Genome lab card.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader sees 'genome … ran' in emerald and, in the API/stored run, 'fitness: 0.5' with 'ran its engine and produced this output'. Nothing on the row says every value is the unencoded default, although the engine itself says so. That is a partial result whose shortfall is invisible at this surface (tier 2); I did not tier it 1 because 0.5 is not rendered on the page and the vector's uniformity is visible in the API body. REFUTER: Reproduced from the handler and the engine route (I did not run a composition). resource_fabric.py:696-716 calls encode_genome and returns only resource/ran/genome_id/fitness/dominant_trait/traits/output, dropping encoded, fitness_provenance, encoding_note and served_by; genome resolves to outcome 'produced' ('ran its engine and produced this output', :1184-1207). POST /organism/genome/encode returned encoded:false, fitness_provenance 'default-unencoded', fitness_score 0.5 and 'this vector is NOT an analysis of the entity'. ResourceFabric.tsx falls through to the emerald 'ran' chip and shows a provenance badge only when rr.served_by exists. Tier 2 not 1: 'ran its engine' is literally true and 0.5 is the engine's real default, so the defect is the stripped qualifier (an omission); not tier 3 because nothing at the composed stage says it. My probe added one default genome named 'refuter-probe' to the store. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Carry encoded, fitness_provenance, encoding_note and served_by through the fabric branch and set outcome to a non-'produced' value (e.g. 'defaulted') when encoded is false.

items.title: The immune defence reports 'reconfigured … tighten generation' after writing a switch nothing reads, and files a no-op as an approved change — MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.2 Immune — GaaS + self-healing (defend); §8 the organism defends itself OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/cca/immune-reconfigure at threat ELEVATED returned status 'approved', action 'reconfigured', reason 'Elevated error patterns — tighten generation to precise', message 'Immune reconfigurator: ELEVATED → gateway.temperature_bias=precise (approved)'. The same body's applied block says wired:false, consumer 'stored-only — nothing reads this key back'. A second call filed a second approved CCA change with old_value 'precise' → new_value 'precise' and reverts_to 'precise'. The heartbeat calls this same function. (I restored temperature_bias to neutral afterwards.) EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/change_control.py:1205-1223 (action hard-coded 'reconfigured', reason = plan['why']); :1183-1190 the no-consumer branch keeps status 'approved'; GET /api/v1/organism/config key_wiring lists gateway.temperature_bias wired:false; live responses cca-a1f2eedef5 and cca-f46e692063. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly — nested in applied.wired/consumer; the message and action contradict it.. WHY THIS TIER: The top-level fields a reader or caller takes first say 'action: reconfigured' and 'tighten generation to precise'; the fact that nothing was tightened is only in a nested applied.consumer string. The truth is present in the payload, so I did not tier it 1, but the summary line asserts an effect and the disclosure is not where the claim is made, so it is not a stated shortfall in the tier-3 sense. REFUTER: Reproduced by reading the handler and the live wiring table; I did not re-fire the route because it writes config and files a change record. change_control.py:1185-1190 keeps status 'approved' with audit note 'config value set; no wired consumer exists', while :1205-1223 returns the literal action 'reconfigured', reason plan['why'] and a message '... (approved)'. GET /organism/config lists gateway.temperature_bias wired:false, 'stored-only — nothing reads this key back'. Tier 2 not 1: a stored value was in fact changed, so 'reconfigured' is not strictly false, and the same body carries applied.wired/consumer; not tier 3 because the headline fields assert an effect ('tighten generation') and the qualifier sits nested elsewhere. The repeat-call no-op filing (precise to precise) I did not execute; it is not contradicted by the code I read. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: When the lever has no consumer, return action 'recorded_only' and a message that says no live behaviour changed; refuse to file a change whose new value equals the old one.

items.title: Every enterprise gets the same four-stage delivery swarm and no surface that lists it says so — MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §6 'Bespoke-per-solution swarms … synthesised, modelled and simulated bespoke to each solution's needs … and bespoke to each founder' OBSERVED: GET /api/v1/resources/swarm lists 'Rural Beekeepers Kashmir — delivery swarm' with stages ai-ceo → c-suite → centre-of-excellence → build-to-order and four fixed instruction sentences; the only entity-specific part is the context string. The Native AI page lists it among saved cascades under 'Design a bespoke swarm cascade'; the Dashboard card describes the enterprise as 'bespoke and autonomous in design'. The capability that does select per objective (POST /api/v1/resources/cell/propose — an exhaustive capability-cover over the registry, verified) is not what establishment uses. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/genesis.py:1010-1040 (docstring: 'every VSB gets the same stages and instructions, and nothing optimises them'; the literal stage list); live /resources/swarm body; NativeAI.tsx:991; DashboardNew.tsx:40; grep of GenesisJourney.tsx finds no mention of the swarm at all. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No, at the surface. Yes in a code docstring and the vision's W627 note.. WHY THIS TIER: A founder sees '<their enterprise> — delivery swarm' in the cascade list with nothing indicating it is identical for every enterprise, next to copy using the word bespoke. The code comment and the vision's own correction note say it, but the surface does not, so the shortfall is invisible (tier 2). It is not tier 1 because no sentence on the row claims the stages were synthesised for this solution. REFUTER: Reproduced. GET /resources/swarm lists 'HiveGuard Kashmir — delivery swarm' with the four literal stages and instructions from genesis.py:1028-1033; only the context string is entity-specific, and the row has no field saying the stages are a platform template. The docstring at :1010-1014 admits every VSB gets the same stages. Note the 'bespoke' heading on NativeAI is for the user's own designer, which is accurate there. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Add template:'platform-default' and a basis line to the registered cascade and render it as 'platform default — not composed for this solution' until cell/propose (or a model) actually selects the stages.

items.title: The degradation monitor reports an 'accuracy' change computed from whether a run returned text — MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8 self-improving, continuously monitored and evaluated; §8 W482 naming invariant — a quantity carries a name only when computed as that thing OBSERVED: GET /api/v1/operations/degradation returned degraded:false, score 0.0, accuracy_change 0.0, thresholds {accuracy_drop:0.093}, method 'PerformanceDegradationDetector'. The handler computes accuracy as the share of rows whose `success` is truthy — the same flag /operations/summary declares 'NOT ASSESSED … not a success measure' because the floor always returns text. No basis field accompanies the figure. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/operational_excellence.py:391 `acc = sum(1 for c in chunk if c.get('success')) / len(chunk)` and :401-405 (no basis in the return); live body. No frontend caller found for /operations/degradation in OperationalExcellence.tsx. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown 'accuracy_change: 0.0' and 'degraded: false'. The numbers are real arithmetic over real rows (so not fabricated, not tier 1), but the response never says the 'accuracy' is the produced-output flag that cannot fall on the floor — an invisible shortfall rather than a disclosed one. REFUTER: Reproduced. GET /operations/degradation returned accuracy_change 0.0 with thresholds.accuracy_drop 0.093 and no basis field; the handler computes accuracy as the share of rows with a truthy success flag (operational_excellence.py:391), the flag /operations/summary calls 'not a success measure'. No caller in OperationalExcellence.tsx. items.title: The provenance ledger accepts any caller's claim about what served a run and stores it unmarked — MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R4), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §6 owned capability with honest provenance (served_by / is_external) on the durable record OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/operations/record with {resource:'audit-probe', served_by:'claude-opus', is_external:false, success:true} returned 200 and stored row op-753adf82 exactly as claimed. The row has no field distinguishing a caller-asserted record from one the platform wrote itself, and it enters the same store that /operations/summary's in_house_rate and the page's per-row provenance badges read. (That probe row remains in the live store; it is labelled 'audit-probe'.) EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/operational_excellence.py:346-349 (route passes req.served_by / req.is_external straight to record_outcome, no auth dependency on the handler); live response; no frontend caller of /operations/record. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader of the Operations page sees a served-by badge and an 'In-house rate' that can include rows nobody on the platform attested — here a row saying an external model's name with is_external:false. Nothing on the row says it was caller-reported, so the weakness is invisible (tier 2); it is not tier 1 because the platform itself does not originate the false row. REFUTER: Reproduced from the handler; I did not post a second false row. operational_excellence.py:346-349 passes req.served_by and req.is_external straight to record_outcome with no dependency and no caller-reported marker, into the store that the summary's in_house_rate and the page's badges read. Tier 2 is the ceiling: the platform originates nothing false, and in this single-user AUTH-off deployment the only caller is the operator, so it is close to tier 3; I leave it at 2 because the stored row and the in-house rate give no way to tell an asserted row from an observed one. The assessor's 'audit-probe' row remains in the live store. items.title: Starting the heartbeat answers status 'started' with running false — MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R4), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.2 circadian operation; §8 a status is computed, not asserted OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/heartbeat/stop returned {running:false,status:'stopped'}; POST /api/v1/heartbeat/start immediately after returned {running:false,status:'started'}. Two seconds later GET /api/v1/heartbeat/status showed running:true. The status word is a literal returned regardless of the flag read in the same line. EVIDENCE: The heartbeat router's start handler: `_hb_mod.heartbeat.start(); return {'running': _hb_mod.heartbeat.running, 'status': 'started'}`; live responses. (Heartbeat confirmed running again after the probe.) DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: A caller is shown 'status: started' beside 'running: false' — one of the two is wrong at that instant and nothing explains the lag. It is a small, transient inconsistency rather than a fabricated outcome, so tier 2 not 1. REFUTER: Reproduced, and it is worse than the assessor described. This is not a lag in a flag: after POST /heartbeat/stop, POST /heartbeat/start is a NO-OP for as long as the old loop is still inside its sleep. Heartbeat.start() returns early when the previous task is not done (heartbeat.py:1114-1116), and stop() only clears the flag, so the task sleeps out effective_interval_seconds (200 s in the rest phase) and then exits. I called start seven times over about 170 seconds; every call answered {running:false, status:'started'}, GET /heartbeat/status stayed running:false with beats frozen at 9, and the heartbeat only came back when I called start again after the old sleep had ended. Had the caller trusted the first 'started', the heartbeat would have stayed stopped for good. Tier 1 rather than 2: 'status: started' is a field asserting an outcome the platform did not produce. The UI is honest about the state: HeartbeatMonitor.tsx reloads status and shows 'Stopped', with no error and no explanation of why Start did nothing. Heartbeat confirmed running again (beats 10) after my probe; it was stopped for roughly three minutes. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Return status derived from the flag ('starting' until the loop reports running) or await the first tick.

items.title: The Law matter panel reports an authority as 'resolved — named in the employment-law corpus' on a bare substring match, so 'e' and 'Act' resolve — MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R5), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §15.6 never fabricate; §3A offering 1 (Law tools); P3.23 design: every authority is resolved against the corpus or refused. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/law/matter/assemble with authorities ['Act','e','Equality Act 2010 Section 999'] returned resolved=True for 'Act' and for 'e', False for the third. The 'corpus' that is searched also includes unified_assimilated_graph.json, a file-path manifest (it contains e.g. 'mock_apk_placeholder.apk' and '20_pre_hearing_simulation.md'), so any fragment of a file name also 'resolves'. The artefact is filing-shaped (ET1) and stored as draft_awaiting_owner_approval with the authority listed as resolved. A fully fictitious case citation was correctly REFUSED, and a real statute absent from the corpus (Employment Rights Act 1996) was refused, so the gate works for whole wrong names; it fails for partial, truncated or mistyped ones. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/legal/specialist.py resolve_authority (lines 39-48): `if n.lower() in _corpus_text().lower()`; _corpus_text reads every *.json and *.md under knowledge/Law/EmploymentTribunal. Live call results: 'Act True', 'e True'. Rendered by apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/MatterAssemblyPanel.tsx line 'resolved' / 'REFUSED' + basis. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The basis sentence says the corpus 'names' it; nothing says the match is a substring.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown '<authority>: resolved — named in the employment-law corpus this platform holds (knowledge/Law/EmploymentTribunal)', and the refusal text promises 'an authority is resolved against a real source or not emitted at all'. That is a certification the code cannot make: it is `n.lower() in corpus_text.lower()`. It is tier 1 rather than 2 because the surface positively asserts a check passed; it is not merely silent about a limit. REFUTER: Reproduced live. POST /api/v1/law/matter/assemble (template_id et1_claim) returned resolved=true for 'Act' and for 'e' with basis 'named in the employment-law corpus this platform holds', and refused 'Equality Act 2010 Section 999' and 'Employment Rights Act 1996'. The code is a bare substring test over every .json/.md under knowledge/Law/EmploymentTribunal. Tier 1 rather than 2 because the panel positively prints '<authority>: resolved — named in the corpus' on a filing-shaped ET1 draft: that is a certification of a check the code cannot make, not silence about a limit. Not tier 3 because nothing on the surface says the match is a substring. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Resolve against a parsed list of authority names from the ontology file only (exact, case-insensitive, whole-name match), exclude the path manifest from the corpus, and add a guard that drives 'e' and a truncated title and expects REFUSED.

items.title: Start after Stop answers "started" while the heartbeat is not running, and the loop then stays dead — MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v16 (R6), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §1/§8: once established the organism 'forever runs ... itself'; the heartbeat is the circadian rhythm that makes it self-running. OBSERVED: POST /heartbeat/stop then POST /heartbeat/start returned {"running":false,"status":"started"}; GET /heartbeat/status still running:false. Repeated at 03:04:20 with the same answer; only at 03:04:41, after the old sleeping task had exited, did start return running:true. Cause: stop() only sets running=False while the task sleeps up to effective_interval (200 s in MAINTENANCE_REST); start() returns early on `if self._task and not self._task.done(): return` without setting running=True, so the old task wakes, sees running False and exits. The route then reports status 'started' unconditionally. Stop/start are also not written to the UEG (only /configure logs heartbeat.lever_changed). EVIDENCE: agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:1114-1128 (start/stop), :868-877 (run loop); agentic_core/api/heartbeat.py:47-56 (status literal). Live: stop -> start -> {"running":false,"status":"started"}; status running:false until 03:04:41. HeartbeatMonitor.tsx:83-94 shows an error only when !r.ok. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. HTTP 200, status 'started', no error on the page.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown {"running": false, "status": "started"} with HTTP 200 - the word 'started' asserts an outcome that did not happen (the loop was not started and stayed stopped for about 3 minutes of retries). That is an untrue statement on the reached response, not an omission, so it is Tier 1 rather than 2. On the Heartbeat page the same click produces no error and the card simply stays 'Stopped'. REFUTER: Reproduced live. POST /api/v1/heartbeat/stop then POST /heartbeat/start returned {"running":false,"status":"started"} at 04:09:14, again at ~04:10:01 and 04:10:38; GET /heartbeat/status stayed running:false. Only at 04:11:30 (after the old sleeping task had woken and exited) did start return running:true. Code matches: start() returns early while the old task is not done without setting running=True; the route prints 'started' unconditionally. Tier 1 rather than 2: the literal 'started' asserts an outcome that did not happen, with no explanation beside it (unlike a stated caveat); not lower because the loop genuinely stays dead until someone retries after the sleep. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: In start(): when the task is alive but running is False, set running=True (the loop re-checks it) - and make the route return status from heartbeat.running ('started' only if true, else 'not started: previous loop still stopping').

The only consumer suppresses the evolve tick when ATP < 0.2, and the platform's own homeostasis basis says ATP 'only rises - from 0.333 at boot to 1.0 - and the thresholds written against it cannot fire'. 'implemented'/'wired' assert an effect that cannot occur, and the disclosure sits on a different surface: Tier 1, not 3. items.title: A loss-making cycle is reported with a reserve set aside, 'capital_preserved: true' and no statement of the loss — MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v16 (R6), measured 2026-10-11 against HEAD ca081db0 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §12: six-stage waterfall with Stage 0 reserves off the top; forms with capital preservation (Waqf/Trust); double-entry books with CFO statements. Books afterwards: assets {cash: -420, reserve_fund: 220}, balanced true. The reserve fund stays transferable to another VSB (the transfer check reads reserve_fund only). The only thing 'capital preserved' enforces anywhere is capital_fund share > 0 in the waterfall. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/economy/metabolism.py:223-231,389; agentic_core/economy/metabolism.py:65-68; GET /economy/board-pack balance_sheet after the cycle; VSBEconomy.tsx:538-550. WHY THIS TIER: For revenue 100 / costs 500 the reader is shown Intake 100, Operating costs 500, Reserve 20, Distributable 0 (in the green tone) and, in the body, "capital_preserved": true. Each number is arithmetically what was posted, so nothing is fabricated; what is missing is the fact that the cycle lost 420 and that the 20 WST 'reserve' exists beside a cash balance of -420. capital_preserved is the entity template's nature flag copied into an outcome report, which invites the wrong reading but is labelled nowhere as an outcome - so Tier 2 (invisible shortfall) rather than Tier 1. REFUTER: Reproduced live. POST /api/v1/economy/cycle {revenue:100,costs:500} (apex, labelled SIMULATION/UNREGISTERED) -> homeostasis_reserves 20.0, operating_costs 500, distributable_profit 0.0, capital_preserved true, no deficit/loss field anywhere in the body. metabolism.py computes reserves = revenue x rate regardless of costs and distributable = max(0, ...); capital_preserved is the template flag copied into the cycle report (line 389). I considered Tier 1 for 'capital_preserved: true' on a losing cycle; it is a nature flag not rendered on the cycle card and not labelled as an outcome, so I leave it at 2. I did not re-check the negative cash balance on a registered entity's books. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Add cycle_result_wst (revenue - costs - reserve, may be negative) and a 'LOSS: costs exceeded revenue by N; reserve taken from a negative cash position' line; rename the report field to form_requires_capital_fund_share.

items.title: DECIDE: should a pasted text measured only against its own headings be certified at all
items.why: Ledger v16 found a pasted deliverable certified as passing against a structure read off its own headings. The first plan item's ACCEPT, kept since W449, has a person's own document measured and passed exactly this way, and two tests hold it. W666 therefore did NOT change the verdict: the record now states that the structure is the text's own and that its coverage is 1.0 by construction, which is all that was done. The closing note on the ledger row says the record is 'not assessable'; that is what the first cut did and it was withdrawn in the same round - this row is the correction. Choices: (a) keep certifying, with the statement now added; (b) record such a text as not assessable unless the caller declares a structure, and change the earlier ACCEPT and its two tests; (c) measure it against the deliverable type's own declared sections instead.

items.title: The quality gate records "specifically designed: met" and "verified: met" (green QMS pass) for pangram filler placed under the declared headings — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R1), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §10: every solution is specifically designed ... verified · tested · validated; status note: 'Measured by the gate (4): specifically designed · verified · compliant · safe. The first two are computed from the delivery's coverage against its declared structure'. Constitution article 2: a figure carries only the name of what it measured. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce with caller-supplied `content` (pangram filler under the five 'brief' headings) and `sections` declared returned qms_gate_passed true, delivery_coverage 1.0, bar_measured.measured_criteria ['specifically designed','verified'] both met:true; the platform QMS then counted it as a gate run with 0 failures (non_conformance_rate 0.0). The same content without `sections` declared is correctly 'not assessable'. The same instrument is what would judge any model-served deliverable: headings present + no stub word = designed and verified. EVIDENCE: Executed: deliverable deliv-39c6f422 ('Filler declared'). Response: `'specifically designed': {'met': true, 'basis': 'delivery coverage 1.0 against the declared structure (min 0.95), stub_found=False', 'measured': true, 'source': 'gate'}`, `'verified': {'met': true, 'basis': 'QMS gate on real coverage/stub metrics', 'measured': true}`; list row `qms_gate_passed: True`. UI read from source: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/Deliverables.tsx lines 243-259 and lib/api.ts qmsChip (emerald 'pass'). Gate code: agentic_core/vbs/quality.py. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the 'specifically designed' basis names coverage against the declared structure; the 'verified' basis and the green chip label do not say the content was not read.. WHY THIS TIER: The stored record and response say `"specifically designed": {"met": true, "measured": true}` and `"verified": {"met": true, "basis": "QMS gate on real coverage/stub metrics"}`, `qms_gate_passed: true`, summary `2 measured`, which Deliverables.tsx renders as a green `Living-QMS gate: pass · cov 100% · doc-controlled` chip whose tooltip lists `MEASURED by this gate: specifically designed · verified`. The text was five headings each followed by 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' x4, unrelated to the brief. That is a positive outcome asserted under a name the instrument cannot establish (certifying what it could not assess), so it is tier 1 rather than tier 2 (not an omission). It is not tier 3 because, although the 'specifically designed' basis names coverage, the 'verified' basis does not say that the only thing checked was heading presence and a stub regex. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. Pangram filler under two caller-declared headings, unrelated to the brief, was stored with 'specifically designed' met:true measured:true and 'verified' met:true measured:true, qms_gate_passed true; the list row returns qms_gate_passed true and Deliverables.tsx/qmsChip renders an emerald 'pass' chip whose tooltip lists both criteria as MEASURED. Tier 1 rather than 3: the 'specifically designed' basis does name coverage against the declared structure, but 'verified: met' with basis 'QMS gate on real coverage/stub metrics' is a positive outcome asserted under a name the instrument (heading presence + stub regex) cannot establish. Not tier 2 because it is an assertion, not an omission. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Rename what the gate reports to what it measured (e.g. 'declared sections present' and 'no stub marker found') and leave 'specifically designed' and 'verified' as met:null with that figure as supporting evidence; or keep the names but never set met:true from heading coverage alone, and put 'heading coverage only — content not read' in the chip label, not only the tooltip.

items.title: The hifz "memorised" count does not equal its own stated basis ("ayaat with at least one successful review") — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R1), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: A.6 feature 3: Memorization Suite 'DELIVERED and honest ... Progress reports its basis: "a review count, not a hifz certification."'; §15 principle 6 honesty over polish. OBSERVED: The count is `len(cards with repetitions >= 1)` and is recomputed only when a review succeeds. A failed review (quality 0) zeroes repetitions but does not recompute, so the ayah stays counted until some later success; at that next success it drops out even though it has a successful review on record. Sequence run: 1:1 q5 -> 1; 2:255 q4 -> 2; 1:1 q0 (blackout) -> still 2; 1:2 q5 -> 2, although three ayaat (1:1, 2:255, 1:2) each have at least one successful review. Also: an ayah never scheduled (2:255) can be reviewed directly through the API and is counted. EVIDENCE: Executed POST /api/v1/qep/hifz/review x4 for uid audit-r1 and GET /api/v1/qep/hifz/progress/audit-r1: `total_ayaat_memorised: 2` after the fourth call; card 1:1 `repetitions: 0`. Code: agentic_core/religious_domain/api.py lines 756-759 (`if req.quality >= 3: hifz['total_ayaat_memorised'] = len([... c.get('repetitions',0) >= 1])`). UI: components/QEPStudio.tsx lines 333 and 394-399. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the disclosed basis is the thing that is wrong.. WHY THIS TIER: The QEP studio shows a green chip `N memorised (≥1 successful review)` and, after each review, `N ayah/ayaat counted: ayaat with at least one successful (quality>=3) review — a review count, not a hifz certification`. I drove three ayaat to a successful review and the figure shown was 2, so the sentence beside the figure is untrue of the figure. A figure whose printed basis is false is a truth defect on a reached surface (tier 1), not an invisible shortfall: the reader is told exactly how it was counted and that is not how it was counted. REFUTER: Reproduced exactly with a fresh learner id. Reviews 1:1 q5, 2:255 q4, 1:1 q0, 1:2 q5 returned total_ayaat_memorised 1, 2, 2, 2 while three ayaat each have a successful review on record; every response prints the basis 'ayaat with at least one successful (quality>=3) review'. The code counts cards with repetitions >= 1 and recomputes only on success, so the figure matches neither its printed basis nor a consistent alternative. QEPStudio.tsx line 333 and 394-399 print the figure beside that basis. A figure whose stated basis is false of the figure is tier 1; it is not tier 2 because the surface does state a basis and that statement is wrong. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Either count what the basis says (ayaat with any successful review in the session history, recomputed on every review) or change the basis to what is counted ('ayaat whose most recent review was successful') and recompute on every review, including failures.

items.title: The SM-2 explanation tells the learner the prior interval "anchors the next spacing step" on runs where the engine discarded it — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R1), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: A.6 (QEP intelligence surface), §11 rule 5 AI content labelled with provenance; QEPIntelligence header: 'Computed by the REAL MemorizationEngine over the inputs below'. OBSERVED: The interval_days rationale is a fixed string for any interval > 0, independent of the branch the engine took. The scheduled interval and e-factor themselves are the real engine's and are correct. EVIDENCE: Executed GET /api/v1/qep/xai/explanations?ease_factor=1.3&interval_days=10&repetition=5&last_quality=1 -> decision 'reset', next_interval_days 1, interval_days row rationale 'the prior interval of 10 day(s) anchors the next spacing step.' contribution 0.583. Code: agentic_core/api/qep_intelligence.py, contributions list in xai_explanations (the ease and repetition rationales branch on _reset/_compounds; the interval one does not). UI: components/qep/QEPIntelligence.tsx lines 125-131 render rationale and `+{c.contribution}`. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The display-weight caveat is shown; the false sentence is not qualified.. WHY THIS TIER: On the QEP Intelligence tab the row reads `interval_days = 10 — the prior interval of 10 day(s) anchors the next spacing step. +0.583` directly under `RESET → next review in 1 day(s)`. On a reset the engine sets the interval to 1 whatever the prior interval was, and at 0 or 1 repetitions it schedules a flat 1 or 6 days, so the sentence is false for those inputs; the neighbouring rows say so themselves ('the ease factor did not affect the interval at all', 'repetitions were discarded') while still showing +0.208 and +0.5 contributions. It is an explanation surface stating something untrue about the decision it explains: tier 1. The amber basis line ('display-weight attribution ... not the engine's internal arithmetic') covers the numbers, not the false rationale sentence, so it does not move this to tier 3. REFUTER: Reproduced. With ease 1.3, interval 10, repetition 5, quality 1 the route returns decision 'reset', next_interval_days 1, and the interval_days row says 'the prior interval of 10 day(s) anchors the next spacing step.' with contribution 0.583, while the neighbouring rows say the schedule was reset to 1 day and repetitions were discarded. QEPIntelligence.tsx renders the rationale (truncated in the row, full text in the hover title) and '+0.583' under 'RESET -> next review in 1 day(s)'. The amber explanations_basis line qualifies the weights as display attribution, not the sentence. Small in consequence, but it is an untrue statement about the decision on an explanation surface, so tier 1 rather than 2; the scheduled values themselves are correct. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Branch the interval rationale the same way as its neighbours: on reset 'the prior interval was discarded'; at repetition 0/1 'the engine schedules a flat interval, the prior one is not used'; and show 0 (or no figure) for a feature the rationale says had no effect.

items.title: POST /api/v1/gaas/intercept reports "Action executed under constitutional supervision" when nothing is executed, and blames a benign action for an earlier trip — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R1), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11: Constitutional/gaas engine integrated into workflows; §15 principle 6 never fabricate. OBSERVED: The intent gate, the breaker and the UEG logging are real and worked (delete_all -> blocked, article 11.1; breaker tripped; admin reset recorded the prior state). The 'execution' is a literal sentence. No UI page calls this route; the resource fabric's gaas_v5 requisition shares the same interceptor. EVIDENCE: Executed POST /api/v1/gaas/intercept {action_type:'delete_all'} -> blocked; {action_type:'write_report'} -> halted with the quoted reason; POST /api/v1/gaas/breaker/reset -> reset (I restored the breaker I had tripped); then write_report -> allowed with the quoted output. Code: agentic_core/api/constitutional_gaas.py lines 78-96 (`return f"Action '{req.action_type}' executed under constitutional supervision."`). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The response body (the reached form of this API-only route, and what is logged to the UEG) says `"status":"allowed","output":"Action 'write_report' executed under constitutional supervision."`. The handler's `_action` only returns that string; no action exists to execute. That is an assertion of an outcome the platform did not produce, not an omission, so tier 1. Separately, after one prohibited intent tripped the breaker, a harmless `write_report` returned `"status":"halted","reason":"Severe constitutional violation in 'sovereign-node' (tripped on the first)"` — the reason reads as a verdict on this action, which was never evaluated. The gate decisions themselves (blocked/allowed, article 11.1) are real. REFUTER: Core claim reproduced: POST /api/v1/gaas/intercept {action_type:'write_report'} returns status 'allowed', output "Action 'write_report' executed under constitutional supervision.", ueg_logged true; the handler's _action only returns that f-string (or the caller's proposed_output). Verdict corrected from STUB to PARTIAL because the gate, breaker, UEG logging and guardrail verdicts are real; only the execution sentence is invented. No frontend file calls the route (grep), so the response body and the UEG record are its reached form, and that body asserts an outcome the platform did not produce: tier 1, not an omission. I did not re-drive the breaker-trip 'halted' reason, to avoid tripping the breaker on the shared live backend; that sub-claim is not reproduced by me. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Return output null with a field such as `executed: false, basis: 'this route gates an intent; it runs no action'` unless the caller supplied proposed_output; when the breaker is open, say 'not evaluated — the breaker is open since <reason of the earlier trip>'.

items.title: The faith-content rules (refuse a ruling, withhold composed Arabic) guard four doors; Authorship, Solve, BDP, Design-Dev and the Genesis journey accept the same request with no record of either — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11 faith-content constitution rule 1: 'Qur'an Arabic text is NEVER AI-generated'; rule 5; A.9.2, A.9.6; Constitution article 18 '*Verified:* the source allow-list; no generation path emits scripture'. OBSERVED: withhold_arabic / ArabicStreamFilter / refuse_faith_ruling are called only from api/deliverables.py, api/education.py, api/swarm.py and synthesis/api.py. The AI gateway's response screen covers unsafe payload patterns only. intelligence.py (authorship, solve, bdp, design-dev, nexus) and genesis.py have no faith screen. The Constitution page nevertheless shows article 18 as verified with 'no generation path emits scripture'. Not executable here: what a model would write through these doors (no model is available), so the consequence is read from code. EVIDENCE: Executed with the text 'Issue a fatwa on whether music is haram in Islam and give the ruling; write out Surah Al-Ikhlas in full Arabic with an English translation of each ayah': POST /api/v1/swarm/delegate -> 409 religious_ruling; POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce (fatwa brief) -> 409; POST /api/v1/intelligence/solve -> 200 status 'complete'; POST /api/v1/intelligence/authorship, /bdp, /design-dev -> 200 streams started; POST /api/v1/genesis/journey -> 200 status 'complete'. grep of agentic_core for the three helpers; agentic_core/ai/gateway.py lines 77-85; agentic_core/religious_domain/composed_text.py docstring ('one place, so every door applies the same two'). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: Nothing untrue is shown today: with only the floor serving, these routes return frames built from the person's own words, labelled as such. But the same sentence that deliverables and the swarm refuse (409) is accepted with status 'complete' and no `faith_content` field, no refusal and no statement that the rule is not applied here — the shortfall is invisible at the surface, hence tier 2 rather than 3. It is not tier 1 because no generated scripture or ruling was produced or could be produced in this environment; the risk is what a model would emit through these doors. REFUTER: Reproduced for the doors I drove and by grep. The same fatwa sentence is refused 409 by deliverables/produce and swarm/delegate, and accepted by /intelligence/solve with status 'complete', three floor frames and no faith_content field or refusal. The helpers withhold_arabic / ArabicStreamFilter / refuse_faith_ruling are referenced only in api/deliverables.py, api/swarm.py, synthesis/api.py and composed_text.py. Correction: the assessor listed api/education.py as a fourth caller; it does not use these helpers (it has its own 409 for religious curricula), so the guarded set by these helpers is three files. I did not drive authorship, bdp, design-dev or genesis for this text. Tier 2 rather than 1: on this deployment only floor frames built from the request come back, labelled as such, so nothing untrue is shown; rather than 3 because nothing at these doors says the rule is not applied there, while article 18 is shown as verified with 'no generation path emits scripture'. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Apply the two rules at the gateway (or in the shared stream writer) so every composing door inherits them, and until then have each unguarded door return a `faith_content` record saying the rule is not applied on this route; correct article 18's Verified line.

items.title: A supplied text in which the gate found a stub marker and too little content is reported "not assessable" and shown as a grey "QMS —" with no word about the stub — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §15 principle 10: 'stubs and mocks never ship'; §10 verified · tested · validated. OBSERVED: When `sections` are not declared, not_assessable overrides everything, including a positive stub detection. With sections declared the same text fails correctly (qms_gate_passed false, a defect opened, rate 0.5). EVIDENCE: Executed POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce with content '## Objective\nTODO: write this later. Lorem ipsum placeholder.' and no sections -> deliv-2d930258: stub_found True, substantive_length False, qms_gate_passed None, qms_basis 'not assessable — the sections were read from the supplied text's own headings ...'. With sections declared -> deliv-b81a6a2b qms_gate_passed False, coverage 0.2. UI: lib/api.ts qmsChip (null -> 'QMS —'); Deliverables.tsx lines 218-220 and 243-259. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — present in the JSON only.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader of the Deliverables page sees a grey `Living-QMS gate: —` chip whose tooltip speaks only of coverage ('the sections were read from the supplied text's own headings ...'). The record carries `stub_found: true` and `substantive_length: false`, but no surface prints them. Nothing false is asserted (the gate does not pass it), so not tier 1; the finding the instrument did make is withheld from the reader, so tier 2 rather than a disclosed gap. REFUTER: Reproduced. A supplied text '## Objective\nTODO: write this later. Lorem ipsum placeholder.' with no declared sections is stored with stub_found true, substantive_length false, qms_gate_passed null, not_assessable true, and a qms_basis that speaks only of coverage. grep finds neither stub_found nor substantive_length anywhere in Deliverables.tsx or lib/api.ts, so the page shows only the grey 'Living-QMS gate: —' chip with the coverage tooltip. Nothing false is asserted (no pass), so not tier 1; the stub detection the instrument made is not shown, so tier 2 rather than a disclosed gap. I did not re-run the declared-sections variant. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Let a positive stub or length finding stand on its own: fail (or at least flag) when stub_found is true even if coverage is not assessable, and print 'stub marker found' / 'too short to assess' in the chip.
