items.title: The QEP translate tool would show a model's unreviewed translation of religious teaching text, and does not recognise an ayah quoted in English as sacred text (read from code; no model here to drive it) — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: A.9.3 'Translation refuses rather than approximates'; A.12.3 'Unreviewed content is WITHHELD, never shown with a disclaimer — a disclaimer is not a review'. OBSERVED: translation_translate: if a model serves, returns {translation, status:'translated', label:'AI-assisted translation — not authoritative ...'}; no call to scholar_review. The prompt asks the model to 'annotate tajweed/recitation notes where relevant' by default (preserve_tajweed defaults True). `_is_sacred_source` = source_language in an Arabic list or Arabic script present; 'Say: He is Allah, the One! (Quran 112:1)' English->Urdu reached the model-availability check rather than the sacred refusal. /translation/status still lists 'Arabic' among supported_languages. EVIDENCE: Executed POST /api/v1/qep/translation/translate with Arabic (UTF-8 body) -> 422 sacred refusal; with the English ayah text -> 503 'no model resource is available' (i.e. it passed the sacred test); GET /api/v1/qep/translation/status. Code: agentic_core/api/qep_intelligence.py lines 233-238 and 278-330. UI: components/QEPStudio.tsx lines 462-486. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: Today the tool refuses (422 for Arabic script, 503 because only the floor is available) and the page says so, so nothing untrue is shown. The shortfall is in the model path, which the surface describes only as 'even then only a model may translate': the handler returns the model's text directly with a label, without the scholar gate that the same file's refusal sentence promises ('AI-composed religious text is withheld until a named scholar approves it'), and its sacred-source test is Arabic script or a declared Arabic source language only. Unstated at the surface, so tier 2; labelled a hypothesis because it was read, not executed. REFUTER: Reproduced as far as it can be without a model. Arabic-script text is refused 422 with the sacred refusal; 'Say: He is Allah, the One! (Quran 112:1)' English->Urdu returns 503 'no model resource is available', i.e. it passed _is_sacred_source and reached the model-availability check. The handler's model path returns {translation, status:'translated', label} directly with no scholar-review call, and the default prompt asks for tajweed annotations. /translation/status lists 'Arabic' in supported_languages while saying Arabic is not offered. The model path is read from code, not executed, so it stays a hypothesis about what a model deployment would show. Tier 2: today the tool refuses honestly, so nothing untrue is shown (not 1); the gap between the refusal sentence's 'withheld until a named scholar approves it' and the ungated model path is not stated anywhere a user reads (not 3). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Route model output of this tool through scholar_review.published_body like the lesson and curriculum routes; drop the tajweed-annotation instruction; refuse (or gate) text that cites a surah:ayah reference or declares itself Qur'an/hadith in any language; remove 'Arabic' from supported_languages.

items.title: The Constitution page lists 33 articles with no article text and cuts each "Verified by" line off mid-sentence without saying so — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11: Constitutional engine; the canon's contract (route comment) that every article 'names its mechanism' and that this 'travels to the surface'. OBSERVED: The route parses headings, sets content to the empty string for every article, and captures the Verified line with a single-line regex. canon_present true, 33 articles, 3 recording a breach, 0 naming no mechanism. EVIDENCE: Executed GET /api/v154/constitution/articles (all 33 `content_len 0`; verified strings ending mid-clause). Code: agentic_core/api/integration_surface.py v154_constitution_articles (`"content": ""`, regex `^\*?Verified:\*?\s*(.+?)\s*$` in multiline mode). UI: pages/governance/ConstitutionalUI.tsx lines 274-291 render art.content and art.verified. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: Every article is returned with `"content": ""` and a `verified` string that is only the first physical line of the article's Verified paragraph — e.g. article 13 ends '`deliverables.py:72` (`rows[-300:]`) and', article 3 ends '`assure_delivery` returns'. The page prints these under 'Verified by' with no ellipsis or 'truncated' note, and nothing says the rule's own text is omitted. Nothing false is asserted, so not tier 1; the reader cannot tell the text is partial, so tier 2. REFUTER: Reproduced. All 33 articles come back with content '' (33 of 33), and the verified strings stop at the end of the first physical line: article 3 ends 'assure_delivery returns', article 13 ends '(rows[-300:]) and', article 21 ends 'Horizon is'. ConstitutionalUI.tsx renders art.content and 'Verified by {art.verified}' with no ellipsis or truncation note. Nothing false is asserted by the cut itself, so not tier 1; the reader cannot tell the text is partial or that the article body is omitted, so tier 2 rather than 3. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Return the article body (text between the heading and the Verified line) as content and capture the Verified paragraph to its blank-line end; if a cap is kept, append a visible 'truncated' marker.

items.title: The QMS what-if gate answers "real": true for figures the caller typed, while the re-verify route defines exactly that as real: false — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R1), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §10 verified · tested · validated; constitution article 2. OBSERVED: Also: posting an empty body runs a gate at coverage 0.0 'over the figures you supplied' and opens a defect; the defect loop (correct -> reverify -> closed, reverify_basis caller_attested) works and labels itself honestly. EVIDENCE: Executed POST /api/v1/vbs/qms/gate {} and {coverage:0.99}; GET /api/v1/vbs/qms/defects; POST /api/v1/vbs/qms/defects/{defect_id}/correct and /reverify on DEF-93e274a4. Code: agentic_core/api/vbs_systems.py lines 38-62. UI: components/VBSSystemsPanel.tsx lines 60-66, 235-238. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Yes in the adjacent basis field and on the panel; the flag itself contradicts it.. WHY THIS TIER: POST /api/v1/vbs/qms/gate with a typed 0.99 returns `{"passed": true, ..., "real": true}`; POST .../reverify on typed figures returns `"real": false, "measured": false, "real_basis": "NOT measured here: the gate was run on a coverage figure the caller typed"`. By the platform's own definition the gate's flag is wrong. The same body carries `basis: 'a what-if gate over the coverage and stub figures you supplied'` and `counted_in_rate: false`, and the panel that calls it shows 'what-if — not counted in the rate' and never renders `real`, which is why this is tier 2 and not tier 1: a reader of the response is told the truth one field away. REFUTER: Reproduced. POST /api/v1/vbs/qms/gate {coverage:0.99} returns passed true and "real": true alongside basis 'a what-if gate over the coverage and stub figures you supplied' and counted_in_rate false; the handler hard-codes "real": True directly under a comment calling the run a what-if on caller-typed metrics. I did not re-run the reverify route to quote its real:false definition, nor the empty-body case. Tier 2 stands: the flag contradicts the adjacent basis, but the same body states the truth one field away and the assessor reports the panel does not render the flag, so a reader is not left believing a measured gate ran (not 1); the inconsistency itself is unmarked (not 3). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Return real: false (or drop the field) on the what-if gate, matching reverify.

The flashcard, heatmap and audio surfaces are not built.' OBSERVED: QEPStudio provides the reader, SM-2 schedule/review, written recall, a sourced translation of the meanings, and counts. No flashcard, heatmap or audio component exists in the file. EVIDENCE: Read components/QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx line 35 and components/QEPStudio.tsx in full; executed POST /api/v1/qep/hifz/schedule, /review, GET /progress. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The card reads `LIVE (W439): real SM-2 scheduling, reviews and progress — in the QEP studio above.` under a green 'live' chip and the feature name 'Memorization Suite'. What it lists is true; what A.6 feature 3 also names (flashcards, heatmaps, audio looping and segment selection, coaching) is absent and the card, unlike its neighbours ('Tournaments are not built...'), does not say so. An omission, not an assertion, so not tier 1; undisclosed, so tier 2 rather than 3. Weakest of the tier-2 rows. REFUTER: Reproduced. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Add to the card: 'Flashcards, heatmaps and audio looping are not built.'

items.title: Text a founder records after establishment is not screened, so ship, website and archive leave with a failing section-11 screen until an unrelated roster visit catches up — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R2), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §13: the repository and its surfaces are 'compliance-screened (§11)' throughout; the code's own docstring (Owner ruling 2026-10-10, FU-687): 'NOTHING THE §11 SCREEN FAILS LEAVES THE PLATFORM UNREAD'. OBSERVED: POST /vsb/{id}/concept and /body/{section} save founder text and mark the repo stale but do not re-screen. _refuse_if_screen_failed reads the roster's compliance history, which still held 'review' from registration. After I recorded a concept containing 'alcohol-wash' (a standard mite-count method), POST /repo/ship returned 200 three times with compliance_overall 'fail' on website, webapp, mobile and repo, surfaces_refused {}, coherent_whole true; POST /website 200; GET /repo/zip 200. The roster row kept saying compliance 'review' (screened_at 06:32:15). Only when another caller triggered a roster visit at 06:39:13 did the history become 'fail' — and that same visit first ran a cycle distributing 233.07 virtual WST (owner 46.61). After that, ship and zip return 409 compliance_fail_hold, but GET /website/page/index still serves the page generated during the gap. With Self-run OFF (the default) no roster visit happens on its own. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:930-968 (_refuse_if_screen_failed reads living_vsbs._history only), :1571-1626 (concept/body handlers: no screen call), :3216-3299 (ship). Git log in C:/tmp/m1_audit/data/vsb_repos/vsb-98b11749a3: 'ship: QMS not assessable · compliance fail · seal None' (commit 490448f). Ledger entries at 2026-10-12T06:39:13Z; vsb_compliance_history.json history [review 06:32:15, fail 06:39:13]. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The ship payload shows 'fail' per surface, but nowhere says the hold was skipped because the entity-level screen is older than the text.. WHY THIS TIER: The ship response itself prints 'compliance is fail - written, not verified', so the reader of that response is not told something untrue (not tier 1). But nothing says the fail-hold the platform states it enforces was not evaluated against the current text, and the roster kept showing 'review' — a shortfall the surface does not state (tier 2, not 3). REFUTER: Reproduced live on a fresh entity (vsb-9ff9b46ad2). After POST /vsb/{id}/concept with an 'alcohol-wash' sentence, POST /repo/ship returned 200 with compliance_overall 'fail' on website, webapp, mobile and repo, surfaces_refused {} and coherent_whole true; POST /website 200; GET /repo/zip 200. The roster (GET /economy/living-vsbs) still showed compliance 'review' and the entity status stayed 'body pending', not 'held'. The concept/body handlers (vsb.py:1571-1626) call no screen and _refuse_if_screen_failed reads only the stored history (vsb.py:930-968). Tier 2 rather than 1: the ship response itself prints 'fail' per surface, so the reader of that response is not told something untrue; the roster's 'review' carries its own screened_at timestamp. Tier 2 rather than 3: nothing on any surface says the fail-hold the platform states it enforces was not evaluated against the current text. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Re-screen the entity (write the compliance history) inside record_vsb_concept and record_vsb_body_section before saving, or have _refuse_if_screen_failed compare the history's last_at with the entity's last body edit and refuse/re-screen when the screen is older; stop serving previews generated from text that now fails.

items.title: The shipped ORGANISATION.md and web app print the pending marker as 'the founder's commercialisation text' after the founder has written one, and the Business Plan record still says all four sections are pending — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R2), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §13: the repo is the enterprise's living body — business plan, organisation — 'reconfigurable and re-runnable'; §15.6 honesty over polish; §15.9 the Chief-owned Business Plan opens with the founder's idea. OBSERVED: ceo_specification is written once at establishment as (commercialisation or concept) with ceo_specification_source 'founder_input' — on a floor-served journey that value is the platform's own marker 'content pending the owned model — this enterprise has not yet composed its own commercialisation', and on a bodiless establish it is '' — both labelled founder_input. After I recorded concept, design, commercialisation and operations through the founder routes and re-shipped, BUSINESS_PLAN.md carried my text, but ORGANISATION.md still read '_Recorded instead: the founder's commercialisation text, which the AI CEO is handed._' followed by the pending marker, webapp/data.json organisation.ceo was the same marker, and GET /business-plan?scope=<vsb> still returned concept 'content pending the owned model — this enterprise has not yet composed its own concept', an executive summary ending in the commercialisation marker, and provenance.body_pending listing all four sections (updated_at unchanged), while GET /vsb/{id} said body_pending all false and stage 'commercialisation (every §4 section on this entity is composed)'. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/genesis.py:1524 and :1765 (ceo_specification = req.commercialisation or req.concept, source 'founder_input'); agentic_core/api/vsb.py:289-296 (ORGANISATION.md), :1234 (webapp data), :1602-1626 (body handler never updates ceo_specification or the plan). Files read on disk after re-ship: C:/tmp/m1_audit/data/vsb_repos/vsb-98b11749a3/ORGANISATION.md, webapp/data.json, BUSINESS_PLAN.md. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The board pack does call the CEO specification a PLACEHOLDER, but the repo, the web app and the plan record do not.. WHY THIS TIER: The repo file states in a sentence that what follows is the founder's commercialisation text, and what follows is a platform marker saying none exists — while the same repo's BUSINESS_PLAN.md carries the founder's real commercialisation text. That is an untrue statement in the shipped record and the stored entity (source 'founder_input'), not a mere omission, so tier 1 rather than 2. REFUTER: Reproduced by live read of the assessor's entity and by code. GET /vsb/vsb-98b11749a3 returns founder-written concept/design/commercialisation, body_pending all false, yet ceo_specification is the platform's pending marker with ceo_specification_source 'founder_input'. ORGANISATION.md on disk prints 'Recorded instead: the founder's commercialisation text, which the AI CEO is handed.' directly above that marker; webapp data.json organisation.ceo is the same marker; GET /business-plan?scope= still returns concept 'content pending the owned model — this enterprise has not yet composed its own concept' and provenance.body_pending listing all four sections. Tier 1 rather than 2: these are positive statements (a label saying the following is the founder's text; a plan record saying no concept has been composed; a source field 'founder_input' on a platform marker) that the entity's own record contradicts, not blanks. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: In founder_wrote_section (or the two handlers) update ceo_specification and the scoped business plan's concept/executive summary/provenance.body_pending when the founder writes; set ceo_specification_source to 'pending' or 'absent' when the value is the marker or empty.

items.title: The generated web app and phone app footer calls the entity a 'Living VSB IDBO web app' while the platform's own record says it is not yet a living, operating enterprise — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R2), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §13 corollary: a floor-served body ships as the founder's words plus an honest pending state — never as more than it is; §15.6 never fabricate. OBSERVED: webapp/app.js and mobile/app.js (byte-identical, 2663 bytes) render a fixed footer 'Living VSB IDBO web app · generated in-house · quality record and compliance screen in the entity repository.' for every entity. For this entity the journey's deliverable sentence was '...body pending; it is not yet a living, operating enterprise' and the README in the same repo says 'registered - not operating: not yet operating on its own'. The phone app prints the same footer, so it also calls itself a web app. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1161 (footer literal in the app.js template); GET /api/v1/vsb/{id}/webapp/page/app.js and /mobile/page/app.js returned 200 with that text; README.md in the generated repo. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the template note covers what the app is, not the entity's status.. WHY THIS TIER: A visitor to the founder's shipped surface is shown the word 'Living' as a description of the enterprise; the platform's own derived status for the same entity denies it, and the word was already removed from the Genesis page for that reason (W646 comment at GenesisJourney.tsx:1146). An assertion contradicted by the system's own record is tier 1; the adjacent template note says the app is a standard viewer but does not qualify 'Living'. REFUTER: Reproduced: GET /vsb/{id}/mobile/page/app.js serves the footer 'Living VSB IDBO web app · generated in-house …' (literal at vsb.py:1161, shared by webapp and mobile). data.json carries no status field, so the app shows nothing that qualifies the word; template_note speaks only to what the app is. It is borderline, because 'Living VSB IDBO' is also the vision's type name; I hold tier 1 rather than 2 because the platform's own standard treats the word as a status claim and its own record denies it for this entity, and nothing on the surface corrects it. The phone app calling itself a 'web app' is a second, minor mislabel. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Print the entity's derived status in the footer (data.json can carry it) or drop the word; give the phone app its own footer wording.

Because the page does state the truth elsewhere I hold it at tier 2 rather than 1; it is not tier 3 because the tile itself says nothing of the shortfall. items.title: The sealed quality record and ORGANISATION.md cut their own text mid-sentence with no mark, leaving invalid JSON and clipped qualifiers — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R2), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §13: the repo is document-controlled and provenance-sealed; its compliance + quality record is part of the living body. OBSERVED: compliance/QUALITY.md ('the SEALED record of this generation') prints each §11 reason clipped at about 160 characters with no ellipsis, e.g. 'sharia_halal: review — ... not a certification (engine ran and produced no finding h' and 'sharia_halal: fail — haram term present in the text: 'alcohol' — a keyword screen, not a certification Engine also flags: HARAM_ELEMENT_ALCOHOL. (engine-backed) The engine's rule is'. ORGANISATION.md's Board block is json.dumps(board)[:2000] inside a ```json fence and ends '"governance": "arms-length: AI CEO cannot instruct the board' — unterminated JSON, with the vision_summary dropped. The journey bodies, by contrast, mark their cuts ('[cut at 220 of 243 characters]'). EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:295-296; files compliance/QUALITY.md and ORGANISATION.md in C:/tmp/m1_audit/data/vsb_repos/vsb-98b11749a3 (also returned by GET /repo/file). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: Nothing untrue is asserted — text is missing — but the reader is not told it was cut, and on the fail line the clipped part is the sentence qualifying what 'engine-backed' means. An unmarked truncation is an invisible shortfall (tier 2), not a disclosed one. REFUTER: Reproduced on disk and in code. compliance/QUALITY.md clips each §11 reason at 160 characters with no mark (vsb.py:502 reason[:160]) — e.g. the fail line ends '(engine-backed) The engine's rule is'. items.title: The generated phone app caches under a fixed name and serves cache-first, so a hosted copy would keep showing the first-shipped body after every re-ship — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R2), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §13: the Phone app is a real installable PWA, offline-capable when hosted; the surfaces are 'continually-developing' and re-shipped as the entity evolves. OBSERVED: Reasoned from the generated source, not run in a browser: mobile/sw.js uses const CACHE = 'vsb-pwa-v1' for every entity and every generation, pre-caches index.html, app.js, styles.css, data.json and the manifest, and answers fetch with caches.match(request) first. Nothing versions the cache or revalidates data.json, and 'activate' does not clear old caches. After an evolve or founder edit re-ships data.json, an installed copy would keep the old one. The manifest note says 'Installable + offline-capable when hosted' and the UI chip says 'offline when hosted'; neither mentions staleness. The service worker also omits icon.svg from its asset list. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1363 (_MOBILE_SW_JS); GET /api/v1/vsb/{id}/mobile/page/sw.js returned the same text. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The surface says the app is offline-capable when hosted, which is true; it does not say a hosted copy will not follow the entity's re-ships. Unstated shortfall, tier 2; not tier 1 because no statement shown is false, and not tier 3 because nothing discloses it. REFUTER: Reproduced by reading the served file, not by running a browser: GET /vsb/{id}/mobile/page/sw.js returns CACHE 'vsb-pwa-v1', pre-caches data.json, answers fetch cache-first, and activate does not clear old caches; index.html registers it. The UI chip tooltip says the preview's worker has nothing to cache, so the defect bites only a copy the founder hosts — which is borderline tier 3 (the platform hosts nothing). I hold tier 2 because the shipped file is the reached artefact, the surface says 'offline-capable when hosted' and nothing says a hosted copy will not follow re-ships. No statement shown is false, so not tier 1. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Stamp the cache name with the ship commit or generated_at and delete older caches on activate, or fetch data.json network-first.

items.title: A LOW change whose automatic approval was withheld is still recorded and shown as auto-approved — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R3), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5: Change Control governs all change at arm's length, and each decision is recorded with what decided it. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/cca/submit with a LOW config_minor change and no rationale or affected systems (both optional on the page's form) returned status 'submitted' with auto_approval_withheld set. The stored record and the queue row still carried decision 'auto_approved', decision_source 'low_tier_auto_approval', a reviewed_at stamp, review_result 'Auto-approved: LOW impact, measured organism health 100% ...' and an audit-trail 'auto_approved' event. The method check on the same record reports 'a-decision-names-its-mechanism: MET — the decision auto_approved names its mechanism'. Only `status` is reset when the gate withholds. The fields are overwritten once a review later decides the change. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/change_control.py:977-988 sets decision, decision_source, reviewed_at and review_result; lines 1032-1039 reset only status. Executed: cca-b7f84c1461 via GET /api/v1/cca/{cca_id} and GET /api/v1/cca/queue. ChangeControlAgency.tsx:223 renders a green 'AUTO' chip when entry.decision === 'auto_approved'; :314-319 renders 'Review — auto approved' with the Auto-approved text; :380-384 renders 'decided by: LOW-tier auto-approval (organism healthy, no immune threat)'. Page rendering is reasoned from source, not driven in a browser. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the card also shows 'Automatic approval withheld' with the reason, so the page states both the truth and its opposite.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown 'AUTO', 'Review — auto approved', 'Auto-approved: LOW impact...' and 'decided by: LOW-tier auto-approval' for a change that is not approved. Those are assertions of a decision the platform did not make, so it is tier 1 and not tier 2. The amber 'Automatic approval withheld' line beside them contradicts them but does not remove them. REFUTER: Stands at tier 1. agentic_core/api/change_control.py:977-988 writes decision='auto_approved', decision_source, reviewed_at, review_result and an 'auto_approved' audit event; :1032-1039 (method gate) resets ONLY status and adds auto_approval_withheld. Nothing between clears the decision. The page (pages/enterprise/ChangeControlAgency.tsx:223 green 'AUTO' chip; :314-319 'Review — auto approved' + the Auto-approved text; :380-384 decided-by words) renders those fields for a change that is merely 'submitted'. A reader is shown a decision the platform did not take, so tier 1 not 2; the amber 'Automatic approval withheld' line contradicts but does not remove it. Caveat: I could NOT re-drive the live state because measured organism health is now 0.0 (EMERGENCY, from other probes' compliance failures), so my own LOW submission was held on health with decision None. Reproduction is by code plus the stored record. The window is from submit until a review decides (then decision_account reconciles). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: When the method gate withholds, clear decision, decision_source, reviewed_at and review_result (or move them to a 'withheld_auto_approval' sub-record), and run the method check after that reset.

items.title: Curation publishes any typed string as an offering 'curated from' a cascade that proposed nothing — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R3), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5: the BTO runs Build-to-Order and the Products Catalogue; the cascade proposes offerings and the Owner curates them. OBSERVED: Cascade c1862a42df was floor-served. Its proposal row read status 'not_proposed_floor_served', items [], with the basis 'its bullets are generic steps and are NOT filed as offerings'. POST /api/v1/swarm/catalogue/proposed/{run_id}/curate with item 'Validate the structured outputs above against the stated objective.' (the floor's boilerplate next step) returned 200. It created an ACTIVE marketplace listing priced 5 WST with description 'Curated from cascade c1862a42df', flipped the proposal's status to 'curated', and wrote a catalogue.curated ledger event. The handler never checks the item against the run's proposed items or the run's status. No page calls this route. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/swarm.py:276-329 — the only checks are that the run exists and the §11 screen. Executed: listing a06888d78d75 created; GET /api/v1/swarm/catalogue/proposed now shows status 'curated', items [], and a curated entry. grep of apps/workstation-superapp/src finds no caller of catalogue/proposed. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The stored record and the listing say 'Curated from cascade c1862a42df' and status 'curated' for an item the cascade never proposed, beside a basis that says nothing was filed as an offering. That is a false statement in the reached form of an API-only surface (response body, stored record, live listing), so tier 1 and not tier 3. REFUTER: Stands. agentic_core/api/swarm.py:276-329 checks only that the run has a proposal row and the §11 screen; it never compares req.item with the row's items or refuses a 'not_proposed_floor_served' row. I did not curate again (it would publish another live listing); I read the stored result of the assessor's call. The row for c1862a42df reads status 'curated', items [], items_basis 'bullets ... are NOT filed as offerings', and a curated entry for the floor's boilerplate next step. Listing a06888d78d75 is ACTIVE in GET /api/v1/marketplace/listings, priced 5 WST, description 'Curated from cascade c1862a42df'. Tier 1 rather than 3: although the curate route has no UI caller, its product is a live marketplace listing other people reach, carrying a provenance sentence that is untrue (the cascade proposed nothing), and the stored row says 'curated' beside a basis saying nothing was filed. Not tier 2 because it is an affirmative false provenance, not an omission. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Refuse curation when the item is not in the run's proposed items, or when the run's status is not_proposed_floor_served; otherwise describe the listing as owner-authored, not curated from the cascade.

items.title: The entrepreneur plan route answers status 'plan_synthesized' when it generated no plan — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R3), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. items.title: Transformation responses assert 'adaptive', 'dynamic' and 'realised' from constants and single presence checks — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R3), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5: the organisation is modelled and simulated for continual improvement; §15.3 and §15.6: Chief = the founder's digital twin; label simulation, never fabricate. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/transformation/orchestrate returns and stores dynamic: true and adaptive: true as literals, on a run whose own validation block says validated: null and 'no stage checks a DELIVERED outcome'. GET /api/v1/transformation reports pillar chief_twin with realisation 1.0 and status 'realised' on one presence check ('Board / Chief live'), while /api/v1/board/chief/model says nothing is modelled. The overall 0.955 is passed to the Chief's plan-drafting prompt as 'Current vision realisation: 95%' (read from code; not observable on the floor, where nothing is written). The Transformation page does not render status and labels the figure 'API surface coverage — not delivery'. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/transformation_orchestration.py:543 ('dynamic': True, 'adaptive': True); agentic_core/api/transformation.py:185 (status = 'realised' if frac >= 0.999); agentic_core/api/business_plan.py:689. Executed: tx-f68551e8b9 and GET /api/v1/transformation/realisation. TransformationDashboard.tsx:184, 216, 312-320. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The page discloses coverage-not-delivery. The API's literals and the prompt line are not disclosed.. WHY THIS TIER: The response body and stored record say adaptive: true and dynamic: true with no basis and no way to be false. That is a statement of something nothing assessed, so tier 1. The pillar status alone would be tier 2, because its own coverage_basis says 'it does not say the pillar is realised' and the page words it as coverage. REFUTER: The code facts reproduce; the tier does not hold. (a) transformation_orchestration.py:543 does hard-code "dynamic": True, "adaptive": True. But no page renders them and no code reads them (grep of the frontend and agentic_core finds only the writer), and GET /orchestrate/runs does not return them. These routes HAVE pages, so the reached form is the page, and TransformationDashboard.tsx says 'API surface coverage — not delivery' and 'N of M checks present · coverage, not delivery' (:184, :216, :312-320) and deliberately never prints 'realised'. (b) The assessor misdescribed the chief_twin pillar: it is titled 'Chief = the Owner's digital twin as a ROLE (apex, arms-length) — no twin model is trained', which agrees with /board/chief/model rather than contradicting it. Its status 'realised' sits beside its own coverage_basis 'it does not say the pillar is realised'. (c) business_plan.py:689 does hand 'Current vision realisation: 95%' to the Chief prompt, which is a coverage figure mislabelled to a model; nothing is written on the floor. Net: unassessed constants and a mislabelled prompt input that the surface does not state, i.e. tier 2. Not tier 1 because no reader is shown the literals and 'adaptive' is a vague self-description, not a figure or a certified outcome. Not tier 3 because the literals and the 95% prompt line are disclosed nowhere. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Drop the two literals or compute them; rename pillar status to 'all_checks_present'; word the prompt line as API surface coverage.

A model-served 'Chief: AI-Generate' fills only fields that are unset, so it would never write Strategy once the cadence has (read from code; not drivable on the floor). On a generated entity (vsb-98b11749a3) the cadence replaced the establish template, but field_sources.strategy still says 'establish_template' and templated_fields still lists strategy. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/organism/cadence.py:300-301 writes plan['strategy']; agentic_core/api/business_plan.py:359-370 (_is_unset, _pending_fields) and :722-725 (model writes only unset fields). Executed: GET /api/v1/business-plan for workstation and for vsb-98b11749a3. BusinessPlan.tsx:195-197 renders the pending chip from body_pending. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The derived origin of the sentence is disclosed; its effect on the pending list and on generation is not.. WHY THIS TIER: The page's chip 'pending the owned model: executive summary · concept · vision · mission' silently omits Strategy, and nothing says the Chief's generation can no longer fill it. That is a shortfall the surface does not state, so tier 2. It is not tier 1 because the Strategy text itself carries an amber line saying the cadence derived it and no model composed it. REFUTER: Reproduced from the live store and code. Workstation plan: strategy = '[as of 2026-10-12 06:40 UTC] Strategic position derived from the plan itself: 0 aim(s) and 2 objective(s)...', and provenance.body_pending = ['executive_summary','concept','vision','mission'] — strategy is absent. business_plan.py:359-370 treats any non-empty text as set, and :722-725 lets a model write only unset fields, so the cadence sentence blocks later Chief generation of Strategy (read from code; not drivable on the floor). On vsb-98b11749a3 the strategy text is the cadence sentence while field_sources.strategy still says 'establish_template' and templated_fields lists strategy. Tier 2: BusinessPlan.tsx:195-197 renders the pending chip without Strategy and nothing says generation can no longer fill it. Not tier 1 because the Strategy text itself carries its 'Written by the strategic cadence ... no model composed it' line. The stale field_sources value is a false statement in the API body but I found no page rendering it for strategy, so it does not lift the tier. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Treat a field whose current text equals the latest applied cadence refresh as unset for _pending_fields and for generation, and stamp field_sources.strategy when the cadence writes.

items.title: The evolution engine files a canned proposal with an invented rationale when no model answers, and approving it opens a real Change Control request — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R4), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8/§17.2: the organism improves itself through the Sovereign Evolution Office and Change Control; §15.6 never fabricate, label simulation; §8 W482 'an engine computes or says it cannot'. OBSERVED: POST /api/v191/evolution/proposals/generate returned generated:1 with the canned proposal. POST .../approve on it returned status under_change_control, cca_id cca-6965d53c7c, impact_tier MEDIUM: a real CCA request titled '[evolution] Review AI provider failover strategy' now exists with the invented rationale. A second generate produced the identical proposal; GET /api/v191/evolution/history lists it as a resolved proposal. No frontend file calls /api/v191/evolution/* (grep of apps/workstation-superapp/src returned nothing), so the reached form is the response body, the store and the CCA record. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/v191/evolution.py lines 173-185 (fallback dict) and 206-216 (approve -> submit_change with title/rationale from the proposal). Executed: generate x2, approve, reject, history. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. Nothing marks the row as a fallback or names what served it.. WHY THIS TIER: The response body and the stored proposal read: title "Review AI provider failover strategy", type PERFORMANCE, impact "Medium", rationale "System observation triggered this review." No observation triggered anything: this is the hard-coded fallback used whenever the reply has no PROPOSAL_ lines, which is every floor-served call. It is an assertion of a cause and an impact the platform did not produce, not a blank, so it is tier 1 rather than 2. The row carries no served_by and no flag saying it is a fallback; only the description field happens to contain the floor's own banner text. REFUTER: Reproduced. POST /api/v191/evolution/proposals/generate returned generated:1 with title 'Review AI provider failover strategy', type PERFORMANCE, impact Medium, rationale 'System observation triggered this review.' - the hard-coded fallback at agentic_core/api/v191/evolution.py lines 173-185; history shows the identical earlier row. Approve code (206-216) passes that title and rationale into submit_change. No row field marks it as a fallback. A stated cause and impact nobody produced is an assertion, so tier 1, not 2; the floor banner inside the truncated description is incidental and does not label the title/rationale as canned, so not tier 3. Grep of the frontend for v191/evolution returned nothing, so API_ONLY holds. I did not re-run approve (it would file another CCA); that leg is confirmed from code only. Note: my generate call left one more pending proposal ep-546b2070 in the store. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: When no PROPOSAL_ line parses, store nothing and return generated:0 with served_by and a basis ('the serving resource returned no proposals'); never write the fallback row.

VISION CLAIM: §7 resources are rerunnable/reusable with evidence of past runs; §6/§15.6 provenance honest wherever output reaches a user, including the durable record. OBSERVED: Ran composition comp-b10c593d (synthesis_studio, genome, resource_optimizer, metabolic, truth_consensus, vsb_spawn). GET /api/v1/resources/compositions/runs row cr-d33555dc: genome outcome 'produced'; no served_by, floor_calls, is_external or encoded on any real_resources row. The Run history in ResourceFabric.tsx (lines 646-663) paints outcome==='produced' in the aura colour with the phrase as tooltip, so the genome reads as a successful engine run. The LIVE run view does better (line 874: 'ran · returned defaults (not encoded)'). Code-read only, not executable here: the record's any_external is taken from the prompt trace alone (resource_fabric.py line 2035, res = orchestrator.swarm result), so a run whose real resources were served externally would be stored any_external:false. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/resource_fabric.py lines 2023-2038; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/synthesis/ResourceFabric.tsx lines 639-667 and 870-876; executed POST /api/v1/resources/compositions/{cid}/run and GET /api/v1/resources/compositions/runs. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: On the live run view yes; on the stored record and the Run history no.. WHY THIS TIER: The persisted row for genome reads outcome "produced", outcome_phrase "ran its engine and produced this output"; the live response for the same run says encoded:false, every trait 0.5, 'this vector is NOT an analysis of the entity'. The record's served_by_basis says "The calls each REAL resource made are NOT in this figure: they are on that resource's row in real_resources" - but the stored rows hold only resource, endpoint, kind, outcome, outcome_phrase, error, duration_ms. Both are statements the record makes that are untrue, on the durable record and in the Run history chips, so tier 1 rather than an omission. REFUTER: Reproduced. GET /api/v1/resources/compositions/runs row cr-d33555dc: genome outcome 'produced', outcome_phrase 'ran its engine and produced this output'; rows hold only resource, endpoint, kind, outcome, outcome_phrase, error, duration_ms. A direct POST /api/v1/organism/genome/encode on this floor returns encoded:false, all ten traits defaulted 0.5. The record's served_by_basis says the real resources' calls 'are on that resource's row in real_resources' - resource_fabric.py 2023-2038 writes no such field. That pointer is a plainly untrue statement on the durable record, which is what keeps it tier 1; the 'produced' phrase alone would be arguable tier 2 (the encode route did run and return something). ResourceFabric.tsx 646-663 renders 'produced' in the success colour with no qualifier. The any_external leg is code-read only and I did not drive it. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Persist served_by / served_by_map / floor_calls / is_external / encoded on each real_resources row, derive any_external from the rows as well as the trace, and give an unencoded genome its own outcome instead of 'produced'.

items.title: The fabric registry and the Instrument Cell count the Digital Twin as a resource whose engine the fabric runs, while the same fabric says no engine runs for it — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R4), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §7 W446 rule: every composed resource runs its REAL engine; corrected W652 that the composed twin stage does not, 'the product's run row says so'. OBSERVED: digital_twin: fabric_runs_engine True in /resources; state 'available', checked 'available' in cell/availability. ResourceFabric.tsx shows the amber 'prompt stage only — engine not run' tag only when fabric_runs_engine === false, so the twin card gets no tag; InstrumentCellPanel prints '39 available · 2 prompt stage only — of 41 registered' with that basis. Status-read organism resources (metabolic, circadian, immune, nervous_system) are also flagged true although composing them only reads state. EVIDENCE: Executed GET /api/v1/resources, GET /api/v1/resources/cell/availability, POST /api/v1/resources/compose/simulate (engines_not_run_by_fabric lists digital_twin). apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/synthesis/ResourceFabric.tsx lines 446-457; apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/InstrumentCellPanel.tsx lines 259-264. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the twin's description and the simulate panel say it; the flag, the tag and the count say the opposite.. WHY THIS TIER: GET /api/v1/resources returns digital_twin with fabric_runs_engine: true, basis "the fabric's real-resource handler has a branch for it"; GET /api/v1/resources/cell/availability counts it among "39 available" under the stated meaning "'available' means the fabric can run the resource's engine". The same service's simulate and run say "no simulator or engine runs and nothing is computed". A flag and a count asserting the opposite of what the system itself reports is an untrue statement, not a silent gap, so tier 1; it is at the mild end because the card's description text does say no engine runs. REFUTER: Reproduced. GET /api/v1/resources: digital_twin fabric_runs_engine true, basis 'the fabric's real-resource handler has a branch for it', while its own description says 'In a composition NO simulator or engine runs'. GET /api/v1/resources/cell/availability: digital_twin state 'available', counts {available 39, prompt_stage_only 2}, basis ''available' means the fabric can run the resource's engine'. POST /api/v1/resources/compose/simulate lists digital_twin under engines_not_run_by_fabric. ResourceFabric.tsx 446-457 shows the amber tag only on === false, so the twin gets none. A flag and a count that contradict the same service's own statement are untrue assertions, so tier 1 rather than 2; the description text softens it but does not correct the count. metabolic and immune also carry true though composing them reads status. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Derive fabric_runs_engine and the availability state from the handler's declared kind (narrative / status_read / facility_run) rather than from 'a branch exists', and give narrated resources their own state in the count.

items.title: Settings tells the user an unapproved avatar answer is "marked as not cleared", and the avatar never shows that mark — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R5), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §9 enterprise-aware avatar; §11/§15.6 ethics architecturally binding and honesty over polish - the clearance chain's verdict should reach the person it concerns. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/avatar/chat returns cleared:null and clearance_reason 'NOT cleared by the constitutional clearance chain: no approval is recorded for this learner in mode instructor... this is the avatar's ordinary answer'. useAvatarSession maps served_by, image, language, profile and grounding fields only; ConversationPanel has no clearance rendering. A repo-wide grep of the frontend for clearance_reason / clearance_gates / '.cleared' finds only the Settings panel's prose. EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/AvatarClearancePanel.tsx line 72; apps/workstation-superapp/src/hooks/useAvatarSession.ts lines 243-272 (no clearance field mapped); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/avatar/ConversationPanel.tsx (whole file read); POST /api/v1/avatar/chat response body. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No - the opposite is asserted.. WHY THIS TIER: The sentence shown in Settings is: "With no approval the avatar's ordinary answer is shown and marked as not cleared." The chat renders no such mark: the hook never reads `cleared`, `clearance_reason` or `clearance_gates` from the response. The surface asserts a behaviour that does not happen (tier 1) rather than being silent about it (tier 2). REFUTER: Live POST /api/v1/avatar/chat returned cleared:null and a clearance_reason beginning 'NOT cleared by the constitutional clearance chain'. useAvatarSession.ts 243-272 maps no clearance field, and a grep of the frontend for clearance_reason / clearance_gates / .cleared finds only AvatarClearancePanel prose. That panel is mounted in Settings (Settings.tsx:319) and, while no reply goals exist, tells the user the ordinary answer 'is shown and marked as not cleared'. The reply text itself carries no such mark. A reached page asserts a behaviour that does not happen: tier 1, not tier 2, because this is a statement rather than a silence. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Map `cleared` and `clearance_reason` in useAvatarSession and render one line under each avatar reply ('not cleared by the chain: ...'), or delete the 'marked as not cleared' clause.

items.title: The legacy assistant route returns a hard-coded confidence of 0.99 and two links to pages that do not exist — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R5), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §15 principle 6: never fabricate; label simulation. OBSERVED: POST /api/civilization/assistant/query?query=... returned the native floor frame with confidence 0.99 and the two actions, for any query. The sibling GET /api/civilization/recommendations was corrected (empty list, states the previous items were invented); this route was not. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/v260/intelligence.py lines 22-35 (`"confidence": 0.99, "actions": ["/fed-portal", "/evolution-dashboard"]`); live response body. No frontend caller (grep of apps/workstation-superapp/src). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The response body shows `"confidence": 0.99` beside a deterministic-floor frame that says of itself it is 'framing the request above rather than analysing it', plus `"actions": ["/fed-portal", "/evolution-dashboard"]`, neither of which is a route in App.tsx. The figure is a literal in the handler, not a measurement: a fabricated figure in the reached form of an API-only surface is tier 1; it is not tier 3 because the body does not disclose that the number is invented. REFUTER: Live POST /api/civilization/assistant/query returned the floor frame followed by "confidence":0.99 and "actions":["/fed-portal","/evolution-dashboard"]; both are literals in agentic_core/api/v260/intelligence.py and neither path appears anywhere in the frontend source. No frontend caller exists, so the reached form is the response body, and that body carries a fabricated figure with nothing saying it is invented. Tier 1 by the fabricated-figure rule; not tier 3 because the body does not disclose it. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Drop `confidence` and `actions` from the response (or return confidence null with a basis), or archive the route as its siblings were.

items.title: The entrepreneur plan route reports status "plan_synthesized" in the same body that says no plan was generated — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R5), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §15 principle 6; principle 9 (the business plan is AI-generable in-house). OBSERVED: POST /api/v310/entrepreneur/generate-plan with creation_id/target_market/funding_goal returned the floor frame under `raw`, generated:false, detail stating nothing was invented, and status 'plan_synthesized'. No UI calls it; GET /api/v310/entrepreneur/mentors is honest (empty, says six invented profiles were removed). EVIDENCE: Live response body of POST /api/v310/entrepreneur/generate-plan; grep of apps/workstation-superapp/src for 'entrepreneur/' returns nothing. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Contradicted within the body: `generated:false` and `detail` are honest, `status` is not.. WHY THIS TIER: The body carries `"generated": false` and 'The model did not return a parseable business plan' together with `"status": "plan_synthesized"`. A reader of the status field is told an outcome the platform did not produce; a field asserting an outcome is an assertion, not an omission, so it is tier 1 rather than tier 3 even though another field in the same body contradicts it. REFUTER: Live POST /api/v310/entrepreneur/generate-plan returned generated:false, detail 'The model did not return a parseable business plan. No projections, steps or risks are invented in its place.' and status 'plan_synthesized' in the same body. No frontend caller (grep for 'entrepreneur/' in src is empty). The status field asserts an outcome that did not occur. I hold tier 1 because a client reading only `status` is told a plan was synthesised; the contradiction by generated/detail makes it a weak tier 1, but a field asserting an outcome is an assertion, so it is not tier 2 or 3. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Set status to 'not_generated' when generated is false, or archive the v310 route.

items.title: A GMP record is stamped "Signed off by <name>" on an identity the caller typed, and the record does not say so — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §3A domain tools of real working capability (Science); §10/§11 verified, compliant delivery; principle 6. OBSERVED: I added a signatory (POST /gmp/roster), submitted a record and signed it as that signatory in three anonymous calls; the record became 'signed'. By source, gmp_sign passes req.signatory_id straight to gmp_signoff.sign with `user` unused, so with AUTH on any authenticated user could sign as any roster member. The identity gap under AUTH on is read from code, not driven (AUTH is off here). No UI reaches these routes. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/science.py lines 282-316; live bodies of POST /api/v1/science/gmp/roster, POST /api/v1/science/gmp/records, POST /api/v1/science/gmp/records/{record_id}/sign, GET /api/v1/science/gmp/records/{record_id}. Residue: roster entry 'r5-qa' and record 'r5-rec-1' remain (no delete route). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The stored record and GET body read `"state":"signed"`, `"basis":"Signed off by r5-qa on 2026-10-12."`. The signatory id is a body field; the handler does not bind it to the authenticated principal. It is not tier 1 because in this single-user deployment the statement is literally what happened (that id was submitted and is on the roster); it is tier 2 because the record gives no hint that the signer's identity was not verified - unlike the QEP hifz record, which states `identity_verified:false` and why. REFUTER: Read agentic_core/api/science.py 282-316 and agentic_core/science/gmp_signoff.py sign(): the signatory_id is a body field checked only for roster membership; the `user` dependency is unused. GET /api/v1/science/gmp/records/r5-rec-1 returns state 'signed', basis 'Signed off by r5-qa on 2026-10-12.' (the assessor's residue is still there). No frontend file mentions gmp. One correction to the finding: adding a signatory is behind require_admin, so only signing and submitting are unbound. In single-user mode the sentence is literally what happened, so not tier 1; the record gives no hint that the signer's identity was unverified, so tier 2 rather than 3. The AUTH-on consequence is read from code, not driven. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Bind the signer to the authenticated user when AUTH is on, and add `identity_verified` + basis to the record as the hifz progress route does.

items.title: The avatar tells a user who has written no profile that the floor "does not read your profile" and to set up a model and ask again — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §9 personalised to each user's instructions and preferences; the W428 explicit profile, with honest statement of when it applied. OBSERVED: The render condition is `profileApplied === false && servedBy === 'native' && profileState not in (unreadable, error)`. profileApplied is `Boolean(resp.data.profile_applied)`, so it is false for 'none_written' as well as 'not_usable_by_floor'. The component's own comment says 'a user with no profile is told nothing'. Live: POST /api/v1/avatar/chat with no profile returns profile_applied:false, profile_state:'none_written', served_by:'native'. DomainTool gets this right (it keys on profile_state === 'not_usable_by_floor'). EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/avatar/ConversationPanel.tsx lines 120-148; apps/workstation-superapp/src/hooks/useAvatarSession.ts line 267; live avatar chat bodies. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: n/a - the notice itself is the defect.. WHY THIS TIER: Under every floor-served avatar reply the user sees: "profile: not usable by the floor — the structured floor answered this, and it does not read your profile. Set up the owned model and ask again." For a user with no saved profile (the backend says profile_state 'none_written') the notice implies a profile exists and that asking again would change the answer. Each clause is literally true, so it is not a tier-1 falsehood; it is a misleading notice the surface does not qualify, hence tier 2 rather than 3. REFUTER: ConversationPanel.tsx renders the 'profile: not usable by the floor ... it does not read your profile. Set up the owned model and ask again.' notice whenever profileApplied === false and servedBy === 'native' (and state is not unreadable/error). useAvatarSession sets profileApplied = Boolean(profile_applied). Live chat with no profile returns profile_applied:false, profile_state:'none_written', served_by:'native', so the notice shows for a user who wrote no profile, contrary to the component's own comment ('a user with no profile is told nothing'). Each clause is literally true, so I do not raise it to tier 1; it misleads by implying a profile exists and the surface does not qualify it, so tier 2 not 3. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Gate the notice on `m.profileState === 'not_usable_by_floor'`, as DomainTool does.

items.title: A project's stage can be advanced directly while its governance proposal is still pending — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.1 one stage-gated lifecycle; §5/§11 governance that binds rather than decorates. OBSERVED: Sequence run live: create project, run (floor output saved, served_by native), propose-advance → 201 pending; advance → 200 stage 'prototype'; GET governance/proposals still lists the proposal pending. After DELETE of the project the proposal remains as an orphan (approving it would 404 by design). The only guard on /advance is that one output exists at the stage - a floor frame qualifies. A single vote by the same anonymous user approves. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/projects/api.py lines 518-552 (advance_stage, no proposal check) vs 564-590 (propose_advance docstring); apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/projects/ProjectsHub.tsx lines 340-350; live bodies for POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/propose-advance, /advance, GET /api/v1/projects/governance/proposals. Residue: orphan proposal cf2a2b25… left pending. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The Projects page tells the user '✓ Proposal submitted — go to Governance Hub to approve or reject', and the route's docstring says 'The stage does NOT advance until the proposal is approved'. Executed: after POST propose-advance (proposal pending, 0 votes), POST /advance moved the project concept → prototype and the proposal stayed 'pending'. The UI does not call /advance, so no page shows a false sentence (not tier 1), but the gate the page describes is not a gate and nothing says so (tier 2, not 3). REFUTER: Reproduced by reading the handlers, not by re-running the sequence (to avoid more residue): advance_stage in agentic_core/projects/api.py checks only for one output at the current stage and never consults proposals, while propose_advance's docstring says the stage does not advance until approval. No frontend file calls /advance (grep empty); ProjectsHub.tsx:345-348 posts propose-advance and shows 'Proposal submitted — go to Governance Hub to approve or reject'. No page shows a false sentence, so not tier 1; the gate the UI describes is bypassable at the API and nothing says so, so tier 2 not 3. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Make /advance refuse while a pending proposal exists (or require an approved one), and close a project's proposals when it is deleted.

items.title: The two front doors promise "best-in-class capability on demand" and an enterprise "that runs itself" without the floor statement the tools carry — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §3A offering 1 'best-in-class capability on demand'; §15.6 honesty over polish. OBSERVED: DomainsHub copy has no statement of what serves; its footer says 'Every tool runs on Workstation IDBO's own native AI fabric'. i18n key home.intro.tail = 'that runs itself.' while a comment in DashboardNew records that 'self-running' was removed from the card text for this reason. EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/domains/DomainsHub.tsx lines 38-47 and 82-86; apps/workstation-superapp/src/lib/i18n.tsx (home.intro.tail); apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/DashboardNew.tsx lines 159-163, 206-217; GET /api/v1/studio/vsb (status 'registered - not operating'). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: On the tool pages and lower on the home page; not on the Domains front door.. WHY THIS TIER: Domains front door: 'Get best-in-class capability on demand inside your domain'. Home header: 'build a living enterprise that runs itself.' On this deployment every tool returns a frame of the user's own words and every listed entity is 'registered - not operating'. The home page does state the lever status a few lines below and each tool page carries the '"Own AI" means an owned model when one is serving' note, so this is not an unqualified falsehood (not tier 1); the Domains front door itself carries no such sentence, so the shortfall is invisible at that surface (tier 2). REFUTER: DomainsHub.tsx offering-1 card reads 'Get best-in-class capability on demand inside your domain' and the footer 'Every tool runs on Workstation IDBO's own native AI fabric', with no sentence about the floor; i18n 'home.intro.tail' is 'that runs itself.' in the home header. The home page does state the lever status a few lines lower (autonomy-levers paragraph), and live a law tool's body says 'NO legal research or analysis was performed'. So the disclosure exists one click away but not on the Domains front door: tier 2. Not tier 1 because the copy is promotional framing qualified elsewhere on the path, not a specific false figure. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Reuse the DomainTool serving note on DomainsHub and change the home tail to 'run by the heartbeat levers you turn on' as the cards already say.

items.title: The system info route names an external model as the default and the config calls AI "unavailable" without an external key — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R5), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §15 principle 1 / §3A: own the core AI capability; external providers are optional accelerants, never dependencies. OBSERVED: settings.default_model defaults to 'claude-sonnet-4-6'; has_ai_provider is true iff an Anthropic or OpenAI key is set; validate() warns 'No AI provider configured (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY). AI features will be unavailable.' - the inverse of the native mandate, and untrue here since the floor always answers. GET /api/v1/avatar/status on the same deployment says effective_serving_mode 'deterministic floor', external_use_permitted false, anthropic_key_present false. No frontend caller. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/config.py lines 42, 52-59; agentic_core/app_mvp.py lines 730-736; live bodies of GET /api/v1/system/info and GET /api/v1/avatar/status. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: GET /api/v1/system/info shows `"has_ai_provider": true, "default_model": "claude-sonnet-4-6"` on a deployment where external use is not permitted, no Anthropic key is present and the floor serves everything. These are config echoes, not a claim that a call was served by that model, so it is not tier 1; but the body gives a reader no way to know that nothing routes there (tier 2). REFUTER: Live GET /api/v1/system/info: has_ai_provider true, default_model 'claude-sonnet-4-6', config_warnings []. Live GET /api/v1/avatar/status: effective_serving_mode 'deterministic floor', external_use_permitted false, anthropic_key_present false, openai_key_present true. config.py: has_ai_provider is true iff an external key is set, and validate() would warn 'AI features will be unavailable' without one. Corrections: has_ai_provider is true here because an OpenAI key env var is present, so that field is literally accurate; and the 'unavailable' warning is not emitted on this deployment (read from code only). The verdict is better PARTIAL than DOC_OVERCLAIM, since this is a route body, not a canon document. These are config echoes with no frontend caller, so not tier 1; the body gives no sign that nothing routes to that model, so tier 2. It is a borderline 2/3. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Report the effective serving mode in system/info (reuse the avatar status computation) and reword the config warning.

items.title: The Centers of Excellence page lists four standing centres, including post-quantum cryptography, that do not exist — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R5), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5 CoE in the living organisation; §9 only wired, functional surfaces are routed; principle 10 aspirational pages archived. OBSERVED: KnowledgeHub maps /api/v1/intelligence/insights rows to 'CoE' cards (e.g. '1 project(s) across 1 realm(s)' becomes a centre) and falls back to the four hard-coded centres when there are none. 'Search CoE knowledge base' filters card names only. Scores are honestly labelled 'Salience weight · not a measurement'. Routed in App.tsx section 7. EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/coe/KnowledgeHub.tsx lines 90-112, 150-165; apps/workstation-superapp/src/App.tsx line 234; GET /api/v1/intelligence/insights; grep for '/coe' across src (route declaration only). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No (but unreached).. WHY THIS TIER: With no project insights (a fresh deployment) the page shows cards 'Security — Post-quantum cryptography and node defense', 'Data Science — Neural synthesis and graph analytics', 'AI Ethics', 'Global Affairs' under 'Federated knowledge hubs derived from live portfolio intelligence'. That is an untrue description, and it would be tier 1 on a reached page - but /coe has no inbound link anywhere in the frontend (not in the sidebar, the search modal or any page), so by the tier rule it is a surface nobody reaches: tier 3. REFUTER: The gap is real but the tier premise is wrong: /coe IS reached. Sidebar.tsx:106 lists 'CoE Hub' (id 'coe') under Governance & Trust, and sub-items navigate to `/${sub.id}`; the assessor grepped for the literal '/coe' and missed it. On the reached page the heading is 'Centers of Excellence — Federated knowledge hubs derived from live portfolio intelligence'. With no insights the four hard-coded centres appear (including 'Security — Post-quantum cryptography and node defense'), which the code comment itself calls 'the standing centres'; on this deployment, where insights exist, portfolio rows such as '2 project(s) across 1 realm(s)' are rendered as '<type> CoE' cards with an icon picked by index. items.title: A beat whose health or circuit read raised still reports an empty steps_failed and says that means no step raised — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R6), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8/§1: the organism runs, defends and heals itself; §15.6 honesty over polish - a beat must report what it could not do. OBSERVED: respond_to_health, respond_to_energy, respond_to_circuits and respond_to_threat catch their own exceptions into out['error']; beat() reads only .get('read') / .get('recovered') / .get('probed') / .get('engaged') and never passes the error to _step_failed. The failed homeostasis step simply vanishes from `actions`, indistinguishable from the wording the basis sentence rules out. EVIDENCE: Isolated process, temp DATA_DIR (not the live store): patched immune.status and self_healer.status to raise, awaited OrganismHeartbeat().beat() -> actions ['pulse','cadence_refresh','transformation_tick'], health null, steps_failed {}, steps_failed_basis as quoted. Code: agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py lines 297-321 (callers), 887-953 (responders set out['error']), 857-862 (basis sentence). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: no. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown `"steps_failed": {}` beside the sentence "Since W611 (FU-461) EVERY beat step's failure is recorded here, so an EMPTY steps_failed means no step raised." I drove a beat with immune.status and self_healer.status both raising: the two steps failed, steps_failed stayed {} and the sentence was returned unchanged. That is an assertion that is untrue in the state it describes, on the reached response body (and the Heartbeat page shows no FAILED badge), so it is tier 1 rather than an omission (tier 2). It only bites when one of the four responders fails, which is exactly the case the field exists for. REFUTER: Reproduced by driving it. The record's basis sentence asserts a universal ('EVERY beat step's failure is recorded here, so an EMPTY steps_failed means no step raised') that is false for the four responder steps, and it is returned on every beat body and in /heartbeat/status recent[]. That is an untrue statement on a reached response, not an omission, so tier 1 rather than 2. Caveat: on the live backend no beat with a failed responder was observed (all 10 recent beats read health), so the untruth is in the universal sentence, not in an observed live instance. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: In beat(), after each respond_* call, `if _h.get('error'): self._step_failed('homeostasis', ...)` (same for energy, circuits, threat), and add a guard test that patches one responder to raise and asserts the step name appears in steps_failed.

items.title: The v191 evolution generator stores an invented proposal with an invented rationale when the engine returns nothing parseable — MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v17 (R6), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8: the organism improves itself via its own evolution office; §8 W482: an engine computes or says it cannot, never an invented value. OBSERVED: POST /api/v191/evolution/proposals/generate returned one 'pending' proposal whose description is the first 200 chars of the floor's frame and whose title/type/impact/rationale are hard-coded. It is saved and can then be approved into Change Control as if the engine had proposed it. The sibling Sovereign Evolution Office handles the same case honestly (source 'default', 'NOT ISSUED BY THE AI CEO'). EVIDENCE: Live call returned {"generated":1,"proposals":[{"id":"ep-2a43a9e6","type":"PERFORMANCE","title":"Review AI provider failover strategy",..."impact":"Medium","rationale":"System observation triggered this review.","status":"pending"}]}. Code: agentic_core/api/v191/evolution.py lines 170-183 (`if not new_proposals: fallback = {...}`). The three mutating routes in this module carry no auth dependency. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: no. WHY THIS TIER: The response says `"generated": 1` with title "Review AI provider failover strategy", type PERFORMANCE, impact "Medium" and rationale "System observation triggered this review." None of the four was produced by anything: they are literals in the fallback branch, and no observation triggered it. The record carries no served_by and no marker that it is a default. This is API-only (no page calls /api/v191), so its reached form is the response body and the stored evolution_proposals.json row - and that row asserts an outcome the platform did not produce, which is tier 1 rather than tier 3. Under AI_DISABLE_LOCAL the floor serving is the environment; the fabricated fields are not. REFUTER: Reproduced from the stored record and the code. Title, type, impact and rationale are literals in the fallback branch; 'System observation triggered this review.' asserts a cause that did not occur, and 'generated: 1' counts it as an engine proposal. No UI file references /api/v191 (grep of the frontend src is empty), so the reached form is the response body and the stored row, which carry the invented fields with no default marker - tier 1 rather than 3. The description does begin with the floor's own frame text, which partly discloses that the floor served it, but not that the other four fields are hard-coded. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Replace the fallback with `{generated: 0, proposals: [], basis: 'the engine returned no parseable proposal', served_by: ...}` and store nothing; or retire the unreached /api/v191 namespace.

items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R6), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8: the organism defends itself and heals. Minor correction: tracked_endpoints is now 1 (model:ollama:llama3.2, 0 calls), not 0. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Have the defence record state what it contained at engagement (`open_circuits_contained: 0`, and that the threat's event types are not circuit-backed), and word the description from that count instead of the fixed 'quarantine failing endpoints'.

items.title: Each beat record and its append-only audit event carry health 1.0 when the immune sensor observed no call at all — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R6), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. The Heartbeat page does not render the per-beat health, so this is the API body and the stored audit row. EVIDENCE: GET /heartbeat/status at 06:31:48: recent beat 1 (06:29:49) and beat 2 (06:31:19) both health 1.0; GET /organism/status at 06:31:48: immune observations_in_window 0, composite_health_measured_only null. Code: agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py 298, 842-849, 895. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: no. WHY THIS TIER: The beat body and /heartbeat/status recent[] show `"health": 1.0` for beats 1 and 2, and the same value is hash-chained into the UEG heartbeat event. At that time /organism/status said "NO call was observed in the last 5 minutes, so the health figure is the absence of failures and not a reading of anything". The number is what immune.status returned, so it is not a fabricated figure (not tier 1); it is a figure shown without the basis that the platform's own rule says makes it not a measurement, on a record that cannot be corrected later - an invisible shortfall rather than a disclosed one. REFUTER: Reproduced by code and the live record shape; the zero-observation beats themselves have rolled out of recent[] so I could not re-observe beats 1-2. immune.status computes health = 1.0 - failures/10, so zero observations gives 1.0; respond_to_health captures observations_in_window but beat() copies only health into the record and the UEG event. The figure is what the sensor returned (not fabricated, not tier 1) and travels without its basis on an append-only record (not tier 3). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Carry `health_observations` (and null the health when it is 0) in the beat record and the UEG event, as /organism/status already does.

items.title: User isolation is absent on most mounted routes and no surface reports that invariant's coverage — MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v17 (R6), measured 2026-10-12 against HEAD d90ca2d4 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.5 invariant 1: user isolation, scoped to user_id. OBSERVED: The organism control perimeter the vision's status note names as open is now gated at the mount (heartbeat, organism status, genome, sovereign evolution, board behind require_admin), and economy.py has a user dependency on 40 of 41 routes with _require_economy_access. The gap is elsewhere: domain tools, products, ingestion, legacy vNNN namespaces, native_ai (33 routes). EVIDENCE: Isolated import of agentic_core.app_mvp with route.dependant walked recursively: 'total routes 572 without any auth-like dependency 317 of which mutating 158'; top modules native_ai 33, integration_surface 21, religious_domain.api 18, products 10. agentic_core/app_mvp.py 133-190 (the only HTTP middleware observes and grants nothing), 407-483 (mount-level require_admin). agentic_core/ingestion/api.py 240-241. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: no. WHY THIS TIER: §17.5 calls user isolation absolute; the realisation surface counts invariant 2 on every read ("37 of 63 API modules") and says nothing about invariant 1. Dependency introspection of the mounted app finds 317 of 572 routes with no user/admin/auth dependency at any level, 158 of them mutating - for example DELETE /api/v1/ingest/{file_id} (signature `delete_ingested_content(file_id: str)`), the three /api/v191/evolution mutators and POST /api/v310/payments/payout. No reader is told anything untrue (not tier 1), and in this single-user instance nobody is exposed; but with AUTH_ENABLED on these accept unauthenticated callers and no surface says so, which is an invisible shortfall rather than a disclosed one. The count is a name-based heuristic over dependency callables, so it is an upper bound, spot-checked on two routes. REFUTER: Reproduced the count exactly with my own dependency walk of the mounted app. No surface reports invariant 1 coverage: the realisation body contains no 'isolation', 'user_id' or 'unauthenticated' string, while it does count invariant 2. Nothing untrue is told (not tier 1) and the gap is not stated anywhere a reader looks (not tier 3). The count is a name-pattern heuristic over dependency callables, so it is an upper bound; handlers that check identity inside the body are not seen by it. In this single-user instance nobody is exposed. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Add an invariant-1 row to /api/v1/transformation/realisation computed the same way (routes with no user dependency, mutating count), then close the mutating ones first.
